## v15.84 - NET LIFETIME EARNINGS COUNT STALL MONEY CARRIED OUT

Trade audit finding (LOW), entry 2 of the confirmed list.

Sell a backpack of found loot at the Peddler stall, say for $5,500, and extract. pedSellAll sets G.bag to what he kept, adds
the sale to G.pedCarry and G.pedSold, and copies it to G.tel.pedSold; endRaid values the haul afterwards (haul is the sum of
ival over G.bag, so the sold items are no longer in it), pays P.credits+=G.pedCarry on extraction (v7.62) and the outcome card
says Stall money carried out, banked. But runEarnings, the one sum behind the Mainframe card Net lifetime earnings (addProgress
through commitRun for every new run, netEarnFromLog once for a profile from before the counter), read only
((rec.outcome==='extract')?(rec.haul||0):0)-(rec.carriedIn||0). So that run added $0 to a card whose text promises everything
you have extracted, minus everything you carried in, and a run that sold the kit it carried up went down by the whole
carried-in value while the money was banked. The stall already takes part in the bookkeeping the other way: since v13.91 a
purchase adds to G.carriedIn and is subtracted here, so a purchase lowers the figure but a sale never raised it. The run row
already carries the figure: pendingRun takes pedSold:T.pedSold||0, and pedSellAll is the only writer of pedCarry and pedSold
and adds the same amount to both. runEarnings dates from v10.27, later than v7.62 when stall money became carried money, and
no comment or ruling leaves the sale out on purpose. It is a displayed counter only: no Credits, XP, dial or loot table reads
it, no player text is a TXSHIP key here, and no text is changed.

THE BUILD. One edit, the finding's own fix (the verdict corrected nothing): runEarnings counts
(rec.haul||0)+(rec.pedSold||0) on extraction, minus (rec.carriedIn||0) as before. The stall money counts only where the game
pays it out: on death or abandonment the outcome card says it was lost where he fell or left behind, and the row sums exactly
as it did. An old row with no pedSold reads 0 for it and sums as it did, so a profile from before the stall figure resums to
the same number. The edit carries a v15.84 comment above the function in the style of the file. No price, no dial, no loot
table, no seeded draw and no word of player text moved, and map building is not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in
__verifySafe cannot move.

## v15.83 - THE SECTOR MAP NEVER SITS OVER THE OPEN STALL

Trade audit finding (MEDIUM), entry 1 of the confirmed list.

Walk up to the Peddler, press E so the stall panel is up, and press M. In raidKey the map toggle, if(code==='KeyM'&&G&&
!G.over&&!repeat){ G.mapOpen=!G.mapOpen; }, sits above the open-stall block and had no stall test, so the map opened. In
render the stall is drawn early (if(G.trade) drawTrade();) and the map last (if(G.mapOpen) drawMapOverlay();), and
drawMapOverlay begins by filling the whole screen at .94, so the stall vanished behind the map while it still owned the keys.
ESC then went to the stall block, which runs before the v12.89 map line, so the hidden stall shut and the map stayed up; TAB
goes through backOut, which tests G.trade before G.mapOpen, so it did the same. The digits still belonged to the stall: 1 ran
pedSellAll and sold every eligible backpack item at the stall rate behind the map, with the panel unseen, and 2 to 9 bought
stock. The other way in was open too: nothing in updatePlayer read mapOpen (its only mapOpen line is the downed reset), so E
with the map already up opened the stall underneath it, and pad X does the same because padHold turns it into KeyE. On a
controller M itself could not do this: the stall branch in pollPad (v13.49) returns before the D-UP toggle. Nothing marks the
stacking as deliberate; the v15.35 note that the map comes first describes the mouse handlers. Not a TXSHIP key, not balance.

THE BUILD. Two edits, the finding's own fix. The M toggle in raidKey carries !G.trade, so a fresh M while the stall is open
does nothing (it falls through the stall block, which does not name M, to the preventDefault list, and nothing further down
answers M). The stall-open line in updatePlayer reads G.trade=ped; G.mapOpen=false; mouse.down=false; blip('pick');, so
opening the stall, by E or by pad X, shuts the map in the same frame, the way the downed screen clears it (v14.07). Those are
the only two places that set mapOpen true apart from the pad D-UP toggle, which cannot run while the stall is open, so no path
leaves the map over the stall. No number, no dial, no loot table and no word of player text moved, and map building is not
touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe cannot move.

MEASURED. Check 15.83 clears the card and profile, snapshots the profile, deploys at seed 4242 on map 0, clears the keys and
the open things, empties G.ents and marks every unopened container within 60 units opened (put back in finally), and makes a
Peddler 40 units to his right. CONTROL: a frame with no key finds the Peddler (G.nearPed) with nothing else claiming E
(pedBlocked, nearContainer). CONTROL: with the stall shut, raidKey('KeyM',false,null) opens the map and a second M shuts it,
on either build, so the key path is live; with state raid the same pair is sent as keydown M through window, and if that pair
does not toggle the map the page arms are left out rather than failing for a reason that is not the finding. CONTROL: a frame
with E let go then a frame with E held opens the stall (G.trade is the Peddler), on either build. THE FIX, ONE: a fresh M at
the open stall must leave the map shut and the stall open; on v15.82 mapOpen goes true, so the check fails for the finding's
own reason. THE FIX, TWO: the stall reopened, a keydown M through window must leave the map shut. GUARD: the stall reopened, a
fresh raidKey('Escape',false,null) still shuts it. THE FIX, THREE, the other way in: the stall shut and E let go for a frame,
G.mapOpen set true, then a frame with E held: the stall must open and the map must be shut; on v15.82 the map stays open, so
this arm also fails. Each reopen that cannot happen skips while keeping any failure already found. In finally the keys and
the mouse are cleared, G.trade, pedLock, mapOpen, nearPed, pedBlocked and the search are reset, the shut containers are
reopened, G.ents is put back, the player position and iv are put back, the raid is abandoned, the profile snapshot is
restored through __applyLoaded, and the card, dials and profile are cleaned.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. Every fixture check that sets mapOpen true (the pause box ESC repeats, the pad A under
the map, the downed screen, TAB and B ordering, the map draw checks, __mapShot) also sets G.trade null or never opens the
stall, and no check presses M with the stall open (the only stall keys sent are E, ESC, TAB, I, B, P and the digits). The
stall checks 15.35 to 15.37 and 15.82 set mapOpen false before they open it.

## v15.82 - HOLDING E AT THE PEDDLER KEEPS THE STALL OPEN

Trade audit finding (MEDIUM), entry 0 of the confirmed list.

Walk up to the Peddler so the plate reads THE PEDDLER [E] DEAL, and press and hold E, the way the game trains you to for every
crate search and for HOLD E TO EXTRACT. On the first frame updatePlayer opens the stall (ped, no crate underfoot, keys KeyE,
no pedLock: G.trade=ped, G.pedLock=1). About half a second later, at the Windows key-repeat delay, the browser sends keydown E
with repeat true; the window listener has no repeat filter for E and ends in raidKey(e.code,e.repeat,e). The open-stall block
in raidKey, if(code==='Escape'||code==='KeyE'||code==='Tab'||code==='KeyI'||code==='KeyB'){ G.trade=null; G.pedLock=1;
return; }, had no repeat test, so the repeat shut the stall, and because E was still down pedLock (cleared only when the key
is up, updatePlayer) kept it shut. The panel flashed open and vanished with nothing said, and he had to let go and tap E
again. Every other one-press toggle in raidKey ignores repeats (v15.49), and the Digit line right under this one already
did. The controller is not affected: pad X calls raidKey('KeyE',false,null) on a fresh press only. Nothing here is a TXSHIP
key, no comment calls the old behaviour deliberate, and it is not balance.

THE BUILD. One edit in raidKey, the finding's own fix: the closing line reads if(!repeat){ G.trade=null; G.pedLock=1; }
return;. A key repeat of E, ESC, TAB, I or B at the open stall now returns with no effect, which also keeps it from the
number row and the preventDefault list below. A fresh E, ESC, I or B still closes the stall and holds the key; a fresh TAB is
taken earlier by backOut, as before. No number, no dial, no loot table and no word of player text moved, and map building is
not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe cannot move.

MEASURED. Check 15.82 clears the card and profile, snapshots the profile, deploys at seed 4242 on map 0, clears the keys and
the open things, empties G.ents and marks every unopened container within 60 units opened (put back in finally), and makes a
Peddler 40 units to his right. CONTROL: a frame with no key finds the Peddler (G.nearPed) with nothing else claiming E
(pedBlocked, nearContainer). CONTROL: a frame with E let go then a frame with E held opens the stall (G.trade is the
Peddler), on either build. THE FIX, ONE: with E still down, raidKey('KeyE',true,null), the repeat as the listener hands it
over; the stall must still be open, and so must it be a frame later with E still down. On v15.81 the repeat sets G.trade null,
so the check fails for the finding's own reason. THE FIX, TWO, on the real path: with state raid, the stall reopened the same
way, a fresh keydown E dispatched at window (repeat false) must close the stall and hold the key (GUARD, and it proves the
page path reaches the raid keys); the stall reopened again, a keydown E dispatched at window with repeat true must leave it
open. GUARD: the stall reopened, a fresh raidKey('Escape',false,null) still closes it. Each reopen that cannot happen skips
while keeping any failure already found. In finally the keys and the mouse are cleared, G.trade, pedLock, nearPed, pedBlocked
and the search are reset, the shut containers are reopened, G.ents is put back, the player position and iv are put back, the
raid is abandoned, the profile snapshot is restored through __applyLoaded, and the card, dials and profile are cleaned.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. No check sends a repeat of E, ESC, TAB, I or B with the stall open: the fixture has no
raidKey('KeyE',true and no keydown with repeat true beside 15.49, which holds ESC and P with G.trade null. The stall checks
(15.35, 15.36, 15.37) open and close it with held keys through updatePlayer and fresh raidKey presses, which are unchanged.

## v15.80 - ONE SET OF ENEMIES, RUN BY THE HOST, SEEN AND FELT BY EVERYONE

His order of 2026-09-25: native multiplayer, co-op first. This is phase 2, build 2 of tools/multiplayer/plan.md with the corrections
in critique.md. Until v15.79 each window in a shared raid ran its OWN pillagers and machines, so two players up top on one seed
saw two different worlds. Now the host runs them all and the linked windows watch. His rulings hold: NO team damage of any kind;
numbers frozen (no dial, count, damage or table moved); coming back empty on death or abandon stays per player. Loot, searching,
revives, extraction, the raid clock, the weather and the bullets themselves stay with each window in this slice.

THE BUILD.
- NUMBERS. Every body gets a number (e.nid) at the build, in list order: netEntsInit(g) runs on the host from netUpAnnounce
  (right after buildRaid, before the raid word goes out) and on a linked window from netUpStart right after its fingerprint
  matched. The populations match by the fingerprint, so number 12 is the same crawler on every window and nothing about a
  body needs to be sent to name it. A body that arrives later on the host (a wave, a reinforcement, a siege arrival, anything
  pushed onto G.ents) is numbered on the next tick from G.nidN and told to the party with what the drawing needs. A solo raid
  numbers nobody (netEntsInit is only reached through the two party paths).
- THE HOST, ten times a second (netEntsTick, called from netUpTick on the clock that already sends where the host stands,
  behind NET.on and the host role, only while a raid is up on the party seed):
    {t:'en',sd,n,e:[[nid,kind,x,y,face,state,health,flags],...]}   on the fast channel, to every link that is in
  kind and state are indexes into NET_ENT_KINDS and NET_ENT_STATES, x and y whole units, face two decimals, health in
  twentieths of maxhp, flags a bit set of what the drawing, the nameplates and the pillager board read (downed, finished,
  alert, moving, hostile, friendly, hit, muzzle, seen you, windup, vent, crouched, rolling, steady, reviving, shooting,
  looting, healing, sprinting, helped, grudge, parley, blind). Only bodies within NET_ENT_RANGE (1600) of any player go in:
  the host player or one of the party up top on this seed, where his window last said he stood. At most NET_ENT_MAX (200)
  rows a packet; more than that and the rest go on the next tick, round robin. A body that left G.ents since the last tick is
  told to every link at once on the reliable channel, {t:'ent',op:'gone',id,how:'dead'|'out',n} (n is the snapshot that
  follows, so a late fast packet naming it is known for what it is); a dead body one of the party killed is credited to that
  seat, {t:'kill',seat,id,k,el}. A body numbered on a tick is announced first, {t:'ent',op:'new',id,k,x,y,n,r,mh,hp,el,ho} plus
  coat, crew, identity, gun, rig and hire for a pillager.
  MEASURED at seed 4242 in the MSHTML engine, JSON on the wire: sector 0 (85 bodies) with the host player and a stand-in
  friend 300 units apart, 21 bodies in reach, 635 characters a packet; every body (reach lifted) 85 rows, 2436 characters;
  sector 1 (374 bodies) 32 in reach, 958 characters, the cap of 200 rows 5838 characters. One row is about 28 characters.
  A new word 117 characters, a hit word 91, a shot word 76. The message cap is 16384. At ten a second the near packets are
  6 to 10 KB/s per link on either sector; a whole sector 0 packet ten times a second would be 24 KB/s.
- THE NEAREST PLAYER. In updateEnts every body picks its target afresh each frame, p=netTargetFor(e) (behind NET.on; with the
  party off p is G.player as it always was): the host player or one of the party up top on this seed, a standing man before
  a downed one, the nearest of those; a hired man keeps the host (netUpBody hands the AI a body with x, y, r 11, face, downed,
  moving, crouched and sprinting from the last word his window sent). Where the AI read the host crouch, sprint or bush cover
  (the Listener ear, the hard crouch rule, the pillager aim error twice, the concealment factor) it now reads the target
  (p.net?p.cr:G.pCrouch and so on; one of the party has no bush cover here, since only his window knows it). navSeek asks
  the nearest player for its earshot rule, feudEngage for its engage-near gate, and the wave spawn stands its arrival far from
  every player; the 24 draws of that spawn and every other seeded draw are unchanged in count and order.
- A BLOW ON ONE OF THE PARTY: the host never touches his health. netHitPlayer(p,amt,src,name,x,y) takes the host player
  through damagePlayer exactly as before and tells one of the party {t:'hit',seat,dmg,kind,name,x,y} on the reliable channel;
  his window takes it through its own damagePlayer (netHitTake), so his armour, his downed rules and his death stay his own
  and his own How hard they hit dial applies. The three updateEnts sites (Listener, twice, and the crawler bite) go through
  it; enemy rounds test the party after the host player (netBulletPeer, in the enemy branch of updateBullets only); a
  pillager charge (never your own), a Howler shell and a bolt reach the party by the same radius, roof and wall rules
  (netAreaHitPeers). NO TEAM DAMAGE: player rounds, fists and charges test G.ents only, as they always did, and one of the
  party is never in G.ents; the host charge branch never reaches the peers test.
- A LINKED WINDOW UP TOP (netEntsPeer: role join, a raid in hand on the party seed, not over): updateEnts returns at its
  first line into netEntsEase(dt), which slides each body toward where the host last put it (1 - e^(-12 dt), the v15.75
  easing; shortest arc; the walk cycle while the host says it moves; the hit, muzzle, roll, windup, vent and shooting timers
  running down; crawler and Listener legs), takes off any body the host has said nothing about for NET_ENT_STALE (3) seconds,
  and any body this window made on its own (nothing the host numbered: a local siege arrival, say). tickRaiderWaves returns
  on such a window. netEntsApply files each row on its body by number (the first row, a row after three seconds of silence or
  a jump past 160 units puts the body there at once, as the floor does); an older snapshot than the last applied is dropped
  (the fast channel is unordered), one from another seed too; a row naming a body never seen makes it on the spot with what
  the drawing needs (netEntMake) and the new word fills it (name, health, coat, crew, gun, rig, the pillager look from
  raiderLook off the identity and the spawn spot, no seeded draw). A gone word takes the body off the list and the map with
  the spark, the puff and the label the host frame shows (netEntDeathFx; what it drops is the host world, later); an out word
  marks a pillager EXTRACTED on the board. A kill word counts the kill, the contract and the grudge on this window as its
  own kill would (netKillTake, saveProfile on its own save). Its rounds (updateBullets), fists (fireWeapon) and charges
  (explodeFrag) on a body send the host {t:'shot',id,dmg,x,y,a,wk} through netShotSend, with the damage worked out here
  (weak point, shield, armour and the back shot) and change nothing on the body themselves; the host applies it if the body
  is alive (netShotTake): the weak point effect, the damage, the seat mark by the v15.45 rule (a killing or downing blow
  marks the seat, a blow a standing man survives clears it; the enemy round, frag and bolt kill sites clear it too), the man
  turned hostile and onto the shooter as a host round turns him, the crier alarm (wound 3.5 seconds flat, where a host round
  draws it, so the net code never draws), the v3.94 dodge roll off the bearing the shooter sent. Not the host hire.
- NET gains entMap (every body by number), entGone (bodies lately gone, by number, with the snapshot they left before), entN
  (the snapshot count), entRot (the round robin) and entLast (the last snapshot a linked window applied); netReset and
  netUpEnd clear them. netOnMsg routes en, ent, hit, shot and kill. The ?netslot and ?p2 test handle window.__net gains
  ents(): whether this window runs its bodies for the party or watches the host run them, how many it holds and how many are
  numbered, and each by number, kind, place, state and health.

SOLO PLAY UNTOUCHED. Every new call sits behind NET.on: the target and the tick in updateEnts and netUpTick, the peers tests in
updateBullets, explodeFrag, howlerImpact and strikeTick, the guards in navSeek, feudEngage and tickRaiderWaves. The crouch,
sprint and cover reads test p.net, which is undefined on the player. Nothing in the net section draws from the seeded stream
(rr, rnd, ri, pick, rollTable). The seed 4242 fingerprint reads ents {0:85,1:374} and containers {0:165,1:593} on the patched
game and the previous one alike, and a solo raid numbers no body (measured, below). No number, dial, loot table or seeded
draw moved. WHATSNEW_VER stays 15.72 (drift 0.08). No new player-facing line in the game (the kill line and the labels a
linked window shows are the ones the host frame shows); no apostrophe inside any JS string; no TXSHIP key is touched.

## v15.79 - THE PARTY ASCENDS TOGETHER INTO ONE SURFACE AND SEES EACH OTHER UP TOP

His order of 2026-09-25: native multiplayer, co-op first. This is phase 2, build 1 of tools/multiplayer/plan.md with the corrections
in critique.md: the smallest slice of the shared raid. No shared pillagers, machines, loot, bullets or extraction yet. Each window
still runs its own pillagers and machines locally (host snapshots replace them in the next slices), and each player still extracts,
dies or abandons on its own, coming back empty on its own save as today. His rulings hold: no team damage of any kind (nobody up
top is a target for anything yet, and nobody collides); the host dropping mid-raid does not end the others in THIS slice (the
abandon-for-everyone ruling is the next slice, once the world is the host's); revives later; numbers frozen.

THE BUILD.
- ASCEND TOGETHER. The host ascends as always: the sector page (ASCEND TO THIS SECTOR), the loadout question (MY LOADOUT or
  FREEBIE KIT), ascendNow, startRaid; or quick ascent (R at the lift), which also ends in startRaid. Right after buildRaid returns
  in startRaid, the party is told on the reliable channel (netUpAnnounce, behind NET.on and the host role):
    {t:'raid',seed,mapIx,cond,wx,iss,terms,merc,cfg,fp}
  seed is G.seed; mapIx the sector; cond 'day' or 'night' (P.cond, which buildRaid reads through isDay for the night counts); wx the
  id of the weather the host got (pickWeather is one seeded draw whose ANSWER a pinned pick replaces, so the linked window pins it
  to the host answer and the draw still happens); iss 1 or 0, whether the host drew a loaner from the seeded stream (G.issDraw,
  stamped in the raid literal from the draw site); terms the host terms (hasTerm('silence') places a Listener and blackout moves
  the hour); merc the host hire id (P.merc splices the identity pool and adds a body); cfg every key of CFG that differs from DEF
  (the Settings rows and console overrides; the fixture pins are such keys); fp the fingerprint of the built world (below).
- THE LINKED WINDOW (netUpTake on a join role, from the real netOnMsg): if it is not on the Undercroft floor past the title with no
  raid in hand (up top already, on the title, still on the run card) it is told in the PARTY window that the party went up without
  it and why, and the host is told {t:'up',st:'no',why} and names it in its status line; the word is otherwise ignored. In the
  Undercroft, netUpStart: a JSON snapshot of P is taken; commitKit runs (its own packed kit, exactly as MY LOADOUT commits it,
  saved under its own dials); its CFG is copied aside and the host world fields go in: every DEF key reset to its default, the
  host cfg on top (keys of DEF only, scalars only), P.mapIx, P.cond, P.terms, P.merc, P.wxPick=wx, P.intel=0; NET.upHold is set
  and NET.upIss=iss; pendSeed=seed; startRaid() runs, the real one. In finally the guard comes off, pendSeed is cleared, CFG comes
  back whole, and P.terms, P.merc, P.intel and P.wxPick come back. P.mapIx and P.cond stay the host ones: the fog saves under
  P.mapIx (critique 4.2), and the hour is the hour of this raid.
  saveProfile returns at once while NET.upHold is set (the one line added to it): buildRaid saves inside its kit block and
  startRaid saves when it spends the intel core, and either would have written P.cfg=CFG with the host dials in (critique A.6 and
  A.7). Once the world fields are out the build is saved once, so the kit that went up, the sector and the hour are on disk under
  its own dials. The intel core is not spent (P.intel is 0 for the build and comes back), and G.intel is not set, so a linked
  window gets no key marks off a core it keeps (the plan: clients' intel is off in v1).
- THE LOANER DRAW. buildRaid draws WEAPONS[pick(STARTERS)] only when the player has no gun equipped, one seeded draw before the
  spawn and population rolls (net.md 2: a client building with its own kit would place a different population). In a party build
  (NET.upHold) buildRaid reads NET.upIss: a window that would draw when the host did not draws its loaner with RNGS saved and put
  back round the draw; a window that would not draw when the host did makes the same draw and drops it. Outside a party build the
  local is null and the block is what it was. The population lands where the host put it, and the window keeps its own gun or gets
  its loaner as before.
- THE FINGERPRINT (netUpFp): the counts of bodies, containers and walls, the weather id, and an FNV-1a hash (Math.imul, never the
  seeded stream) over every wall by x, y, w, h, every body by kind, x, y and every container by x, y, rounded. It is computed on
  the host right after the build and on the linked window right after its own, and compared field by field (netUpFpSame). A
  mismatch, or a throw inside startRaid, never plays a different surface: G is dropped and keys cleared, showScreen('hub'), the P
  snapshot is put back in place (netUpPutP writes into the same object every closure holds, deleting keys the snapshot lacks) and
  saved, the PARTY window says which world each side built and that this window stays in the Undercroft, the floor says so in one
  line, and the host is told {t:'up',st:'no',why:'surface'}. The kit committed for the ascent is back in the stash.
- SEE EACH OTHER. The loop's raid branch calls netUpTick(dt) while NET.on, ahead of the pause and superhot branches so a paused
  or frozen player is still seen where he stands. It eases everyone on NET.up as the floor does (1 - e^(-12 dt), shortest arc,
  the walk cycle while he said he was walking, the roll running down), takes off anyone whose seat left the roster, and every 0.1 s
  sends the v15.75 word from up top on the fast channel (the reliable one where the fast is not open):
    {t:'st',k:'r',sd,x,y,f,m,r,c,sp,dn,w[,lk][,s]}
  k:'r' marks a word from up top; sd is the seed of the raid the sender is in; c crouched, sp sprinting, dn downed, w the id of
  the gun in hand; lk the look as on the floor, in the first word, once a second and on change; the host names its seat 0, a
  friend names none. netOnState files a word with k r on NET.up (clamped to a 20000 by 20000 surface, not the 700 by 470 floor),
  never on NET.floor, keeps c, sp, dn, w and sd on the entry, and the host passes it on to the other links as it came, never back
  to the sender. render2D pushes each shown entry into the depth list right after the player, keyed by y minus the deck lift
  (netUpDraw), and the list draws it with netUpDrawOne: drawOp as the player is drawn up top, hero 0, his fit colour, his racks
  from his look, his gun from w (own carries the gun and the hair lag, as any body), mode down, roll, crouch, none (no gun) or
  standing, walking and sprinting as he said, lifted by the deck he stands on, wrapped so a fault in one body never costs the
  frame. netUpTags paints his name in amber on a dark plate over his head, in the world pass right before the pillager
  nameplates, so it sits where those do. Shown means: said something, said it in the last 3 s, not this seat, in the roster, and
  the same seed as this raid (a word from another seed is filed and not drawn, so a window still in an old raid never draws into
  a new one).
- ENDINGS. endRaid, right after G.over is set and while NET.on, calls netUpEnd: NET.up is emptied, the seed and fingerprint let go,
  and every link is told {t:'up',st:'out',how}. On receipt (netUpWord) the seat's entry is dropped at once, so a player whose raid
  ended is hidden the same frame; the host passes up words on under the seat of the link they came from. A bye or a lost link takes
  the seat out of the roster and the next tick takes him off. netReset clears NET.up with the floor list. The host ending its own
  raid does not end anyone else's in this slice.
- NET gains up (the list by seat), upAcc, upN (the send clock), upSeed, upFp, upHold (the party build guard) and upIss (the loaner
  word). The ?netslot and ?p2 test handle window.__net gains up(): whether this window is up top and whether its raid is over, the
  seed and fingerprint it holds, where its player stands, and the list with each entry's seat, name, place, target, seed and shown.

SOLO PLAY UNTOUCHED. Every new call sits behind NET.on: the announce in startRaid (and the host role), the tick in loop, the three
draw calls in render2D, the end word in endRaid. The loaner draw in buildRaid reads NET.upHold, which only netUpStart sets, so a
solo build and a sim build make exactly the draws they made. saveProfile returns early only under the same guard. Nothing in the
net section draws from the seeded stream (rr, rnd, ri, pick, rollTable): the fingerprint is an FNV hash over numbers. The seed
4242 fingerprint reads ents 85/374 and containers 165/593 on the patched game and the previous one alike (measured, below). No
number, dial, loot table or seeded draw moved. WHATSNEW_VER stays 15.72 (drift 0.07). Every new player-facing line was checked
against his vocabulary (surface and up top, never the map as a place; Undercroft; sector; the run card; no ship, boarding,
touchdown, hotbar, bag, inventory); no apostrophe inside any JS string; no TXSHIP key is touched.

## v15.78 - IN A SAME MACHINE MODE, WORLD SOUND COMES FROM ONE WINDOW ONLY

His order of 2026-09-25: native multiplayer, played first as two players on the SAME PC in two game windows on two screens,
player 2 on a controller. This is phase 1, build 5 of tools/multiplayer/plan.md (section E) with the corrections in critique.md.
The problem this build solves: two windows on one PC both play the world sound (the Undercroft ambience, the music, the
footsteps, the blips) through the same speakers, a few milliseconds apart, so everything is heard twice with a smear on it.
Player voices are not part of this build.

WHERE THE MUTE SITS. The game reaches the speakers through exactly three nodes, and nowhere else (every .destination in the
file): BUS (bus(), the shared output every sfx, blip, machine voice and the ambient bed connect to, which also feeds the room
reverb send), the reverb's wet return (verb(), REV.wet) and the music's lowpass (tickMusic(), MUS.lp; the music is dry, by
design, and never on BUS). The fourth .destination in the file, blip's OUT=bus()||a.destination, is a fallback that can only
be taken when there is no context at all, so it is left alone. Those three lines now connect to netSndOut(a): in a same
machine mode (NET.same set) one master gain, NET.sndG, made on first use per context and connected to a.destination; outside
the modes a.destination itself, so no node is added and the chain is what v15.77 had. A window switched OFF sets that gain to
0 and nothing else: every oscillator, buffer, ramp and scheduled note keeps running behind it, the context clock keeps
counting, the music scheduler keeps filling its window, so switching back ON is instant and in step with the other window.
Never AC.suspend: a suspended context stops its clock, and the music would come back mid-bar and out of step (the
visibilitychange handler that suspends a hidden tab is untouched; a visible window that is not in front is not hidden).
The fixture overrides say, sfx and blip at the source (mkfixture), so the mute sits below them, at the output. The menu
blips go through it too: a menu click plays the same 'pick' voice a pickup does, through BUS, so there is no clean way to
leave the blips audible in a window switched off; it is silent, and the PARTY window says so.
THE HOST already plays frames on the title before it picks the mode (tickVerb and tickMusic run every frame from load), so
its three nodes may already sit on the destination at the pick; netSndRoute moves them behind the gain once (disconnect from
the destination, connect to the gain, a marker on the node so a second pick does nothing), leaving the BUS feed to the reverb
send in place. The player 2 window sets NET.same at boot, before any node exists, so its nodes are made behind the gain.

THE SWITCH. THIS WINDOW: SOUND ON or SOUND OFF, a row in the PARTY window (#partysnd, #partysndbtn, #partysndnote) under the
CONTROLLER row, shown in a same machine mode only; a press flips it (netSndToggle). The host defaults to ON, the player 2
window to OFF (netSndDefault); the choice is kept under salvagerun:samesound:host or :p2 ('1' or '0'), beside the pad pick and
not in the profile, so saveProfile is untouched; and it is told to the other window as {t:'snd',pair,on} at the host pick
(netSamePick, netSndInit after netPadInit), at the player 2 boot (netSameBootP2, before ready, so ready stays the last word
of the boot as checks 15.76 and 15.77 read it), again when a ready arrives on the host (a reloaded player 2 window), and on
every change; the receiver keeps it on NET.sndOther (-1 not said) and the note reads: Press to change. The other window:
sound on / sound off / not said yet. Two windows on one PC play the same world sound twice, so one of them is switched off. A
window switched off keeps every sound running and comes straight back when switched on. END THE PARTY (netSameStop, via
netReset on the host) puts the gain back to 1 and forgets the other window's word (netSndRelease); the node stays, at 1,
which changes nothing. A player 2 window keeps its mode and channel across netReset as before, so its switch stays. The
player 2 title line adds: World sound plays from the player 1 window; the SOUND row in the PARTY window switches it. No word
on the row that controller B looks for (leave, close, back, done, return).
- NET gains sndOn, sndOther, sndG, sndAc. The ?netslot and ?p2 test handle window.__net gains snd() (on, other, gain as the
  node holds it or null, routed, ctx, state, kept) and sndSet(on), for tools/nettest.html.

SOLO PLAY AND THE INVITE CODE PARTY UNTOUCHED. netSndOut returns a.destination unless NET.same is set: no gain node in the
chain, nothing new read, nothing suspended. netSndRelease runs inside netSameStop on every netReset and does nothing without

## v15.77 - EACH WINDOW ON ONE PC GETS A CONTROLLER OF ITS OWN

His order of 2026-09-25: native multiplayer, played first as two players on the SAME PC in two game windows on two screens,
player 2 on a controller. This is phase 1, build 4 of tools/multiplayer/plan.md (section E) with the corrections in critique.md,
on the risk d1576 named: a browser hands the keyboard, the mouse and (in Chrome) the controllers to the window in front only.
In a window that is not in front navigator.getGamepads returns nothing, or a state that never moves. Player 1 plays the window
in front on the keyboard and mouse or on a pad; player 2 sits at the second window with a controller, and that window is not
in front, so until this build player 2 had no controller.

THE BUILD.
- THE HAND-OVER. In a same machine mode (NET.same set, host or p2) pollPad asks netPadTick for the pad to play instead of
  taking the first connected pad. The window in front (document.hasFocus, read through netPadFocused) reads every connected
  pad in the one navigator.getGamepads call pollPad always made, hands the other window the state of that window's pad
  (netPadSend: which pad, the sender's own pick, every button as down or not and how far, every stick to three places) as a
  word {t:'pad'} on the channel between windows, once a frame while that pad is plugged in, about sixty times a second, and
  plays its own pick. The window not in front plays the last state handed over (netPadRecv keeps it on NET.padFwd as a
  gamepad-shaped object; pollPad fills PAD from it exactly as from a real pad: PAD.on, the sticks, the held keys, PAD.prev)
  and never its own read; a state older than NET_PAD_STALE (0.25 s) is dropped, so an unplugged pad or a window that
  stopped handing over lets go through the normal padRelease path.
- THE CHANNEL. The BroadcastChannel the two windows already share (v15.76, netSamePost), not the fast data channel of the
  link. Three reasons: it is open from the pick on the host and from the boot on player 2, so the controller works on the
  player 2 title before the two are linked and if the link fails; it survives END THE PARTY on the player 2 side; and on one
  PC it is a message between two windows of one browser, well under a millisecond, where the data channel goes out through
  DTLS and SCTP on the loopback and back. The pair code is on every word, so a third window is ignored as before.
- WHOSE PAD IS WHOSE. Each window has a pick, NET.padIx (-1 none). The host plays the keyboard and mouse unless it picked a
  pad (default none). Player 2 plays the pad it picked, or with none picked the first connected pad the host has not taken
  (netPadFor). A pick both windows made goes to the host; player 2 then falls to the first free pad. A pick of a pad that is
  not plugged in plays nothing and is handed nothing. Each window tells the other its pick ({t:'padpick'}, NET.padOther on
  the receiver) at the host pick (netSamePick, through netPadInit), at the player 2 boot (netSameBootP2, before ready, so
  ready stays the last word of the boot as check 15.76 reads it), again when a ready arrives on the host (a reloaded player
  2 window), and on every change. Every handed state names the pad it came from and the sender's own pick, and the receiver
  (netPadWant) refuses a state from the sender's own pad, from a pad it did not pick, from another pair, or of a bad shape:
  player 1's pad never moves player 2 and player 2's never moves player 1.
- THE ROW. The PARTY window gains a CONTROLLER row (#partypad, #partypadbtn, #partypadnote), shown only in a same machine
  mode: THIS WINDOW: NO CONTROLLER, KEYBOARD AND MOUSE (host, none) or THE FIRST FREE CONTROLLER (player 2, none) or
  CONTROLLER 1 to 4; a press cycles none, 1, 2, 3, 4, none (netPadCycle), the note names the other window's pick and says
  each window keeps its own controller, in front or not. The pick is kept under salvagerun:samepad:host or :p2 for next
  time, beside the saves and not in the profile, so saveProfile is untouched. No word on the row that controller B looks
  for (leave, close, back, done, return). The player 2 title line adds: Your controller works here whether this window is
  in front or not.
- NET gains padIx, padOther, padFwd, padSent, padGot; netSameStop lets go of padFwd and padOther and keeps padIx. The
  ?netslot and ?p2 test handle window.__net gains pad() (on, pick, other, the handed state and its age, the buttons the
  reader holds down, sent, got, front) and padSet(ix), for tools/nettest.html.

SOLO PLAY AND THE INVITE CODE PARTY UNTOUCHED. pollPad asks netPadTick only while NET.same is set; otherwise it takes the
first connected pad from the same one getGamepads call as before, never reads document.hasFocus and hands nothing over (the
check holds all three). The controller code never calls rr, rnd, ri, pick or rollTable and never reads G; map building is
not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) has no way to move. No number,
dial, loot table or seeded draw moved. WHATSNEW_VER stays 15.72 (drift 0.05). Every new player-facing line was checked
against his vocabulary (no ship, boarding, touchdown, hotbar, bag, inventory); no apostrophe inside any JS string; no
TXSHIP key is touched.

## v15.75 - THE PARTY SEES EACH OTHER ON THE UNDERCROFT FLOOR

His order of 2026-09-25: native multiplayer, co-op first, up to four. This is phase 1, build 2 of tools/multiplayer/plan.md
(section E), with the corrections in tools/multiplayer/critique.md. Raids stay solo and there is no voice yet (build 3).

THE BUILD.
- Every copy in a party sends where its man stands on the Undercroft floor about ten times a second: x, y, facing, walking or
  not, and what is left of a roll. What he is wearing (one rack id per kind: hair, hat, skin, fit, cut, beard, eyes, face,
  boots, gloves, pack, patch, tattoo, outfit) rides in his first packet, then once a second and whenever it changes. The message
  is JSON {t:'st',x,y,f,m,r,lk}; a friend sends it to the host; the host sends its own with s:0 and passes each friend on to the
  others with s set to that friend's seat, never back to him. The host files a friend under the seat it gave his link and never
  reads a seat a friend claims.
- THE CHANNEL. A second data channel on every link, negotiated like the first as id 1, unordered with maxRetransmits 0, so a lost
  packet is replaced by the next one a tenth of a second later instead of holding up the queue. Negotiated channels are not
  written into the offer, so the invite code does not grow. A link whose fast channel is not open uses the reliable channel
  (id 0), which is what a stand-in link in the check has. The fast channel closes with its link.
- netHubTick(dt), called from updateHubWorld while NET.on, AHEAD of the window test: a man reading the PARTY window at the lift
  is still seen. It eases each of the others toward where he last said he stood (1 - e^(-12 dt) a frame, about 14 units behind
  the last spot a walking man sent), turns him on the shortest arc, runs his walk cycle while he said he was walking, takes anyone whose
  seat left the roster off the floor list, and every 0.1 s sends where this man stands to every link that is in.
- netDrawPeers(DR), called from drawHubWorld while NET.on, puts each of the others into the floor's y-sorted list, so walls,
  posts, the crowd and the player cover him and are covered by him as they do each other; the list draws him with netDrawPeer,
  which is drawOp, the body the crowd and the pillagers use: hero 0, his coat from his fit, every other rack from his look,
  walking, standing or rolling as he said. netDrawTags(S,ox,oy), called after the station names, paints his name over his head
  in amber on a dark plate, above the darkness like the station names.
- The first word from a man, a jump past 160 units, or a word after 3 seconds of silence puts him where he said at once. Nobody
  is drawn who is not in the roster, nobody on this copy's own seat, and nobody who has said nothing for 3 seconds (up top in a
  raid, or his window hidden); he comes back when he speaks. A bye or a lost link takes his seat out of the roster and he is
  gone from the next frame; netReset clears the floor list.
- A look off the wire keeps only ids the racks know, each under its own kind (cosFind(id).kind), so nothing another copy sends
  reaches drawOp but a real rack id. Ownership is not checked: a copy that wears a rack it has not earned shows it to the others,
  which is cosmetic only. Positions must be numbers and are clamped to the room (700 by 470); a facing outside -100 to 100 is 0.
- The PARTY window blurb now says the others walk the floor with you, with their names over their heads, and every raid is still
  played alone. That sentence was new in v15.74 and is in none of his edits; no TXSHIP key is touched.
- The ?netslot test handle window.__net gains me() (where this copy stands, and its seat), floor() (who it draws, where, and
  whether shown) and fast() (how many fast channels are open), for tools/nettest.html.

SOLO PLAY UNTOUCHED. Every new call site is behind NET.on: updateHubWorld calls netHubTick, and drawHubWorld calls netDrawPeers
and netDrawTags, only while a party is on, and the DR loop's new branch runs only for an entry netDrawPeers put there. A solo
floor frame draws, sends and changes nothing new. The floor code never calls rr, rnd, ri, pick or rollTable and never reads G;
map building is not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) has no way to move.
No number, dial, loot table or seeded draw moved. WHATSNEW_VER stays 15.72 (drift 0.03). Every new player-facing line (the

  NET={on:false,proto:1,max:4,role,seat,peers,roster,pend,made,...}; netHost(), netJoin(code), netAccept(code); sdpPack and
  sdpUnpack (async, deflate-raw through CompressionStream when the browser has it, else plain) over sdpPackPlain and sdpUnpackPlain
  (sync); netSend, netBroadcast and netOnMsg; netDrop and netReset.
  A star, host authoritative, up to four: the host is seat 0 and holds one peer connection per friend (seats 1 to 3); friends never
  link to each other. The host offer has one negotiated data channel (id 0, reliable, ordered) and no audio, and is packed after
  ICE gathering completes (or after 5 seconds). The code is PTY1, then o (invite) or a (reply), then z (packed) or p (plain), then
  base64url; PTY1 is not PIL1, the restore code. A chat window that breaks the code over lines or puts words round it changes
  nothing. STUN only: stun:stun.cloudflare.com:3478 with stun:stun.l.google.com:19302 behind it.
  Messages are JSON: hello {proto,ver,pid,name} from the friend when the channel opens; welcome {you,roster}, reject {why:'version'
  or 'full'} or roster from the host; bye from either side. The host turns away a copy on another VER or protocol and says which
  version it is on; the friend is told both versions. pid is 8 hex of an FNV hash of the install id, or of a session id when the
  save has none. Timeouts: 30 seconds for the link after LET THEM IN, 3 minutes for a reply code to be used, 10 seconds for a hello.
  A failed link says one of the routers may be blocking a direct link and to try a new code or another network.
- ?netslot copies alone get window.__net (state, rngs, open, reset), the handle tools/nettest.html reads. A copy opened any other way
  sets nothing on window.

extra pack came to nothing. No comment or ruling makes this deliberate, and it is not balance.

## v15.70 - A KEY DRAGGED ONTO A FILLED KEY ON THE STASH SCREEN BELT SWAPS THE TWO KEYS, AND A KEY ON THE GUN IN HIS HANDS CAN BE MOVED LIKE ANY OTHER

Grid audit finding (LOW), entry 9 of the confirmed list (index 8).

On the Stash screen every tactical belt key in #hotplanwrap is a drag source (grabbable(el,_pk,'plan:'+ix,...), v8.72) and a
drop target. After the v14.17 same-key guard, the drop ran var why=(from==='rack')?rackPut(ix,key):planPut(ix,key), so a key
dragged off another key always went through planPut.
Case A: Medkit on key 3, Frag Charge on key 4, drag key 3 onto key 4. planPut deletes every key holding Medkit and writes key 4 =
Medkit. It never reads what key 4 held, so the Frag Charge loses its key (it shows again in the backpack grid) and key 3 is
empty. The floor backpack swaps the two (v14.25, whose comment calls the overwrite a bug) and so does the raid (v8.04).
Case B: a key on gun 1 or gun 2. The armoury row drags with from 'rack', and rackPut binds the key alone for a gun in his hands
(rackToStash returns null for P.equipped and P.equippedSec, so the gun never enters the stash). Drag that key to another key and
from is 'plan:N', so planPut counts the stash, finds no gun_smg and refuses with the line "That is not in your stash any more."
and a clank; with a spare field SMG in the stash it packs the spare instead, and the spare goes up the lift unasked.
dropDeadKeys (v14.85) already counts the two equipped guns as live keys, so a key on a gun in his hands is a supported state.
The ascent check belt (renderStage) registers no drag sources, so a plan: drag cannot happen there. Nothing in the file calls
the overwrite or the refusal deliberate, and it is not balance.

THE BUILD. One code edit in the renderHub belt dropzone, the verdict's fix as proposed (no corrected fix was given), plus VER and
DEVNOW. Before the put it reads _fk, the key the drag came from (from 'plan:N', else -1), and _was, what the target key holds. A

## v15.69 - A CLICK ON THE MEDICAL KEY OF THE UNDERCROFT BELT NEVER BINDS A BANDAGE

Grid audit finding (MEDIUM), entry 8 of the confirmed list (index 7).

Pack two Medkits and nothing else, with no belt keys set, and press I on the Undercroft floor. hubBagState builds the floor
player at hp 100 of 100, so findHeal skips both heals (healReach 100 is at or over the Bandage ceiling of 85 and the Medkit
ceiling of 100) and returns -1. hotbarSlots then builds the Medical cell on key 6 with the fallback icon 'bandage' and count 2
(countHeals). Click it, press and release without moving: the floor branch of the cv mousedown gave _sdk='bandage' (kind heal,
ITEMS.bandage exists, count over 0) and started G.drag={key:'bandage',fromHot:5}. The window mouseup floor branch found the
release on the same cell; its v14.25 if(d.fromHot!==_H.i) only guards the move and swap, and G.hotAssign[5]='bandage' ran anyway,
then P.hotAssign took it and saveProfile ran. Key 6 now held a greyed Bandage on the floor belt and a red 0 on the Stash screen's
tactical belt, and Medical was gone. With one Medkit packed, the Bandage issued at the ascent kept the pin alive in the raid and
his Medkit had no key. Dragging the Medical cell to another key bound a Bandage he may not have. With a Bandage packed, a plain
click on Medical pinned the Bandage there too. And a click on any belt key released a few pixels off the belt unbound it,
because the floor drag had no press point and no distance test. The raid has had the same-cell rule since v8.14
(if(d.fromHot===HC.i){ dropped=true; break; }) and the 24-unit click threshold since v14.61. Nothing in the file calls the floor
behaviour deliberate, it is not balance, and it touches no player text.

THE BUILD. Three code edits in the floor mouse handlers, the verdict's fix as proposed (no corrected fix was given), plus VER and
DEVNOW. A click on Medical on the floor now does what it does in a raid and on the ascent check plan: it binds nothing.
- cv mousedown, floor branch: a derived heal cell drags only when G.bag (the kit, inside withHubBag) holds the item it shows,
  G.bag.indexOf(_sl.icon)>=0 in place of _sl.count>0, so the Bandage fallback over Medkits starts no drag and the press does
  nothing. A cell he bound himself (itemKey) drags exactly as before. The drag also keeps its press point, px and py, as the
  raid's belt drag does.
- window mouseup, floor branch, over a belt cell: if(d.fromHot===_H.i) return; before anything is written. A release on the key
  it came from is a click. The early return is inside the withHubBag callback, so the write-through of P.kit and P.hotAssign and
  the save still run, unchanged. A key he bound himself stays bound (the old write put the same value back); a derived grenade,
  plate or Medical key clicked no longer pins what it shows. The v14.25 if(d.fromHot!==_H.i) is now always true there and is
  left alone.
- window mouseup, floor branch, off the belt: the unbind needs the release to be more than 24 units from the press, the raid's
  v14.61 test written the same way; a drag with no press point (a staged one) unbinds as before.
No word of player text was added or reworded (nothing near a TXSHIP key), no ruling is touched, and no number, dial, loot table or
seeded draw moved. Map building is not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593)
cannot move. Not changed here: the raid's Medical cell drag uses the same count>0 test, so at full health with only Medkits its
drag to another key would bind a Bandage too; the raid's click on its own key is already guarded, and that drag is outside this
floor finding.

## v15.68 - DRAGGING A BACKPACK STACK AND LETTING GO ON ITS OWN CELL MOVES NOTHING

Grid audit finding (MEDIUM), entry 7 of the confirmed list (index 6).

On the Stash screen, pack two Medkits so the backpack shows Medkit x2. Press on the Medkit stack, drag it toward the stash,
change your mind, bring it back and let go on the same cell. The backpack drop (renderKitCol's dropzone on kitcol) takes only
from the stash, so for from 'kit' it returns at if(from!=='stash') return; and nothing is re-rendered. That part is right. But the
browser then sends a click to the cell, because the press and the release were both on it, and invCell's guard
if(GRAB) return; (a drag ending on this cell is not a click) can never fire: the document mouseup listener runs grabEnd, which
sets GRAB to null, while the mouseup is still being dispatched, and the click comes only after it. So the click runs opt.act(1):
P.kit.splice, clearKeysFor, saveProfile, sfx and renderHub, with no say2. The backpack reads Medkit x1 and one Medkit went home
with no word. The ascent check has the same cells: a kit cell dragged out and back ran click: put one back, and a stash cell
dragged out and back ran click: carry one. Nothing in the file calls this deliberate (the guard's own comment says the opposite);
the v14.17 rule that a belt key picked up and let go on itself is a clear belongs to the belt-key drop handler, which does not use
invCell. It is not balance.

THE BUILD. Five code edits in the pointer drag and one in invCell's click, plus VER and DEVNOW.
- var GRAB=null; gains a neighbour, var GRABSKIP=null;: the cell a drag that really moved started on.
- grabbable's mousedown keeps the cell and the press point, GRAB={key,from,el,x,y}, and clears GRABSKIP, so a new press always
  forgets the last drag.
- The document mousemove sets GRAB.moved once the pointer is more than 6 pixels (x plus y) from the press. A plain click with a
  shaky hand still moves less than that.
- The document mouseup, before grabEnd, sets GRABSKIP to the pressed cell when the drag moved and to null when it did not.
- invCell's click, after the old guard (left in place), reads GRABSKIP and clears it; if it named this cell and the click is a
  mouse click (detail not 0) the click is dropped. A controller A press is el.click(), detail 0 (the rule check 14.74 relies on),
  and is never a drag, so it still acts.
This differs from the audit's proposed fix on purpose. The audit set a GRABMOVED flag on mouseup and cleared it with
setTimeout(0). __regress runs every check in one synchronous loop, so that timer never fires between checks: a check that drags
with movement (8.72 belt to stash, 9.82 belt to backpack, 9.89 off the belt message) would leave the flag up and the next check's
mouse click on any backpack or ascent check cell would be eaten. A flag named for one cell and cleared by the next press cannot
leak that way; at worst a stale name points at a cell that has been re-rendered away, and a press on any cell clears it. No word
of player text was added or reworded (nothing near a TXSHIP key), and no number, dial, loot table or seeded draw moved. Map
building is not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move.
Not changed here: the stash screen's own stash cells use a separate click handler (plain mouse click does nothing there), and the
belt keys have their own drop rules; neither reads invCell.

MEASURED. Check 15.68 clears the card, resets CFG (so the text editor cannot eat clicks) and cleans the profile, snapshots it,
enters the floor with __hubEnter, shuts any open window (a fresh profile opens the welcome window), and stages two Medkits in the
stash and both packed, with no belt keys and freeKit 0, then renderHub and #hub on. It aims only at the Medkit stack in #kitgrid
when its centre is on screen and elementFromPoint there is that cell, else SKIP. CONTROL: packedCount('medkit') is 2 and the
stash holds 2; a plain mousedown, mouseup and click (detail 1) at the centre leaves 1 packed, so the click verb and its handler
are live, on either build. Then the stack is staged again and pressed, the pointer moved to the middle of #stashgrid and back,
and released on the cell. CONTROLS: the press armed GRAB, the release cleared it, and the release alone moved nothing (still 2).
Then the click on that cell: packedCount must still be 2 and the stash must still hold 2. On v15.67 the click unpacks one and
the check fails with 1 packed, the finding's own reason. Then, on a pass, a plain press and click on the same cell must leave 1
packed, so the next real click after a drag is not swallowed. In finally: grabEnd if GRAB is still set, GRABSKIP cleared where it
exists, mouse.down cleared, the profile restored through window.__applyLoaded(snapshot), #hub put back on or off as it was (and
re-rendered when on), then __topClear, __resetCfg and __cleanProfile.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. The checks that drive the DOM drag (8.72, 9.82, 9.89, 14.17) never click the dragged cell
after it: 8.72, 9.82 and 9.89 release elsewhere and read the profile or the toast, and 14.17 presses and releases a belt key with

dropped. No fixture or chain script reads the shape of GRAB beyond GRAB.from (check 15.70), which is unchanged.

## v15.67 - RED NOISE MARKS FOR UNSEEN SOUNDS ARE DRAWN ABOVE THE DARKNESS AND FOG OF WAR SHEETS

Stealth audit finding (LOW), index 5 of the confirmed list in audit-wfxd2t8x2.json. The verdict found it real with no corrected
fix; the build is the auditor's fix plus the verdict's own optional refinement (keep the old place behind the ringsOnTop dial).

The v9.07 noise marks (G.noiseRings, the red #ff5a4a ring for a sound he cannot see) were drawn in the world pass of render2D,
inside wc.save(); wc.scale(Z,Z); wc.translate(-ox,-oy); after the puffs and before the throws. After that pass render2D lays the
darkness sheet (wc.drawImage(litC,0,0); NIGHT_SHEET, about 0.30 by night) and then the fog of war sheet
(wc.drawImage(fogC,0,0); about 0.46 by day and 0.60 by night) over the whole world. noiseMark returns early on
if(canSee(p.x,p.y,p.face,wx,wy,G.vseg)) return;, so a mark only ever exists where he cannot see, which is ground under the fog
sheet (the small ambient cutout around him aside). Both sheets were laid over every mark: by night a mark reached the screen at
roughly 28 percent of its alpha. This is the fault the v4.05 note names for the pings ("the rings were being buried exactly
where they mattered"), fixed then by the ringsOnTop pass that draws G.pings after the fog; the v9.07 marks came later and went
back under the sheets, and their own comment gives world space as the only reason for the place. Gunshots also get a ping ring
on top, but some sounds have only this mark: the charge warning where a pillager grenade lands (v15.28), the Listener and Crier
windups, and the extraction inbound, landing and last call sounds. By night a grenade landing out of sight behind him showed as
a faint smudge. CFG.noiseSee is 1, so the marks are on. Draw order only, not balance.

THE BUILD. Two code edits plus VER and DEVNOW.
1. The world pass block (near 24027): if(G.noiseRings) for(...) becomes if(G.noiseRings&&CFG.ringsOnTop===0) for(...). The body
   is untouched, so with ringsOnTop dialled to 0 the marks are drawn exactly where and how they were, with the pings, which is
   what the v4.05 comment promises ("ringsOnTop 0 restores the old order"). This is the verdict's optional refinement.
2. The same block, word for word in its drawing (colour #ff5a4a, lineWidth 2.2, radius 6+nf*r, the trailing ring past nf 0.22
   at 0.55 of the alpha, y-10), is added after the ringsOnTop ping pass's closing wc.restore(); } and before the weather
   comment, inside its own wc.save(); wc.scale(Z,Z); wc.translate(-ox,-oy); ... wc.globalAlpha=1; wc.restore(); and gated
   if(CFG.ringsOnTop!==0&&G.noiseRings&&G.noiseRings.length). At that point the canvas is in source-over at alpha 1 (the
   wc.globalAlpha=1; wc.globalCompositeOperation='source-over'; after the warm glows), the transform is the absolute DPR reset
   plus the same world scale and translate the pings use, i is the function's shared var and nr and nf are declared inside, so
   nothing else moves. The marks now sit above the darkness and the fog and below the rain, like the pings.
No number changed: every alpha, radius, width, life and the NOISEMARK table are as they were. No player text was added or
reworded (no TXSHIP key touched), no dial default, loot table or balance number moved. render2D draws no seeded random here,
and map building is not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move.
The sim never draws, so no paired number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.67 records draw order rather than pixels. It cleans the card and profile, resets dials, snapshots the
profile, deploys map 0 at seed 4242, requires a sized pane and ringsOnTop on after the reset, pins his facing to PI/2 and takes
a spot 300 units directly behind him. The mark and a control ping are told apart by a fraction of a unit no map place is given
(x+0.3125 for the mark, x+0.6875 for the ping). CONTROL: canSee says he cannot see either place. It wraps wc.drawImage (records
the darkness sheet litC and the fog sheet fogC) and wc.arc (records arcs at the two test x values with radius, composite,
alpha, stroke colour and getTransform), and draws one frame with render2D(0) holding only G.noiseRings=[{t:0.35,life:1.15,r:60,
a0:0.65}] and G.pings=[{src:'robot',typ:'fire',s:500,occ:1,t:0.3,life:1.1}]. CONTROL: the frame laid the darkness sheet and then
the fog sheet. CONTROL: the ping ring is drawn after the fog sheet on either build (the v4.05 pass), so a ring above the fog is
seen by the recording. THE FINDING: the mark must be drawn, as exactly two rings (the ring and its trailing ring at this age),
both after the fog sheet; on v15.66 both are drawn before the darkness sheet and the check fails for the finding's own reason.
It also holds the mark to what it always was: #ff5a4a, source-over, alpha 0.65*(1-nf) and 0.55 of that, radius 6+nf*60 and
6+(nf-0.22)*60, and the same transform as the ping on the same ground (all true on either build). THE DIAL: with ringsOnTop 0
(CONTROL: the ping is then drawn before the darkness sheet) the mark must be two rings, both before the darkness sheet; true on

## v15.66 - PILLAGERS SEE A DOWNED OR ROLLING PLAYER AT THEIR NORMAL RANGE

Stealth audit finding (MEDIUM), index 4 of the confirmed list in audit-wfxd2t8x2.json. The verdict found it real and gave a
corrected fix, which is the build as written.

Crouch behind cover, get found by a pillager inside 170 and shot down. G.pCrouch, the flag every sight rule reads for his stance,
is written in exactly two places: G.pCrouch=!!botCrouch in updateBot and G.pCrouch=!!crouch at the bottom of updatePlayer. Both
early returns in updatePlayer sit above that line: the downed branch (if(p.downed){ ... tryExtractTick(dt,!!keys['KeyE']);
return; }) and the roll branch (if(p.roll>0){ ... tryExtractTick(dt); return; }). The going-down line in damagePlayer,
p.hp=0; p.downed=true; p.downT=CFG.downTime; p.pendKiller=src; p.prep=null; p.prepA=null;, touched neither G.crouchTog nor
G.pCrouch, and neither did tickDowned, giveUpTick or selfRevive. So for the whole bleed-out (up to 17 seconds) the body kept the
stance, the bush and the concealment of his last standing frame. The hard crouch rule in updateEnts,
if(sees&&G.pCrouch&&!WDC&&CHID>0&&!onYou&&dist(e,p)>CHID&&(!G.sim||HARDC)) sees=false;, then blinded every pillager further than
170, so his acqT never built and he never fired at the body, although each hit on a downed player costs 3 seconds of bleed
(p.downT-=3 in damagePlayer). A man downed standing at the same spot was shot as intended. The very next line in updateEnts,
if(sees&&p.downed&&e.kind!=='raider') sees=false;, blinds only machines, so pillagers are meant to keep seeing a downed man.
Crouched in a bush, G.pConceal stayed at the crouched value (concealAt 0.10 still, against 0.40 for a man lying still), which
multiplies every sight range through pcon, and the plate under the red wash read HIDDEN, CROUCHED. The sim already disagrees
with the live game here: updateBot guards if(CRN>0&&!p.downed) before it crouches the bot. The roll did the same for 0.38s:
tryRoll's G.crouchTog=false (his v11.53 note, rolling stops crouching) left G.pCrouch true until the roll returned, so a roll out
of a crouch stayed hidden past 170 with the HIDDEN plate up while the status read ROLLING. Stale state, not a dial: no comment or
ruling calls it deliberate.

THE BUILD. Three code edits plus VER and DEVNOW, the verdict's corrected fix word for word in code:

3. tryRoll, the v11.53 line (near 12336): G.crouchTog=false; G.pCrouch=false; G.pConceal=concealAt(p.x,p.y,true,false,false);
   the roll leaves the crouch for the sight rules the moment it starts, as a man moving on his feet, and the bottom of
   updatePlayer takes over again when the roll ends.

## v15.65 - CTRL WITH THE MOUSE WHEEL SIZES THE HUD WITHOUT TOGGLING CROUCH

Stealth audit finding (MEDIUM), index 3 of the confirmed list in audit-wfxd2t8x2.json. The verdict found it real and gave a
corrected fix, which is the build, with two small additions named below.

In a raid, standing, hold Ctrl and roll the wheel: that is his v9.95 HUD size gesture (and every browser's zoom gesture, which
the canvas listener already prevents). The Ctrl keydown reaches raidKey first, and the v9.92/v10.07 crouch line
if((code==='ControlLeft'||code==='ControlRight'||code==='KeyC')&&G&&!G.over&&!G.sim&&!repeat){ G.crouchTog=!G.crouchTog; }
flipped the toggle. The canvas wheel listener then ran if(e.ctrlKey){ if(e.deltaY!==0) hudSizeStep(...); return; }, which sized
the HUD and never touched the stance, and the keyup listener only cleared the key. Crouch has been a toggle since v10.07, so
letting go of Ctrl did not undo it: sizing the HUD standing left him crouched at .52 speed with the HIDDEN plate up, and sizing
it while crouched in a bush stood him up and dropped the 170 hide rule. The only message was hudSizeStep's HUD size line;
nothing said the stance changed. The two features come from two separate notes of his (v9.92 Ctrl or C crouches, v9.95 Ctrl
and the wheel size the HUD); no comment or ruling mentions the clash. An input bug, not balance.

THE BUILD. Four code edits plus VER and DEVNOW.
1. raidKey, the crouch line (near 11083): before the flip, G.ctrlUndo=(ev&&code!=='KeyC')?G.crouchTog:null; keeps the stance
   from before a keyboard Ctrl press. C is never a modifier and keeps nothing. ADDITION ONE: the controller right stick click
   (v13.36) reaches raidKey as raidKey('ControlLeft',false,null) from pollPad, with ev null, so it keeps nothing either; the
   verdict's version would have kept a stance for a press with no Ctrl key behind it. The flip itself is unchanged, so a plain
   Ctrl press still crouches at once, one change per press (his v13.36 rule).
2. The canvas wheel listener (near 11258): inside if(e.ctrlKey), when G.ctrlUndo is set and a keyboard Ctrl is really held
   (keys ControlLeft or ControlRight), the crouch toggle is given back its stance from before that press; G.ctrlUndo is then
   cleared on every Ctrl wheel, so only the first notch restores and later notches only size. The keys test means a trackpad
   pinch, which sends ctrlKey wheel events with no Ctrl keydown, changes no stance. The HUD step line is unchanged.
3. The window keyup listener (near 11267): a Ctrl keyup also clears G.ctrlUndo, so a Ctrl let go with no wheel stays a plain
   crouch press and a later Ctrl with the wheel cannot give back a stance from an older press.
4. ADDITION TWO, releaseAllKeys (near 29956): if(G) G.ctrlUndo=null; beside the existing bag and drag clear. A Ctrl held when
   the window loses focus (Ctrl+Tab to another browser tab is the common case) never sends its keyup to the game, and the
   verdict names a stale value as the thing to avoid.
Restoring the old stance rather than flipping a second time is the verdict's point: holding Ctrl and then rolling or sprinting
(both set crouchTog=false) before the wheel does not crouch him again from standing. Known gaps, both small: he is crouched for
the few frames between the Ctrl press and the first notch (avoiding it would move crouch to the key release and change when
crouch happens), and if he started crouched, pressed Ctrl, rolled while holding it and then rolled the wheel, the restore puts
him back crouched where the roll alone would have left him standing. No player text was added or reworded (no TXSHIP key is
touched), no number, dial or loot table moved, and no seeded draw was added or reordered; map building is not touched, so the
seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move. G.ctrlUndo lives on the raid object, so a
new raid starts with none.

MEASURED. Check 15.65 cleans the card and profile, snapshots the profile, deploys map 0 at seed 4242 and requires state 'raid'
with no pause box. It sets the HUD size to the middle UISCALES step so a step either way is possible. Keys are dispatched as
KeyboardEvents at window only (the raid key listener hears them once); wheel notches are cancelable WheelEvents on cv with
ctrlKey set. After each gesture one updatePlayer(1/60) frame is stepped standing still with every key up, so G.pCrouch shows
the stance. CONTROL: a plain Ctrl keydown flips the toggle on (else SKIP), and after the keyup and a frame he is still crouched
with G.pCrouch true, on either build. THE FINDING, standing: Ctrl down (CONTROL: the toggle flipped), a notch up (CONTROL: the
HUD moved exactly one step up), a notch down (CONTROL: back on the same step), Ctrl up, a frame: he must be standing, toggle off
and G.pCrouch false. THE FINDING, crouched: the toggle on and a frame, Ctrl down (CONTROL: stood up), a notch down (CONTROL: one
step down) and a notch up, Ctrl up, a frame: he must still be crouched. CONTROL: a controller right stick click, raised the way
pollPad raises it (raidKey('ControlLeft',false,null) and the key cleared), crouches him; a Ctrl wheel with no Ctrl key held,

failure keeps the failure (skip helper, as in 15.64). In finally the keys and the mouse are put back, the position, the crouch
toggle, G.pCrouch and G.ctrlUndo are cleared, the raid is abandoned, the profile snapshot is restored with __applyLoaded (the

## v15.64 - C CROUCHES WITH SHIFT HELD WHEN NO SPRINT CAN START

Stealth audit finding (MEDIUM), index 2 of the confirmed list in audit-wfxd2t8x2.json. The verdict found it real and gave no
corrected fix, so the finding's own fix is the build.

Sprint away from a pillager holding Shift and W until the bar hits 0. The stamina lines at the end of updatePlayer set p.stamLock
and p.stamRelease (v4.24 and v8.73), and the release latch is cleared only when Shift is let go (if(!_shHeld) p.stamRelease=0),
so a held Shift cannot saw sprint on and off. Still holding Shift and W, which is what a man fleeing does, press C to crouch and
break the chase. raidKey turns G.crouchTog on. On the next frame the v11.53 line just above var sprint=,
if(_shHeld&&mg>0&&G.crouchTog&&!p.downed){ G.crouchTog=false; crouch=false; }, turned it off again: it asked only that Shift was
held and he was moving. The sprint line below it then refused the sprint for the stamina flags anyway. He jogged on at full height,
no sprint, no crouch, footstep noise at the standing interval instead of none, no crouched bush cover, and no word why: C looked
broken exactly when he needed it. The same happened aiming (p.ads cancels the sprint at if(p.ads) sprint=false;) and wading in
deep water (if(wading) sprint=false;): Shift stood him up and he did not sprint. The v11.53 comment quotes his note, "activating
sprint should automatically stop crouching", and says movement is required, the same rule sprint itself has, so the line was meant
to follow sprint's own rules and missed the breath, aim and water ones. Where no sprint starts his note does not apply, and no
ruling says Shift alone should stand him up. Not balance: no number moves.

THE BUILD. One edit in updatePlayer: the cancel line now also asks p.stam>2, !p.stamLock, !p.stamRelease, !p.ads and
!inWaterDeep(p.x,p.y,(CFG.wadeInset===undefined?11:CFG.wadeInset)), the same questions the sprint lines below ask, with the same
wading edge as the var wading= line. So whenever a sprint can start, Shift with movement still stands him up and he sprints, which
is his v11.53 note untouched; when none can start, C keeps him crouched. p.ads is a lasting flag (the right mouse button and the
pad's aim both set it before updatePlayer runs), and inWaterDeep only reads the map. The stim still clears the crouch for a sprint:
it holds the bar at 100 and never sets the lock or the latch. No stamina, speed or noise number, dial or loot table moved, no
player text was touched (no TXSHIP key), and no seeded draw was added or reordered; map building is not touched, so the seed 4242
fingerprint in __verifySafe (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move. The bot crouches on its own flag and never reads this
line.

MEASURED. Check 15.64 cleans the card and profile, snapshots the profile and deploys map 0 at seed 4242. At the spawn (required
dry; if deep water the check skips) it steps updatePlayer(1/60) once per case with every key cleared, then Shift and W held,
G.crouchTog on, no roll, not downed, auto-jog off and the mouse up, and reads G.crouchTog, G.pCrouch and G.sprinting.
CONTROL: full breath (stam 100, no lock, no latch), not aiming: the crouch clears and he sprints, on either build, else SKIP.
THE FINDING: stam 0 with the lock and the latch set: CONTROL that he did not sprint, then he must still be crouched (toggle on
and G.pCrouch true). Aiming at full breath: CONTROL that he did not sprint, then still crouched. Wading: the middle of the first
water rectangle more than 2*wadeInset+40 across both ways where inWaterDeep answers true, at full breath: not sprinting and still
crouched; if the map has no such pool this case is left out. CONTROL again: the full breath frame at the spawn still clears the
crouch and sprints. On v15.63 the out of breath and the aiming frames both leave him standing and not sprinting, so the check
fails for the finding's own reason. In finally the keys are cleared, the mouse, position, stamina, lock, latch and aim put back,
the crouch and sprint flags cleared, the raid abandoned, the profile snapshot restored with __applyLoaded, and the card, dials
and profile cleaned.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. 11.53 holds Shift and W crouched with stam 100, no lock, no latch and not aiming at this same
seed 4242 spawn and requires the crouch cleared and a sprint: every new condition is true there, so it stays green (it already

standing, so it never reaches the changed line with the crouch on. 13.36 crouches on the right stick and walks on the stick with

## v15.63 - BACKING OUT OF THE LOADOUT QUESTION RETURNS TO THE SECTOR PAGE

Menus audit finding (LOW), entry 1 of the confirmed list in audit-wfxd2t8x2.json.

At the lift, press E: the lift act runs liftResetDay, renderSector and openModal('sectormodal'). Pick NIGHT and press ASCEND TO
THIS SECTOR. The #sectordeploy handler takes #sectormodal down and calls askKit, the only caller of askKit in the file, which
raises What are you taking up? with openModal('askmodal'). askKit never set ASKBACK. ESC and TAB (the document capture listener,
and for TAB also backOut on window) and controller B all reach escCloseTopModal, which finds no data-esc or close button on the
card and presses #askno, the Not yet button. #askno runs askRestore, which returns at if(!ASKBACK), so he was left on the bare
floor. Getting the page back meant walking to the lift and pressing E again, and that act runs liftResetDay, which puts P.cond
back to 'day', so the NIGHT he had picked was lost. The v12.68 rule written above var ASKYES=null, ASKALT=null, ASKBACK=null says
a card that closes the window it asks about names that window to restore; the Hire nobody card follows it with
ASKBACK='tradermodal'. No comment or ruling exempts the loadout question, and it is not balance.

controller B or Not yet now puts the sector page back exactly as he left it, NIGHT and the weather still picked, because the page

shuts every window). askRestore clears ASKBACK on every answer. If the card is ever shut without an answer, the next card to be

No player text was added or reworded, no TXSHIP key is touched, and no number, dial, loot table or seeded draw moved. Map building

## v15.62 - ESC AND TAB LEAVE THE END OF RAID CARD THROUGH ITS OWN BUTTON

Menus audit finding (MEDIUM), entry 0 of the confirmed list in audit-wfxd2t8x2.json.

Extract, die, or abandon a run with at least one shot fired (that skips the instant quit branch), and the EXTRACTED, KILLED or
ABANDONED card comes up. ESC and TAB did nothing on it. The card is <div class="outcome" id="outcome">, not a .modal, so the
document capture listener (escCloseTopModal) returned at its '.modal.on' test. endRaid sets G.over and shuts the pause box, but
state stays 'raid' until oc_btn's onclick calls showScreen('hub'), so the main window listener handed the key to raidKey, and
every ESC and TAB branch there (the emote bar, the stall, the map and backpack line, the pause toggle) waits on !G.over. TAB went
through backOut first, and backOut's raid branch sits behind if(G&&!G.over), so it returned false. TAB is also in raidKey's
preventDefault list, so it could not even move the focus to the button. The only ways off the card were the mouse on Log run and
return, or controller B, which padMenu finds by its word return since v15.57. That broke his rule that every menu closes on ESC
(his 50 answers of 2026-09-03) and the TAB ruling of 2026-09-13 that TAB closes whatever is in front. No comment or ruling says

along the bottom of the same frame, the last fillText in drawHubHUD, had no controller branch and still said WASD WALK, SHIFT
JOG, E USE STATION. A controller has no E. On the floor pollPad's hub branch holds KeyE on button 0 (A works a station) and
ShiftLeft on button 10 (the left stick click jogs), and updateHubWorld walks on PAD.mx and PAD.my, the left stick. The raid swaps
its legends for LEGEND_MINI_PAD and LEGEND_PAD; this floor line never had a pad version, and the v11.58 note says it is the only
place the floor controls are taught. The line is not a TXSHIP key (the table holds no WASD, JOG or STATION), no ruling or comment
calls it keyboard only on purpose, and it is not balance.

THE BUILD. One edit at the end of drawHubHUD, the verdict's corrected fix in effect: with a controller connected the bottom line

keyLabel('KeyE','E') the station prompt uses. Without one it draws exactly what it drew before. The corrected fix is a one-line
ternary on the fillText line itself, but that line holds a literal middle dot, and a patch script cannot anchor on it: PowerShell
5.1 reads the .ps1 as ANSI and the escaped anchor never matches. So the script anchors on the three ASCII lines above it (the
v10.93 colour note, the font and fill, the centre alignment) and adds if(padOn()){ fillText the pad line at W/2,H-16; textAlign
left; return; } before it. The keyboard line is the last draw in the function and the return also sets the alignment back, so the
two are the same behaviour, and the keyboard line is left byte for byte. The new line writes its dots as the escape
backslash-u00b7, the way the credits line in the same function does, so the script stays ASCII. No word of existing player text
was reworded, the new words use none of the retired words, and no number, dial, loot table or seeded draw moved; map building is
not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint in __verifySafe cannot move. The H CONTROLS panel on the floor is also keyboard only on
a controller; that is outside this finding and is not changed here.
