## v15.58 - EXTRACTING WITH THE FREEBIE KIT KEEPS THE GUN YOU CHOSE IN GUN 1

First run audit finding (MEDIUM), entry 6 of the confirmed list.

Fresh profile: weapons ['pistol'], equipped 'fists'. Take the welcome pack, open the stash and choose Equip as your gun on the
Compact SMG, as the loaner line tells you to (P.weapons ['pistol','smg'], P.equipped 'smg'). At the lift answer FREEBIE KIT
(P.freeKit=1). buildRaid loads the SMG from P.equipped, moves the flag onto the raid (g.freeKit=1), then replaces the gun with
WEAPONS[FREEKIT_GUN] and sets wepIssued=false and wepFromArmory=false, so that an extraction keeps the kit (v6.88, his spec), and
gun 2 becomes issued fists. Extract. carriedGuns skips only issued guns and fists, so kept=[pistol]. The per-hand loop finds
'pistol' already owned and not from the armoury and puts a gun_pistol in the stash, which is the kit being kept, as intended.
Then "if(kept.length) P.equipped=kept[0].id;" set gun 1 to 'pistol'. Nothing put it back: the v14.79 repair below it only acts on
a gun he does not own, and the gun slot snapshot went at v13.06. His SMG was quietly unequipped, the sector page said Going up
with: Scav Pistol, and the next raid took his own armoury pistol up, where it wears and can be lost. A character still on fists
was moved to the pistol the same way, which undoes the v2.80 rolled starter that v2.82 protects on the death path. What is New
(the v13.06 line) promises that what you go up with comes from the gun you have equipped, which taking the kit does not change,
and the death path already treats this pistol as the kit's loaner rather than his gun (_egFree, v12.03). The v12.38 comment
calls this line the best carried gun going in gun 1; no comment or ruling applies that to the kit's gun.

The verdict found the proposed fix incomplete: the gun 2 collision repair below also read the raw list. His own SMG in gun 1 and
his own Burst Carbine in gun 2, kit taken, a Carbine picked up in the raid, extract: kept=[carbine,pistol], gun 1 became the
Carbine by the tier sort, gun 2 collided with it, and the repair put kept[1], the kit pistol, in gun 2.

THE BUILD. Two edits in the extract branch of endRaid, from the verdict's corrected fix. The line that sets gun 1 now reads a
filtered list, _keq: kept without a gun whose id is FREEKIT_GUN, held in either hand (compared by object with _kp.wep or
_kp.sec, _kp being G.player from the loop above) and not from the armoury, on a raid with G.freeKit set. That is the death
path's _egFree test. If _keq is empty, gun 1 is left as he set it. The gun 2 collision repair reads _keq in both places too.
The kit pistol is still kept exactly as before: the per-hand loop that banks it is untouched. A gun found in the raid still
takes gun 1 by the tier sort. This keeps his own choice; it is not an automatic switch to a gun (his ruling of 2026-09-13
stands). A Scav Pistol found in the raid on a freebie run, not from the armoury, is treated as the kit pistol here, the same
approximation _egFree makes on the death path. A character on fists who extracts on the kit now stays on fists and goes up with
a rolled loaner next time, as a fresh character does, and if he owned no pistol the kit pistol still goes to his armoury.

## v15.57 - THE END-OF-RAID CARD CAN BE LEFT WITH A CONTROLLER

First run audit finding (HIGH), entry 5 of the confirmed list.

Play with only a controller: take the welcome pack, ascend, then extract or die. endRaid puts .on on #outcome, whose class is
outcome, not modal, and leaves state at 'raid' with G.over set. On every frame after that pollPad asks padMenu first, and
padOpenModal looked only for an open .modal, the pause box, the title and #hub, so it returned null and padMenu returned false.
The pad fell through to the raid branch, where every way to act is shut once the raid is over: A does not fire (rtOn needs
!G.over), B taps Space and tryRoll needs !G.over, Menu taps P and the pause line needs !G.over, and togglePauseBox returns at once
when G.over is set. Nothing else presses #oc_btn: its onclick is the only way off the card, and PAD.focus and .padfocus are set
only inside padMenu. So a pad player's first extraction or first death left him on the card until he picked up the mouse.
v14.23 closed the same gap for the pause box and v14.26 for the title screen; this third panel that is not a .modal was missed.
hubModalOpen already counts the card as a panel.

THE BUILD. Two lines in padOpenModal, after the pause box and before the title: an #outcome with .on is returned as the open
panel. padFocusables finds Log run and return first and Copy report second (the run feel tags are .tag divs and the note is a
textarea, neither a pad control), so the focus lands on Log run and return and A presses it. B's way-out search,
leave|close|not yet|back|done|return, matches Log run and return before Copy report, so B presses the same button; both run the
button's own onclick, so the run is logged, the tags and note go with it, and the page goes back to the Undercroft exactly as a
click does. An A held through the death does not press it: every raid frame stamps PAD.prev for every button, so tap(0) sees a
held A as already down. Checked after the windows, which still win, and after the pause box, which endRaid shuts before the card
goes up. No player text, no number, no dial and no seeded draw moved; map building is not touched.

is up; the page is still in the raid with the same G; no window and no pause box over the card; Log run and return is among

card up; A let go keeps it up (control); a fresh A must leave the card the same way. When a pad press fails to leave, a plain

## v15.56 - A DOOR KEY IS NEVER HIDDEN IN THE VAULT CASE OR BEHIND ANOTHER LOCKED DOOR

Keys audit finding 4 (LOW).

Every locked room is promised one key on the map (v1.75): the guarantee in buildRaid looks for a copy of the key outside the room it
opens, and if there is none it pushes the key into a random container from a list that leaves out caches, the strongbox and boxes
inside THAT room. Two kinds of box it must never use were still on the list. THE VAULT CASE (v4.40) is built just above the
guarantee as type jackpot with no cache flag, so it was a legal pick. LOOT.jackpot has no KEY, so a key in the case can only come
from here, and his v4.40 answer says the case is not on the map and not marked; with a Data Core burned, startRaid lists every box
holding a key_ item and the sector map drew KEY on it. The finding estimates about one raid in 70 to 80 (not measured). And outside()
only tests the room this key opens, so an ordinary crate, locker or safe standing inside a DIFFERENT locked room was legal too: the
v2.12 reach pass leaves those in place on purpose (49 across 20 maps). The door then needs a second key first and nothing says so,
and if two rooms' keys land in each other's rooms neither door opens unless a spare key rolls or the Peddler stocks one. The
verdict found the same hole in the have test: a KEY that rolled naturally (LOOT.safe or LOOT.cache) into a safe or cache inside
another locked room counted as the promise kept, so no reachable key was placed.

THE BUILD. Three edits inside the guarantee IIFE, all existing comments kept.
1. sealedAny(CC), defined once before the room loop: true when the box is within 40 units of ANY locked room, the same 40 unit test
   outside() uses for one room.
2. The have test now records two answers in the same pass: have, any copy outside this room (the old answer), and haveOpen, a copy
   clear of every locked room. Only haveOpen skips the room.
3. The candidate list and the single ri(0,cands.length-1) draw are exactly as before. If the drawn box is THE VAULT CASE or
   sealedAny, the pick walks forward through the same list, wrapping, to the next box that is neither. When have was true (the old
   code took no draw at all, because a copy behind another door satisfied it) no draw is taken now either: the walk starts at
   (seed>>>0)%cands.length, buildRaid's own seed. If no box on the list qualifies, no key is placed, as when the list was empty.

WHY NOT THE VERDICT'S correctedFix AS WRITTEN. It filters the jackpot and every sealed box out of the list BEFORE the draw. A shorter
list turns the same drawn number into a different box, so on seeds where the old key already sat in a perfectly good box it would
move, and on the seeds where a natural key sat behind another door it adds one ri draw and shifts everything drawn after it. Both
break the seed fingerprint rule. This build does the same thing for the broken cases and nothing at all for the rest: on every seed
the guarantee takes the same draws in the same order, and every key the old code put in an open box stays in that box. Only a key
the old code put in THE VAULT CASE or behind a locked door, or never placed because of a sealed natural copy, lands somewhere new.
Nothing after the guarantee reads which box holds a key until startRaid builds G.intelKeys (checked: no later line in buildRaid
draws from container loot or best), no container is added or removed, and no loot table, number, dial or player text moved, so the
seed 4242 counts (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move. If seed 4242 was itself one of the broken cases on either map, a key
there moves box; the counts still hold.

MEASURED. No browser. The old and new guarantee blocks were cut out of the real file and run side by side in JScript (cscript) over
6000 synthetic layouts with 1 to 4 locked rooms, up to 43 boxes, a quarter of them set inside a room, caches, strongboxes, natural
keys in 12 percent of boxes and a Vault Case sometimes inside a room, far more broken cases than a real map has: draws taken and the
RNG state after were identical in all 6000; 11566 keys the old code put in an open box stayed in exactly that box; all 2554 broken
old placements (1032 of them the sealed natural copy) went to a box clear of every room and not the case; and whenever a legal box
existed every room had a copy clear of every room.

Check 15.56 runs two ascents on COLD STORAGE (map 0, rooms BLAST FREEZER and FOREMAN OFFICE) at seed 4242 with mkContainer wrapped
for the ascent only. The wrapper takes every key_ item out of every box it builds, sets the first ordinary box (crate, locker, safe
or body) down in the middle of the Blast Freezer holding a Foreman Office Key, moves THE VAULT CASE to the middle of the map if it was
built within 40 of a locked room, and gives every other box the strongbox flag, which keeps it out of the key draw. Ascent two also
leaves alone the next ordinary box built 240 clear of every locked room (more than a pad push can move it). Controls on each ascent:
a live raid whose map carries the authored rooms in order at the authored spot; the staged boxes are in G.containers with the box
in the freezer before THE VAULT CASE; the jackpot is tagged THE VAULT CASE and stands clear of every room; the freezer box is still
strictly inside the freezer, not strong, not a cache, and still holds its Foreman Office Key; on ascent two the open box is in the
list before the case and not strong; and no other box built before THE VAULT CASE (the boxes the draw saw) is out of the strongbox
or cache flags. Ascent one: THE VAULT CASE must hold no key and the freezer box exactly one. On v15.55 the office key is kept by
the freezer box, and the freezer key has only the case to go to, so it goes into THE VAULT CASE and the check fails for the
finding's own reason. Ascent two: the open box must hold both keys, and the case none. On v15.55 the office key is again kept by
the box behind the freezer door and no office key reaches the open box, so it fails there too; on v15.56 the office key walks from
the seed to the open box and the freezer key from its draw. A control that cannot run after a failure keeps the failure. The same
staging was run against both blocks in JScript over 3000 random draws and seeds: the old block failed both ascents 3000 times, the
new block passed both 3000 times. In finally mkContainer is put back (also after each ascent), the raid is abandoned, the profile
snapshot goes back through __applyLoaded and the fixture is cleaned.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. No check reads which box the guarantee chose. Check 15.17 takes whichever listed box holds a
key at seed 4242 and stages its own when there is none; 15.55 stages its own key box. __verify counts containers and entities only.

Dry run on fresh scratch copies of dark_raiders.html and mkfixture.ps1 as they stand (15.51 applied): p1552 and f1552, p1553 and
f1553, p1554 and f1554, p1555 and f1555, then p1556 and f1556, in version order with nothing moved by hand, every script printing OK
and every anchor a whole line block matching once; a second p1556 run was refused with the first anchor matching 0 times. The
chained guarantee block and the check entry both parse in JScript. None of p1552 to p1555 touches the guarantee. p1557 anchors on
var VER='15.56', which this build writes, and p1557 to p1559 with f1557 to f1559 applied on top, all OK. Rechecked in review with a
fresh JScript run of the real old and new blocks over 8000 other synthetic layouts: 0 RNG state differences, 6558 good placements
unmoved and 0 moved, 2986 broken old placements and not one new key put in the case or inside a locked room, and every room on a
layout with a legal box had a copy clear of every room; the check's staging over 3000 seeds failed both ascents on the old block every time and passed both on the new.

Not verified: the check has not been run in a browser, the seed 4242 counts were not re-read on a built fixture, and no real raid

## v15.55 - THE INTEL KEY MARK LEAVES A CONTAINER ONCE ITS KEY IS TAKEN OUT

Keys audit finding 3 (MEDIUM).

Slot a Data Core and ascend. startRaid lists every container whose loot holds a key_ item in G.intelKeys, and the sector map draws
a gold KEY on each. The mark asked one thing, if(IKC.opened) continue, and opened turns true only in the full open, when the whole
search bar fills. Live play empties a box through the staged pulls in updatePlayer: near.loot.shift() then openContainer(near,[_k]),
which returns through grantLoot before ct.opened=true. Loot is sorted worst first (the locked room guarantee re-sorts after it
pushes the key, and setLoot and mkContainer sort the same way), and a key is worth 600 to 750, so a safe or locker that also holds
a Titanium Cell, a better gun or a Black Box gives up its key first. Let go of X or E before the bar fills, or be pulled into a
fight, and the key is in the backpack while the box stays shut with no key in it. The KEY stayed on it for the rest of the raid,
even after the key was spent at the door, and with several locked rooms it sent him back across the map for a second key that was
not there. Nothing else ever took the box off the list: restock skips unopened boxes and the merc skips half searched ones. This is
the same wrong mark v15.17 took off restocked boxes, reached by an ordinary search broken off early. The map header calls keys live
intel, so it is a bug, not a rule. Crates never showed it: a crate's key is its last item and lands on the frame opened is set.

THE BUILD. One line in drawMapOverlay, the INTEL block: a listed container is skipped when it is opened or when nothing in its loot
starts with key_, the same test startRaid used to put it on the list. A box that held two keys keeps its mark until both are out.
The loot is read as (IKC.loot||[]) so a container without a loot array can never throw the whole map; the finding's fix read
IKC.loot directly and every container has one today. The v15.17 restock splice is left in place: it is now redundant for the mark
but harmless. Map only, drawn on the frame: no player text, no number, no dial, no loot table and no seeded draw moved, and map
building is untouched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move.

MEASURED. Check 15.55 burns a Data Core (P.intel=1 before __deploy at seed 4242, map 0) and requires the ascent to have set G.intel,
built G.intelKeys and spent the core. It takes a shut container the game listed that holds its key and has a spot in search reach
(24, 32, 40 or 16 units out, no wall within his radius plus 1.5, clear line on G.vseg), else any shut non-strongbox with such a
spot; the key is its own, else a listed one, else key_ of the first locked room. It stages that box with setLoot as the key plus a
Meridian Black Box and wants the game's own sort to put the key first (else SKIP), with the search at zero. He is put on the spot
with the map, backpack, drag, stall and waves cleared and iv 99, and any other shut container within 60 is marked opened for the
check. Controls: one frame of updatePlayer with no key down leaves him within 0.5 of the spot, finds that box as G.nearContainer and
searches nothing; with G.intelKeys set to that box alone the sector map calls mapLabel with KEY exactly once (calls are counted, so
the same-word merge cannot hide one). Then the play path: X held, updatePlayer(1/30) a frame at a time until no key is left in the
box (900 frames at most), X let go. Controls: the raid is live and he is up, the backpack holds one more of that key, the box is
still not opened, and its loot is the Black Box alone. Then the map is drawn again with that box alone on the list and must write
no KEY. On v15.54 it writes one, so the check fails there for the finding's own reason. Last, a second shut container still holding
a key (a listed one, else the first shut container, given the key) alone on the list must still get exactly one KEY; that holds on
both builds. In finally mapLabel is put back, keys and mouse.down are cleared, the containers marked opened are shut again,
G.intelKeys and G.ents are put back, his position, speed, iv, roll and auto jog are restored, the map, backpack, drag, stall, stall
lock, search and wave clock are restored, the raid is abandoned, the profile snapshot goes back through __applyLoaded and the
fixture is cleaned.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. Check 15.17 is the only one that draws the intel marks. Its crate and locker restock with no
key and leave the list, and its third container still holds its key, so it draws the same marks on v15.55 as on v15.54. No other
check reads G.intelKeys or the drawMapOverlay source near the INTEL block.

## v15.54 - WITH THE FREEBIE KIT TAKEN, BUILD A RACK NAMES THE PACKED PARTS IT USES

Rack audit finding (LOW).

At the Stash, with 7 Circuit Boards and enough of the other three parts, pack 3 Circuit Boards, then press TAKE THE FREEBIE KIT.
The button keeps the packing aside, P.kitSaved={kit:(P.kit||[]).slice(),hot:...}, and then sets P.kit=[] (v12.16), and the
panel says "Your own packing is kept for when you switch back." At THE MAINFRAME, press BUILD A RACK. spendHeld counted packed
copies through packedCount, which walks stageKitLive, which reads only P.kit, so it found 0 packed and all 7 boards loose:
free=7, fromPacked=0. Six boards came out of the stash, spendHeld returned 0, and the rack line had no backpack sentence (v15.18
adds one only when that number is above 0). Nothing updates P.kitSaved when parts are spent, so the set-aside list still named 3
boards. At the lift, askKit counts that list raw (v14.65) and said "the 3 items you packed"; MY LOADOUT and USE MY OWN GEAR both
run freeKitRestore, which trims the list against the stash, so he went up with 1 board and nothing had said why. Without the
freebie kit the same rack says "Used 2 packed Circuit Board out of your backpack." The crafting bench spends through spendHeld
too, and since v15.53 so do SLOT A DATA CORE and Arm on the ascent check, so all of them had the same gap.

THE BUILD. One edit, spendHeld, the corrected fix from the audit verdict. When P.freeKit is set and P.kitSaved.kit is a list, the
copies of that item on the set-aside list are counted as packed, capped at what the stash holds beyond P.kit's live packing (the
same test freeKitRestore makes, so a set-aside list longer than the stash is not over-counted). Loose copies still go first
(v13.59). Any set-aside copies still needed come off the set-aside list from the end, and once none of that item are left on it,
a set-aside belt key bound to that item is let go, the way clearKeysFor does for live packing (dropDeadKeys still runs in
freeKitRestore). With no freebie kit taken, or no set-aside list, the old path runs unchanged: unpackSome on P.kit. The return
value is the number of packed copies used either way, so buildRack, the bench, SLOT A DATA CORE and Arm name them with their
existing sentences, and askKit's raw count now matches what freeKitRestore gives back. The Stash grid is greyed and takes no
pointer while the freebie kit is on, so P.kit stays empty there. No player text was added or reworded, no TXSHIP key touched, and
no number, dial, loot table or seeded draw moved. The map build is not touched, so the seed 4242 fingerprint (ents 85/374,
containers 165/593) cannot move.

MEASURED. Check 15.54 runs in the Undercroft (it skips while a raid is live), snapshots the profile after __topClear and
__cleanProfile, and stubs say so the rack line is read from the call itself. Each arm stages P.racks 0, P.arrays 0, no freebie
kit, no set-aside list, no belt key, the rack cost in the stash plus one extra Circuit Board and one Medkit, and packs 3 boards
and the Medkit, so the loose boards cover all but 2 (EXP, computed from RACK_COST).
- CONTROL, no freebie kit: the staging reads back (7 held, 3 packed, rack affordable), buildRack builds rack 1, the line names
  " 2 packed Circuit Board" and 1 board is left packed. This holds on both builds and proves the rack names packed parts here.
- THE FIX: the same staging, then renderFreeKit and the real .fkbtn onclick. Control: the kit is taken, the set-aside list holds
  3 boards and the Medkit, nothing is live-packed, 7 boards are held and a rack is affordable. buildRack must build rack 1
  (control), and then the line must contain " 2 packed Circuit Board" and "backpack", the set-aside list must hold 1 board and
  still the Medkit. Then askKit is drawn and "the N items you packed" is read from #asksub, and freeKitRestore runs. Control: MY
  LOADOUT gives back 2 (the board still held and the Medkit), which holds on both builds. The lift count N must equal it.
On v15.53 the rack line has no backpack sentence, the set-aside list still holds 3 boards, and the lift says 4 items while 2 go
up, so the check fails there for the finding's own reason. A later control that cannot run keeps a failure already found. In
finally say, ASKYES and ASKALT are put back, the lift question is closed, the profile snapshot goes back through
window.__applyLoaded, the freebie kit panel and the Mainframe are redrawn from it, then __topClear and __cleanProfile.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. 15.18 and 14.98 build racks and 15.52 presses BUILD A RACK with no freebie kit taken and no
set-aside list, and 15.53 slots a core the same way, so spendHeld takes the old path in all of them. 14.65, 12.26, 12.82, 12.87,
13.06 and 15.11 take the freebie kit or set packing aside but spend nothing from the stash. No check crafts with the freebie kit on.

Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html and mkfixture.ps1 as they stand (15.51 applied): p1552 and f1552, p1553 and f1553,
then p1554 printed OK, 2 edits plus DEVNOW, and f1554 printed OK, 1 edit, every anchor a whole line block matching once. The
edited spendHeld and the check parse in JScript. A JScript model of the old and new spendHeld with this staging gave: no freebie
kit, both builds use 2 packed boards and 2 go up; freebie kit taken, the old one uses 0 and leaves 4 set aside while 2 go up, the
new one uses 2 and leaves 2 set aside (1 board and the Medkit, its belt key kept) and 2 go up. All five files are ASCII only.

## v15.53 - SLOT A DATA CORE SAYS WHEN IT TAKES A PACKED CORE OUT OF THE BACKPACK

Rack audit finding (LOW).

At the Stash, pack your only Data Core into the backpack (drag it in, or Equip). Packing leaves the item in P.stash, so THE
MAINFRAME RACKS tab still says "One is in the stash." and SLOT A DATA CORE is live. Press it: "Core slotted. Your next ascent
carries intel." slotCore spliced the first core out of P.stash with no look at the packing, so with every core he held packed
the backpack lost its core with no word. P.kit still named it until stageKitLive next read it and trimmed it quietly, and a belt
key bound to the core stayed pointing at nothing until dropDeadKeys ran after a raid. BUILD A RACK, two buttons up in the same
tab, has spent through spendHeld since v13.59 and named the packed parts it took out of the backpack since v15.18. With a loose
core left over the old splice did no harm, because the packed copy stayed live. The Arm button on the Intel row of the ascent
check (renderStage) had the same bare splice.

THE BUILD. Two edits, both the corrected fix from the audit verdict.
1. slotCore: P.stash.splice(ix,1) becomes var _cp=spendHeld('core',1). A loose core goes first (the v13.59 rule); only when
   every core is packed does spendHeld call unpackSome, which takes the core off P.kit and, through clearKeysFor, lets its belt
   key go, and then the stash copy is spent. The core line is unchanged and one sentence is added after it when a packed core
   was taken: "Used 1 packed Data Core out of your backpack.", the same words BUILD A RACK uses. One toast, because a second
   would write over the first.
2. renderStage, the Intel row: the Arm handler spends through spendHeld the same way, and when it had to take a packed core it
   says "Used 1 packed Data Core out of your backpack." through say2, the Undercroft answer line the rest of that screen uses.
   No route opens the ascent check today (every way up goes through ascendNow since v6.18, and nothing adds on to #stagemodal),
   so this edit only keeps the two ways to spend a core one rule.
"Core slotted. Your next ascent carries intel." is not a key in TXSHIP, and no sentence in TXSHIP was reworded; the new
sentence is new text. No number, no dial, no loot table and no seeded draw moved. The map build is not touched, so the seed 4242
fingerprint (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move. The v14.99 core hint and the button label are untouched.

MEASURED. Check 15.53 runs in the Undercroft (it skips while a raid is live), snapshots the profile after __topClear and
__cleanProfile, and stubs say and say2 so both lines are read from the calls themselves (a raid an earlier check ended leaves G
set, and say then writes G.msg rather than the toast). Each arm stages P.intel 0, no freebie kit and no set-aside packing
(P.freeKit 0, P.kitSaved null, so the check does not lean on what the profile holds), P.stash with that many cores, P.kit with
that many packed and, when one is packed, belt key 4 (P.hotAssign[3]) on the core, and reads the staging back through
heldCount, packedCount and the key before it acts.
- CONTROL: two cores, one packed. slotCore must slot (P.intel set, "Core slotted" said), or SKIP. Then one core must be left, the
  packed one still live, belt key 4 still on it, and nothing said of packed or the backpack. This holds on both builds and
  proves the loose copy still goes first.
- ARM ONE: one core, packed. Control: slotted, no core left, "Core slotted" said. Then the line must contain "1 packed Data Core"
  and "backpack", and belt key 4 must be empty. On v15.52 the line is the bare core line and the key still names the core, so
  the check fails there for the finding's own reason.
- ARM TWO: the same staging, renderStage drawn, and the Arm button found by its text inside #stageload (SKIP if the ascent check
  will not draw or offers no Arm). Its onclick runs. Control: armed and no core left. Then say2 must have said "1 packed Data
  Core" and "backpack", and belt key 4 must be empty. On v15.52 nothing is said and the key stays.
A later control that cannot run keeps a failure already found, so the old build fails rather than skips. In finally say and say2
are put back, the profile snapshot goes back through window.__applyLoaded, the Mainframe and the ascent check are redrawn from
it, then __topClear and __cleanProfile.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. 15.52 stages the core loose and asserts that no core is slotted, so spendHeld spends the
same loose copy the splice did. 14.99 reads only the Mainframe core hint, 15.17 sets P.intel by hand, 13.61 checks that a
restored code clears an armed core, and 10.97 only lists the core as wanted because slotCore exists. No other check calls slotCore
or presses Arm.

## v15.52 - BUILD A RACK KEEPS THE CONTROLLER HIGHLIGHT WHEN IT GREYS OUT

Rack audit finding (MEDIUM).

On a controller, open THE MAINFRAME on its RACKS tab with exactly one rack's worth of parts in the stash and a Data Core, put
the highlight on BUILD A RACK and press A. The rack goes up, "Rack 1 hums to life", and renderMainframe greys the button out
because the parts are gone. padFocusables leaves out disabled controls, so on the next poll BUILD A RACK was no longer in the
list, and the v14.22 recovery in padMenu (a rebuilt panel keeps the pad's place) put the focus on list[PAD.focusIx], the same
index, which is now SLOT A DATA CORE. The stick never moved. The next A, say to try another rack, ran slotCore: the core left the
stash and P.intel went to 1, and nothing unslots it. At nine racks the same thing happened with the tenth rack: BUILD A RACK
became THE WALL IS FULL (disabled), FOLD 10 RACKS INTO AN ARRAY went live right after it in page order and took the highlight,
and the next A folded all ten racks into an Array without being asked. A mouse click never moves anything, and the v14.22 line
was written for panels that rebuild their controls, not for a control that stays put and greys out. The same jump as the v14.22
bug that moved focus onto TAKE THE FREEBIE KIT.

THE BUILD. Two lines in padMenu.
1. Before the recovery: if the focused control is disabled, still inside the same panel, measures at least 4 by 4 and is not
   display none or visibility hidden, the pad stays on it and the recovery does not run. A on a disabled button does nothing,
   exactly as a mouse click on it does (HTMLElement.click returns at once on a disabled control). padStep reads only the current
   control's rectangle, so the D-pad still steps off it from where it sits, and the highlight stays drawn where he left it.
   A panel that rebuilds its controls still recovers as v14.22 set it, because the old control has left the panel, and a
   control hidden with its tab measures 0 by 0 and hands the pad on as before.
2. PAD.focusIx is written only when the focus is in the list, so a disabled control kept under the pad does not overwrite the
   place it last held with -1.
No player text, no number, no dial, no loot table and no seeded draw moved. The map build is not touched, so the seed 4242
fingerprint (ents 85/374, containers 165/593) cannot move.

MEASURED. Check 15.52 runs in the Undercroft (it skips while a raid is live), snapshots the profile, stubs say, and fakes one
connected controller (17 buttons, 4 zero axes) through navigator.getGamepads. Each arm stages P.racks, P.arrays 0, P.intel 0,
nothing packed and the parts loose in the stash, opens the Mainframe with openOps('mf'), polls once, puts the highlight on BUILD A
RACK with padSetFocus and polls again, then A down, A up, one idle poll, A down, A up.
- CONTROL: parts for two racks and a Data Core. BUILD A RACK is still live after the first rack, so both presses must build a
  rack, with no core slotted and the core still in the stash. This proves the faked A reaches the highlighted button and that
  the highlight stays while the button is live. It holds on both builds; if not, SKIP. Also SKIP if BUILD A RACK is not in
  padFocusables (a 0x0 pane) or the highlight will not stay on it.
- ARM A: parts for one rack and a Data Core. Control: P.racks is 1. Then the core must still be in the stash with P.intel 0, and
  the highlight must still be on BUILD A RACK. On v15.51 the second A slots the core (P.intel 1, no core left), so the check
  fails there for the finding's own reason.
- ARM B: ARRAY_RACKS-1 racks (nine) and parts for one. Control: racks plus ten for each Array equals ten, a conserved count that
  proves the tenth rack went up whether or not a fold followed. Then P.arrays must be 0 and P.racks 10. On v15.51 it ends with
  0 racks and 1 Array.
A later control that cannot run keeps a failure already found, so the old build fails rather than skips. In finally say is put
back, the pad is disconnected with one poll, the pad focus, focusIx and focusMd are cleared and padRelease run,
navigator.getGamepads is restored, PAD.aSpent and PAD.announced are restored, the Mainframe window is shut if it was shut before,

## v15.50 - THE CONTROLLER MENU BUTTON PAUSES AT THE PEDDLER STALL

Pause audit finding 10 (LOW).

On a controller, open the Peddler's stall with X and press Menu. Nothing happened. pollPad asks padMenu first, but padOpenModal
looks only for an open .modal, the pause box, the title and the Undercroft screen, and the stall is none of them: drawTrade paints
it on the canvas. So padMenu returned false and the raid reached the stall branch, if(G.trade&&!G.over). That branch reads only
D-UP, D-DOWN, A and X, stamps PAD.prev and returns, before the tap loop further down where PADTAP turns button 9 into KeyP. No
other line reads button 9 in a raid. The stall is not a pause on purpose (v12.34: the raid clock, the machines, the extraction
clocks and the waves all run on behind it), so a pad player could not stop the raid until he walked away with X. Keyboard P at the
same stall reaches raidKey, passes the stall block (which closes only on ESC, E, TAB, I and B) and opens the pause box. The v13.49
line "nothing else on the pad acts behind the panel" is about world actions, and pausing is not one of them.

THE BUILD. One line in the stall branch of pollPad, after the X line and before PAD.prev is stamped: a fresh Menu press calls
raidKey('KeyP',false,null) and lets KeyP go, exactly what the tap loop does in the rest of the raid. The pause box opens over the
open stall and the stall is still open behind it. On the next poll padOpenModal finds the box, so padMenu owns the pad, and its
tap(9) sees PAD.prev[9] already true, so the same held Menu does not resume the run at once; Menu or B then resumes it with the
stall still open. If X and Menu land on the same poll, the stall shuts and the box opens, the same as E then P on the keyboard.
No player text, no number, no dial and no seeded draw moved.

MEASURED. Check 15.50 deploys a raid at seed 4242 with the map, backpack, emote bar, stall and drag cleared and the box shut, and
fakes one connected controller (17 buttons, 4 zero axes) through navigator.getGamepads. It takes the raid's own Peddler, or makes
one beside him if the map has none; G.ents is not touched. Controls: two idle polls leave the box shut; a fresh Menu with the stall
shut opens the box through the raid tap loop, so the faked Menu reaches the game; the box shut again and an idle poll keep it shut;
with G.trade set to the Peddler an idle poll leaves the stall open and the box shut; keyboard raidKey P at the open stall opens the
box and leaves the stall open, so a pause at the stall is offered; shut again with the stall still open. Then a fresh Menu at the
open stall must open the box. On v15.49 the stall branch returns without reading button 9 and the box stays shut, so the check
fails there for the finding's own reason. When it opens, the stall must still be open behind it, and one more poll with the same
Menu held must leave the box open. In finally the box is shut, the pad is disconnected with one poll, the pad focus is cleared and
padRelease run, navigator.getGamepads is put back, PAD.aSpent, PAD.xAfterTrade and PAD.announced are restored, keys and mouse.down
are cleared, the map, backpack, emote bar, stall, stall lock, stall marker and drag are put back and the raid is abandoned.

## v15.49 - HOLDING ESC OR P DOES NOT FLICKER THE PAUSE BOX

Pause audit finding 9 (MEDIUM).

In a raid, hold P for longer than the keyboard's repeat delay. The first keydown opens the pause box. Every key repeat after it
also reaches raidKey: the main keydown listener drops repeats only on its Backquote, Backspace and TAB lines, the pause lockout at
the top of raidKey lets P, ESC and TAB through, and the toggle line tested repeat only for TAB. So the box flipped open and shut
on every repeat, each opening wiped keys and mouse.down, and when P was let go the box was open or shut by chance. Holding ESC did
the same by a two-step loop: with the box open, the capture-phase ESC and TAB listener shut it on a repeat (it skipped only TAB
repeats, v13.44), and the next repeat reached raidKey with the box shut and opened it again. Holding the ESC that closes the map
ends the same way, because the map and backpack line takes only a fresh press and every repeat falls through to the toggle. On the
Undercroft floor the floor branch already requires a fresh press, but a held ESC still opened the box and its first repeat, caught
by the capture listener, shut it again. v13.44 fixed exactly this for TAB and left ESC and P.

THE BUILD. Two lines. In raidKey the pause toggle now reads (code==='Escape'||code==='KeyP'||code==='Tab')&&!repeat, so a key
repeat of any of the three does nothing there. In the capture listener the v13.44 line becomes if(ev.repeat) return, still after
its stopPropagation and preventDefault, so while the box is open every repeated ESC or TAB is swallowed and neither the raid keys
nor the floor branch can reopen it. A fresh press of ESC, P or TAB toggles the box exactly as before. The gamepad calls raidKey
with repeat false from its edge-detected taps, so the pad is unchanged. No player text, no number, no dial and no seeded draw
moved.

MEASURED. Check 15.49 deploys a raid at seed 4242 with the map, backpack, emote bar and stall shut and the box down. Control: a
fresh raidKey P opens the box and a second closes it. Then a fresh P opens it and five raidKey P repeats follow; the box must not
flip and must rest open. On v15.48 it flips five times and rests shut, so the check fails there for the finding's own reason.
Then the map is opened and a fresh raidKey ESC is pressed; control: the map closed and the box stayed shut. Four raidKey ESC
repeats follow; the box must not flip and must rest shut (v15.48 flips four times). Then the page path: control that the page is
in the raid state, P opens the box, and a fresh ESC keydown dispatched on document.body (so the capture listener on window runs
first, as for a real key) closes it. P opens it again and four repeated ESC keydowns are dispatched on the body; the box must not
flip and must rest open (on v15.48 the first repeat shuts it through the capture listener and the next opens it through raidKey,
four flips). Last, fresh raidKey TAB presses still open and close the box on both builds. Keys and mouse.down are cleared around
every press; the box is shut, the map, backpack, emote bar, stall and drag are put back and the raid is abandoned in finally.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. No check in mkfixture.ps1 sends a key repeat (no repeat:true event and no raidKey call with
repeat true), and every pause check toggles the box with fresh presses, which still toggle. Check 13.44 presses TAB fresh through
window, and a fresh TAB still toggles the box.

## v15.48 - WHILE THE SITE BURNS OR A DEATH PLAYS OUT, THE PAUSE BOX OFFERS NO ABANDON AND NO EXTRACT

Pause audit finding 8 (MEDIUM).

Let the raid clock run out with no extraction called. The loop sets G.nuking, says MERIDIAN IS BURNING THE SITE, and from then on
runs tickNuke in place of updatePlayer, so there is no way out: tickNuke puts him down at 1.15 seconds and ends the raid with
endRaid('dead') at 2.6. But the pause box and the Abandon run handler only asked whether he was down, hp 0 or in the death beat,
and for the first 1.15 seconds of the burn he is none of those. ESC, P, TAB or the pad Menu button in that second froze the burn
and offered Abandon run, and its confirm ran endRaid('abandon'): the armoury guns the death would have taken were kept and no death
was counted. That is the same death-into-abandon swap v9.37 closed for the bleed-out; the burn was missed. Coming back empty
stands: a timer death stays a death.

The same test also chose the title and the downed line. killPlayer leaves hp 0 with downed false for a 1.5 second death beat, and
G.over is not set, so ESC still opens the box. Over that beat the box read BLEEDING OUT and showed YOU ARE DOWNED, You can extract
while downed, over a dead man, and pressing Abandon run brought that line up again. Later in the burn, when tickNuke has put him
down, the box said the same thing while nothing could be extracted.

THE BUILD. Two places, same rule. In togglePauseBox the bleed test also counts G.nuking, so Abandon run is hidden and a primed
confirm is put away for the whole burn; a second flag, set only for a real downed player outside the burn, now picks the BLEEDING
OUT title and the downed line, so the burn and the death beat read RAID PAUSED with no line. The Abandon run handler refuses on the
same widened test and brings up the downed line only for a real downed player outside the burn. The confirm handler needs nothing:
an open box pauses the clock, so the box cannot already be armed when the burn starts. Being downed is unchanged: BLEEDING OUT,
the downed line and no Abandon run. On his feet Abandon run is offered and arms as before. The words of the title and the downed
line are untouched (neither is a TXSHIP key). No player text, no number, no dial and no seeded draw moved.

MEASURED. Check 15.48 deploys a raid at seed 4242, lifts every ent and presses P through raidKey to open and close the box, reading
its title, Abandon run and the downed line, then pressing Abandon run once and reading the confirm and the line again, and putting
the button back to sleep. Controls: the raid has a clock, no call made, is fresh and on his feet; on his feet the box reads RAID
PAUSED, offers Abandon run with no line and the press arms the confirm; really downed (downed, hp 0) it reads BLEEDING OUT with the
line and no Abandon run and the press arms nothing. Then one live frame through __loop with 0.01 seconds left; control: that frame
started the burn on its own branch and he is not down yet. In that first frame of the burn the box must not offer Abandon run and
the press must not arm the confirm; on v15.47 it offers it and arms YES, ABANDON THIS RUN, so the check fails there for the
finding's own reason. Then tickNuke(1.2), the game's own burn step; control: he is down, the burn still running, the raid not
over. Down in the burn the box must not read BLEEDING OUT or show the line, before or after the press; v15.47 shows both. Then the
burn is cleared and killPlayer opens the death beat; control: hp 0, not downed, beat running, not over. Over the beat the box must
not read BLEEDING OUT or show the line, before or after the press; v15.47 shows both. Everything it moved (keys, lastTs, the burn
flags, the death beat, the clock, the killer and med flags, hp, downed, dying, ents) is put back and the raid is abandoned.

Older fixture checks: none restaged. Check 9.37 stages a real downed player (downed, hp 0), which the fix still treats as bleeding
out, so its downed stage and its standing control read as before. Check 10.41 reads the words of the downed line, which are
unchanged. No check reads BLEEDING OUT or opens the box during the burn or the death beat.

## v15.47 - EACH RUN IN YOUR STATS COUNTS ITS LISTENER, PILLBOX AND WARDEN KILLS

Bodies audit finding (LOW).

Destroy a Listener, a Pillbox or the Warden and walk out. The run keeps nine kill counts (sentry, crawler, raider, snitch, warden,
listener, howler, bulwark, choir, where choir is the Pillbox), and the death path in updateEnts fills whichever one matches the kind
that died by your fire (T.kills[e.kind]++). The end card adds every count (the v8.42 fix) and so does statSummary, which feeds the
Average kills per run card on the Your stats tab. But fmtRun, which draws each line of the EVERY RUN, NEWEST FIRST list on that same
tab, added six by hand: sentry, crawler, raider, snitch, howler and bulwark. So a run whose only kill was a Listener, a Pillbox or
the Warden said 1 kill on its end card and counted in the average above, and read 0k on its own line in the list. No comment says
the gap is on purpose and it moves no number in the game.

THE BUILD. One line in fmtRun: the hand-listed sum becomes
  var kills=0; if(r.kills) for(var _fk in r.kills) kills+=(r.kills[_fk]||0);
the same loop statSummary uses. A run logged before the newer counts existed adds the four it carries, and a run with no kill
record reads 0k as before. This is the finding's fix as written; the verdict found it correct and gave no correctedFix. The line
still prints the figure as Nk in the same place. No player text, no number, no dial, no loot table and no seeded draw moved. The
Export for Claude report line (buildExport) has the same six-count list, but that report is for Claude, not the player, and is
left for its own finding.

OLDER CHECKS. None needed restaging. Check 12.90 calls fmtRun on a run with four zero kill counts and reads only the tag it prints.
Check 12.96 reads statSummary, which is not touched. No older check reads the kill figure on a run line or the #loglist text.

MEASURED. Check 15.47 deploys a raid at seed 4242. Controls: the live raid record keeps a number for sentry, listener, warden and
choir, and holds no kills on landing. contractKill is set aside for the one frame (read back, else SKIP) so no saved kill contract
ticks, and put back after. It stages mkSentry, mkListener, mkWarden and mkChoir 60 units around the player as the only entities,
each at 0 health, marked as killed by the player, and runs one updateEnts(0.016) down the ordinary death path. Controls: all four
left the raid, the record counted exactly one of each and four in all. The raid's entities go back, the raid record is given 40
units walked, and the raid is abandoned through __endRaid, which writes the run to the log. The 40 units matter: endRaid throws
away an abandon with under 1.5 seconds on the clock, under 8 units walked, nothing searched and nothing fired as an instant quit
and logs nothing (checks 15.10 and 15.11 rely on a fresh deploy being exactly that), so without them the log control below would
SKIP on both builds and the check could never fail. Controls: the newest run in the log is a new record, this abandon with those
four kills, and
statSummary over that run counts 4 (the Average kills per run card). The #loglist element is emptied and renderHub draws the list
the way the hub does. Controls: the first line reads ABN# and this run number, and it prints a kill figure. The figure must be 4k;
on v15.46 it reads 1k (only the sentry), so the check fails there for the finding's own reason. Kept, on both builds: fmtRun on a
run logged with only sentry, crawler, raider and snitch counts and two raider kills reads 2k, and on a run with no kill record
reads 0k. In finally: contractKill put back, the raid's entities restored, the raid abandoned if still running, the run log and

## v15.46 - REVIVING A PILLAGER NEVER LOSES THE GUN IN HIS HANDS

Bodies audit finding (MEDIUM).

Pick a downed pillager up with E and he pays you out of his own kit: the payout closure in updatePlayer takes the first gun_ item in
his pack, on the belief written above it that this is the gun in his hands, and then sets downRdr.paidRevive=1 whatever it paid. The
death path adds the held gun to the body only when paidRevive is unset (and the pack does not already carry it), so the flag was
written to stop a revive-then-kill paying the same gun twice. The belief does not hold for an elite, ever: mkRaider pushes the gun
he spawned with (pistol, SMG, rifle, carbine or scattergun) into his pack first, and blessElite then puts a Marksman Rifle, Support
MG, Magnum, Whisper, Longshot or Meridian Lance in his hands without touching the pack. The two lists share nothing. So an elite
holding a Marksman Rifle, picked up, said he puts his Scav Pistol (field) in your hands, the flag went on, and when he died later
(he turns on you, or a machine gets him) his body held no Marksman Rifle. The gun you watched him fire was never paid and never
dropped. Elites are on by default (eliteRate 0.08, eliteGuns 1, raiderDown 1). An elite who swapped his blessed gun away and an
imported friend (applyGhost swaps e.wep and leaves the pack) reach the same mismatch.

THE BUILD. One line in the revive payout closure in updatePlayer, under the v9.10 THE BODY MUST NOT PAY IT AGAIN comment:
  if(_rpk==='gun_'+(downRdr.wep&&downRdr.wep.id)) downRdr.paidRevive=1;
The flag goes on only when the gun paid is the gun in his hands. Paid from the pack, or from his hands by the empty-pack fallback:
flag set, so that gun still pays once and a second revive still pays nothing from his hands (v13.88). A different gun paid, or a
non-gun item: no flag, so the death path puts the gun in his hands on his body, and its own indexOf test still stops a duplicate
when the pack carries a copy. A man with no gun in his hands matches nothing. This is the finding's fix as written; the verdict
found it correct and gave no correctedFix. No player text, no number, no dial, no loot table and no seeded draw moved.

OLDER CHECKS. None needed restaging. Check 9.10 revives and kills the first pillager in the seed 4242 raid and fails only if the
gun paid is also on the body; with the fix a different gun in his hands can reach the body, never the one paid. Check 13.88
revives an empty-packed SMG holder twice: the fallback pays the SMG in his hands, which matches, so the flag is set and the second
revive pays nothing, as before. Check 15.07 pays a Medkit and a Frag Charge and never kills the man. Check 11.64 reads only the kill
mark. No older check reads a body after a revive that paid a gun other than the one in his hands.

MEASURED. Check 15.46 deploys a raid at seed 4242. Unopened containers within 90 of the landing spot are marked opened for the check
(so E has nothing else to open) and put back after. Each arm stages one mkRaider pillager (IDENTITIES[0], simBuild on) 24 units from
the player as the only entity: a probe name, off the ledger (ident null, so the revive writes no standing), downed with 30 health,
the named gun in his hands and exactly the named pack. E is pressed for one updatePlayer(0.016) on the play path with the backpack
emptied first; then he is killed down the ordinary death path by nobody (hp 0, finished, byPlayer false, one updateEnts(0.016)),
and the check reads what reached the backpack and the body named for him.
  A (control, then kept): holding the Scav Pistol with a pack of Scav Pistol and scrap. Controls: he is picked up, the revive paid
  one Scav Pistol, he died and left a named body holding his scrap (else SKIP). Kept: the body holds no Scav Pistol, so the gun in
  his hands pays once; a fix that drops the flag would pay it twice. Same on both builds.
  B (the finding): an elite holding the Marksman Rifle with a pack of Scav Pistol and scrap. Controls: picked up, the revive paid
  the Scav Pistol and no Marksman Rifle, he still holds the Marksman Rifle, he died and left a named body with his scrap. Must be one
  Marksman Rifle and no Scav Pistol on the body. v15.45 leaves no Marksman Rifle anywhere, so the check fails there for the
  finding's own reason.
  C (kept): holding the Compact SMG with an empty pack. Controls: picked up, the revive paid one Compact SMG from his hands, he died.
  Any body he left must hold no Compact SMG, on both builds, which guards against a fix that stops flagging the empty-pack payout.
In finally: keys and the mouse cleared, the revive lock and the revive prompt target cleared, the containers put back as they were,
the probe bodies removed, the raid's entities, backpack and revive tallies restored, the player's invulnerability restored, the raid
abandoned, then __topClear, __resetCfg and __cleanProfile.

and f1545, then p1546 and f1546, every anchor a whole line matching once. The patched updatePlayer and the new check entry both

## v15.45 - A ROUND INTO A PILLAGER YOU DOWNED KEEPS YOUR KILL WHEN HE BLEEDS OUT

Bodies audit finding (MEDIUM).

Down a hostile pillager with your gun and he is marked as yours: the player-round hit branch of updateBullets wrote
en.byPlayer=en.hp<=0, the down in updateEnts leaves the mark alone, and when he bleeds out the death path reads it (if(e.byPlayer))
to count the kill in the run report, tick a pillager kill contract, write the grudge into P.rivals and say the grudge line. Both
revives clear the mark (v11.64 for yours, v13.98 for a crewmate's) precisely because it is meant to carry through the down. But that
same line wrote the mark on every round of yours, killing or not, so one more round into him on the floor that left him breathing
(50 down to 40 or so) set it back to false. He crawls for cover (v10.15), or you turn to deal with his crewmate, and he bleeds out:
no kill, no contract progress, no grudge and no grudge line, where holding fire would have kept all four. Frags (only on a lethal
blast), fists, enemy rounds and lightning only ever write the mark on a killing blow; this line was the one writer that cleared it
without a kill. The death path's own comment says the last hit wins, as the flag was set at the killing blow, and a floor round that
does not finish him is not a killing blow.

THE BUILD. One line in updateBullets, the player-round hit branch right after notoAggress(en):
  if(en.hp<=0) en.byPlayer=true; else if(!en.downed) en.byPlayer=false;
A killing round marks him yours exactly as before. A round into a standing man that does not kill him clears the mark as before
(and a standing man never holds the mark with health left, since only the two revives stand a man back up and both clear it). A
round into a downed man that does not finish him now leaves the mark with whoever downed him: yours stays yours, and a man downed by
a machine, a pillager round or lightning stays not yours. A finishing round on the floor still makes him yours (check 13.38). Only
non-hire pillagers are ever downed, so nothing else reaches the new branch. This is the finding's fix as written; the verdict found
it correct and gave no correctedFix. No player text, no number, no dial, no loot table and no seeded draw moved.

OLDER CHECKS. None needed restaging. Checks 9.91 and 10.04 fire non-lethal rounds into a downed pillager but read only his health
and whether he is still there. Check 13.38 fires a finishing round into a downed man whose mark is false and needs it true, the
same on both builds. Checks 11.64 and 13.98 stage the mark by hand around a revive, and check 9.10 sets it by hand before a kill.
No check reads the kill tally or a grudge after a round on the floor.

MEASURED. Check 15.45 deploys a raid at seed 4242 and finds open ground (no wall within 40, well inside the world) 150 to 900 units
from the landing spot. Each arm stages one hostile mkRaider pillager there as the only entity: IDENTITIES[0] with simBuild on, then
a probe name and a probe rival id no identity carries, one health, no armour, empty pack, no roll, facing the round. A round of
yours in the fire path's shape is pushed 8 units short of him and resolved by updateBullets(0.001); his clock is run out with downT
0.01, updateEnts(0.05) and updateEnts(0.016), and the check reads the change in G.tel.kills.raider and in the probe record's kills.
The profile's contracts are set aside for the check so a credited kill pays nothing.
  A (control): your 19 round downs him (downed, 50 health), he bleeds out, he is gone from the raid, one kill and one grudge. Both
  builds; if not, SKIP.
  B (the finding): your 19 round downs him, a 10 round lands on the floor (spent on him, still down, health lower but above 0:
  controls), he bleeds out and is gone (control). Must be one kill and one grudge. v15.44 gives none of either, so the check fails
  there for the finding's own reason.
  C (kept): a lethal round that was not yours downs him (hp 0 and the mark false, what the enemy bullet path writes), your 10 round
  lands on the floor (controls as in B), he bleeds out and is gone. Must be no kill and no grudge, on both builds, which guards
  against a fix that credits you for any round on the floor.
In finally: bullets and entities put back, the probe bodies removed, the kill tally, hits and elite kills restored, the contracts

## v15.44 - A PILLAGER WHO SWITCHES GUNS NEVER LEAVES TWO COPIES OF HIS OLD GUN ON HIS BODY

Bodies audit finding (HIGH).

mkRaider puts a copy of the gun in his hands into his pack (r.bag.push('gun_'+wk)), and the death path counts that copy as the
held gun: v8.44 adds the held gun to the body only when no copy of it is already in the pack. raiderUseKit runs for every pillager
every frame and kitT starts unset, so the swap test runs on his first frame. When it found a better gun in the pack it took the new
gun out (splice) and pushed a fresh copy of the old one, so the old gun now sat in the pack twice. Kill him and the body paid both
copies plus the new gun, which the death path adds because its copy was spliced out. Example: a Scav Pistol pillager whose pack
rolled a Compact SMG (the body and locker tables both hold one) swapped at once and died with two Scav Pistols and the SMG, though
he only ever had one pistol. A gun he looted later did the same. Every pillager who swapped paid out one extra gun.

THE BUILD. The verdict's correctedFix. The two lines in the EQUIP block of raiderUseKit become one:
  if(old&&old.id!=='fists'&&e.bag.indexOf('gun_'+old.id)<0) e.bag.push('gun_'+old.id);
Nothing is spliced out any more. The new gun's copy stays in the pack and stands for the gun in his hands, the same way the spawn
copy does, so the death path pays it once, and a man carrying two of the better gun still pays both. When the old gun already has
its copy (every pillager holding the gun he spawned with) nothing moves at all: the copy stays as the gun he put away and the pack
length is what it always was. When the old gun has no copy (an elite, whose gun blessElite hands him after the spawn copy is
pushed) it is pushed as before, so all his guns pay once; that pack is one longer after the swap than it was, because the new
gun's copy is no longer taken out. No player text, no number, no dial and no loot table moved.

Why not keep the splice for the no-copy case, as the first draft of this build did to hold the pack length: an elite carrying two
of the better gun then kept only one copy for two guns and his body paid one Longshot where he had two, and a pillager who had been
revived for the gun in his hands (the copy gone, v9.10) and later swapped lost the new gun from his body. The correctedFix pays
both. What the one extra pack slot touches: the extraction call skips a pillager carrying 5 or more things (and the rnd draws that
send him to investigate), and drawOp fills the pack on his back by length over 7. A no-copy swap is rare: at spawn it needs an elite
whose pack rolled a gun that outranks his blessed one, and only the safe table carries one, which only a medium or heavy rig rolls,
and that pack already holds 5 or more; later it needs an elite, or a pillager revived for the gun in his hands, looting a better
gun. So a seeded draw can move only in a raid where that happens.

What reads the pack and now reads it right: the hire's extraction cut (10 percent of what his pack is worth) and the roster value
stamped when a pillager extracts counted the old gun twice after a swap and the gun in his hands not at all; they now count each
gun he has once, as they already did for a pillager who never swapped.

OLDER CHECKS. One restaged. Check 15.16 stages a plain pillager holding a Scav Pistol with a pack of only an Auto Rifle (no copy of
the pistol) and its control counts every gun in his hands and pack and wants 2. With the correctedFix the rifle's copy stays in the
pack beside the pistol, so that count reads 3 and the check would SKIP from here on. f1544 restages its guns helper to count each
gun kind once, in his hands or his pack: rifle and pistol, 2 on v15.43 and on v15.44, and the friend half of the check is untouched
(an imported friend skips the swap). Check 9.10 (revive pays out, then kill) reads the first gun in his pack and whether the body
repeats it; a pillager holding his spawn gun takes the nothing-moves path, so it reads the same. Check 9.24 only needs the revive to
pay a gun, and the spawn copy is still first in the pack.

MEASURED. Check 15.44 deploys a raid at seed 4242 and stages five pillagers from mkRaider (IDENTITIES[0], simBuild on, so no
profile record is touched), each with a named body tag, full health, no heal queued, kitT 0 and an exact pack: A holds the Scav
Pistol with [gun_pistol, gun_smg]; B the same with a second SMG; C is an elite holding the Marksman Rifle with [gun_pistol,
gun_sniper]; D holds the pistol with [gun_pistol, scrap]; E is the elite of C with [gun_pistol, gun_sniper, gun_sniper].
raiderUseKit runs once on each. Controls: A and B hold the SMG, C and E the Longshot and D still the pistol. Kept on both builds:
the packs of A, B and D did not change length. Then all five are set dead (hp 0, finished, not by the player), made the only
entities, and one updateEnts(0.016) runs the ordinary death path. Controls: all five left a body named for them, and D's body holds
exactly one Scav Pistol (the ruler: the held gun pays once). The finding: A's body must hold one pistol and one SMG (v15.43 gives
two pistols), B's one pistol and two SMGs (v15.43 gives two pistols and one SMG, the case a fix that only skips the push would also
get wrong), C's one pistol, one Marksman Rifle and one Longshot on both builds, and E's one pistol, one Marksman Rifle and two
Longshots (v15.43 gives one Longshot, as would a fix that keeps the splice). So the check fails on v15.43 for the finding's own
reason. The staged bodies are removed, the raid's entities put back, and the raid is abandoned.

Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html (at 15.39) and mkfixture.ps1: p1540 to p1550 and f1540 to f1550 applied in order,
every anchor a whole line block matching once, the 15.16 restage included. The patched raiderUseKit, the new check entry and the
restaged 15.16 helper parse under JScript. A JScript model of the swap with the v8.44 death rule gave, with the correctedFix: A
pistol + SMG, B pistol + SMG x2, C pistol + dmr + sniper (pack 2 to 3), D pistol, E pistol + dmr + sniper x2 (pack 3 to 4); with
the old swap A and B pistol x2 + SMG and E one sniper; with the first draft's guarded splice E one sniper as well. The 15.16 plain
pillager counts 2 gun kinds on both builds, and 3 by the old every-copy count with the correctedFix.

## v15.43 - THE RAID CLOCK READS 0:10 WHEN TEN SECONDS IS SAID, AND 0:00 ONLY WHEN IT IS OUT

HUD audit finding (LOW).

Let the raid clock run down. The clock at the top of the HUD rounded its seconds down (Math.floor of G.timeLeft), while the
v15.24 warnings in tickClockWarn fire on the frame the clock crosses a mark (prev above it, now at or below it). So on the frame
that says TEN SECONDS and plays the first tick the clock is at something like 9.98 and the figure read 0:09. THIRTY SECONDS came
with 0:29 on screen and 1 minute left with 0:59. The last tick played as the figure turned 0:00, and then a whole second passed at
0:00 before the site began to burn, because the burn waits for G.timeLeft<=0. Once it burns, the loop keeps taking the frame time
off the clock, and the floor of a negative figure drew -1:0-1, then -1:0-2 and -1:0-3, for the rest of the burn (read from the
code: mm and ss both floor to negative numbers and the zero pad is added in front of the minus sign). Every other countdown on
screen already rounds up: extractNowLine, INBOUND Ns and the closes in line on the map. An extraction window clamped to the clock
(z.hold=G.timeLeft=2.4) therefore read EXTRACT NOW! 3S LEFT beside a raid clock of 0:02.

THE BUILD. Three lines in drawHUD, the clock block. The countdown figure is now Math.ceil(Math.max(0,G.timeLeft)), so it turns to
0:10 on the same frame TEN SECONDS is said, to 0:30, 1:00 and 0:01 on the frames of their warnings, reads 0:01 through the last
live second, and reads 0:00 only once the clock is out, including through the burn. The red colour now tests the figure shown
(_tSrc<45) instead of the raw clock; testing the raw clock would have turned it red while the rounded figure still read 0:45, so
red still starts at 0:44 exactly as before. This is the verdict's corrected fix; the proposed one-line fix missed the colour. The
count up on a raid built with no clock is untouched (the other arm of the same line), and so are tickClockWarn, every warning
line, every sound, the burn and every number. No player text, no dial and no seeded draw moved.

MEASURED. Check 15.43 deploys a raid at seed 4242 with the default dials (it skips unless raidClockOn is true and the raid length is
above 0), wraps the HUD canvas fillText to record each string with its fillStyle and textAlign, and takes the clock as the centred
string shaped like a clock (a minus sign allowed, so the old burn figure is still found). say and blip are replaced by recorders.
Controls on both builds: exactly 10 seconds draws 0:10, exactly 45 draws 0:45 in the plain colour and exactly 44 draws 0:44 in red.
THE FIX: for each of one minute, thirty seconds, ten seconds and the last second it calls tickClockWarn across the mark (60.02 to
59.98, 30.02 to 29.98, 10.02 to 9.98, 1.02 to 0.98). Control on both builds: that call says 1 minute left., THIRTY SECONDS. and TEN
SECONDS. and plays clockwarn, clockwarn, clocktick and clocktick, so the warnings still fire at the same moments. It then draws the
clock at both sides of the frame and requires 1:01 to 1:00, 0:31 to 0:30, 0:11 to 0:10 and 0:02 to 0:01. On v15.42 these read
1:00 to 0:59, 0:30 to 0:29, 0:10 to 0:09 and 0:01 to 0:00, so the check fails there for the finding's own reason. THE FIX: 0.02
seconds left draws 0:01 (0:00 on v15.42), and 44.5 seconds draws 0:45 in the plain colour (0:44 in red on v15.42; a fix that
rounded up but kept the raw colour test would draw 0:45 in red and fail too). Control on both builds: exactly 0 draws 0:00. THE
FIX: the clock run on to -0.4, as the burn leaves it, draws 0:00 (-1:0-1 on v15.42). Last, on both builds: with the raid length set
to 0 the clock is off, and 65.7 seconds up draws 1:05 in the plain colour. The fillText wrapper, say, blip, the raid length, G.t,
G.timeLeft and G.warnPrev are put back, and the raid is abandoned. No older fixture check reads the clock figure or its colour
(check 9.56 only finds where the clock is drawn, and its figure still matches a whole-seconds clock), so none is restaged.

Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html (at 15.39) and mkfixture.ps1: p1540 and f1540, p1541 and f1541, p1542 and f1542
applied in order, then p1543 made 2 edits (the clock block and VER) plus DEVNOW and f1543 1 edit, every anchor a whole line
matching once, and a second p1543 run refuses. The check and the edited drawHUD parse in JScript. The old and new clock lines and
the real tickClockWarn replayed in JScript give exactly the figures above: the four crossings say and play the same on both, the
old figures run one second behind at every mark, 44.5 reads 0:44 red against 0:45 plain, -0.4 and -2.5 read -1:0-1 and -1:0-3
against 0:00, and the count up reads 1:05 on both.

Not verified: a real raid by hand, watching the clock run out. The check itself has not been run in a browser yet.
## v15.42 - CROUCHED BESIDE YOUR HIRE OR A DOWNED PILLAGER, THE READOUT SAYS HIDDEN

HUD audit finding (MEDIUM).

Hire a pillager. He starts on FOLLOW, and under FOLLOW he walks back toward you whenever he is more than 120 away
(if(dF>120) navSeek), so he spends the raid inside the 170 units of the crouch rule. Crouch somewhere quiet with every hostile far
off. The concealment plate in drawHUD finds the nearest body and says PARTLY HIDDEN, TOO CLOSE in amber when it is within
crouchHide (170), else HIDDEN, CROUCHED in green. Its loop skipped only dead bodies, the Peddler and a survivor, so the hire counted
as someone too close, and the plate named a danger that does not exist while the hard crouch rule in updateEnts (sees=false past
CHID) was hiding him from every machine and pillager. A hire cannot give him away: the branch in updateEnts that acts on a body
seeing him opens with if(sees&&!(e.merc&&!e.downed&&(...||true))), so a hire never enters it, and a hire is never downed (the
downing needs !e.merc). A pillager lying downed near him did the same, although the
downed branch in updateEnts continues before any sight test, so he sees nothing. The one readout that exists to teach crouch told
him his strongest stealth state was not working. It is not always, since a hire on FOLLOW can wander to a crate or go fight, but
it is the normal state of a crouch with a hire along.

THE BUILD. One line in drawHUD, the concealment loop: it also skips a body with merc, downed or finished set. finished bodies are
cleared on the next frame through the hp<=0 path, so skipping them only spares the last frame. With the hire following and nothing
hostile inside 170 the plate reads HIDDEN, CROUCHED; a standing pillager or machine inside 170 still reads PARTLY HIDDEN, TOO CLOSE,
with or without the hire beside him. The crouch rule, the 170 dial, every word on the plate, every colour and every number are
unchanged. No player text, no dial and no seeded draw moved.

MEASURED. Check 15.42 deploys a raid at seed 4242 with the default dials (it skips unless crouchHide is between 100 and 400), shuts
the backpack and map, lifts every ent, builds a standing hostile pillager and a hire with mkRaider the way buildRaid builds one
(merc 1, hostile false, grudge false, friendly 1), and wraps the HUD canvas fillText to record every string one drawHUD hands it,
compared whole (both needles assembled, the too close one from pieces). Before each draw only the named bodies are in G.ents, each
put east of him, with G.pCrouch true and G.pBush false. Controls: with nobody near the plate reads HIDDEN, CROUCHED; with the
standing pillager 60 away it reads the too close warning; with the hire 400 away it reads HIDDEN, CROUCHED. THE FIX: with the hire
60 away the plate must read HIDDEN, CROUCHED and not the warning; on v15.41 it reads the warning, so the check fails there for the
finding's own reason. THE FIX: the same pillager staged downed (downed 1, state down, the bleed clock and raiderDownHp, the fields
the real downing sets) 60 away must read HIDDEN, CROUCHED; on v15.41 it reads the warning. Last control, on both builds: the hire at
60 with the standing pillager at 100 still reads the warning, so the hire never hides a real one. The fillText wrapper, G.ents, the
crouch and bush flags, the backpack and map flags and the pillager's staged fields are put back, and the raid is abandoned. No older
fixture check reads the concealment plate, so none is restaged.

Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html (at 15.39) and mkfixture.ps1: p1540 and f1540, p1541 and f1541 applied in order,
then p1542 made 2 edits (the loop line and VER) plus DEVNOW and f1542 1 edit, every anchor a whole line matching once, and a second
p1542 run refuses. The check and the edited drawHUD parse in JScript. The old and new loop lines replayed in JScript give: nobody,
hidden on both; standing pillager at 60, too close on both; hire at 400, hidden on both; hire at 60 and downed pillager at 60, too
close on the old line and hidden on the new; hire at 60 with a standing pillager at 100, too close on both.
