## v15.41 - WITH BARE HANDS UP THE RETICLE NEVER SAYS EMPTY - R OR NO AMMO

HUD audit finding (MEDIUM).

Deploy carrying one gun. The second gun slot starts as Bare Hands, which have a magazine of 0 (buildRaid gives sec=WEAPONS.fists
and secAmmo=0). Press 2: setHot calls swapGuns, so Bare Hands come up with nothing loaded while p.reserve still holds the gun's
rounds. The reticle state in drawHUD read only the rounds loaded, so it went to the amber struck-through cross with EMPTY - R under
it, and to the red NO AMMO once the reserve was gone. At the same moment the corner readout said MELEE (it checks the magazine size
first) and the punch worked. Pressing R did nothing, because the reload in updatePlayer needs fewer rounds loaded than the magazine
holds, and 0 is not below 0. Putting the only gun into the backpack ends the same way, since bagHeldGun leaves Bare Hands in hand
with 0 loaded. The cursor told him his hands were out of ammo and to press a key that does nothing.

THE BUILD. One line in drawHUD, the reticle state: a weapon with no magazine (p.wep.mag===0) is never empty or dry. With Bare Hands
up the reticle is the plain cross, and the round count ring already skipped a zero magazine. JAMMED still shows if a jam timer
carries over the swap, which is true, because the punch also waits for the jam to clear. The reload ring and every gun's warnings
are unchanged. No player text, no number, no dial and no seeded draw moved.

MEASURED. Check 15.41 deploys a raid at seed 4242 with the default dials, puts the mouse mid-screen with the backpack and map shut,
and wraps the HUD canvas fillText to record every string one drawHUD hands it (before any text edit, compared whole). If the raid did
not start with one gun and Bare Hands, it hands him a pistol with Bare Hands in slot 2. The reserve is set to 37. Controls: key 1 is
the gun in his hands and key 2 is Bare Hands, a real gun cell and not the vacant one. With the gun and nothing loaded the drawn HUD
carries EMPTY - R, and with the reserve at 0 it carries NO AMMO (both needles are assembled, never written whole). Then setHot(1),
the way key 2 takes it. Controls: Bare Hands are up with 0 loaded, 37 in reserve, no reload, no jam and key 2 lit; one updatePlayer
frame with R held starts no reload. THE FIX: the drawn HUD must not carry EMPTY - R; on v15.40 it does, so the check fails there for
the finding's own reason. Control: the corner reads MELEE in that frame. With the reserve at 0 the drawn HUD must not carry NO AMMO
(on v15.40 it does). Last control, on both builds: setHot(0) brings the gun back, and with 0 loaded it still draws EMPTY - R, and
NO AMMO with no reserve, so the fix did not silence the gun. The fillText wrapper, the keys, the mouse, key 1 and every weapon and
ammo field it moved are put back, and the raid is abandoned. No older fixture check reads the reticle text, so none is restaged.
Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html (at 15.39) and mkfixture.ps1: p1540 and f1540 applied, then p1541 made 2 edits
(the reticle line and VER) plus DEVNOW and f1541 1 edit, every anchor a whole line matching once, and a second p1541 run refuses.
The check and the edited drawHUD parse in JScript. The new reticle line replayed in JScript gives no warning for Bare Hands with 37
in reserve or none, empty and dry for a gun with a 12 round magazine, and still JAMMED for Bare Hands with a jam timer.

Not verified: a real raid by hand, pressing 2 with one gun carried and putting the only gun in the backpack (the backpack path
shares the fixed line but the check drives only key 2). The check itself has not been run in a browser yet.
## v15.40 - THE INCOMING HEAL SHOWS ONLY THE HEALTH THAT WILL ARRIVE

HUD audit finding (HIGH).

Get down to 80 health with no Medkit running and put on a Bandage. When it lands, the green incoming heal block on the health bar
ran from 80 to 100, the ring over his head read 7s and the line said Bandage is healing you, 6 sec. What really happens: tickHeal
stops him at 85 about a second and a half later, clears the queue, and the block, the ring and the seconds all vanish with 15 of the
promised points never arriving. His ruling of 2026-09-16 is that bandages only get him to 85 and only a Medkit gets him back to 100,
and the screen was promising the opposite. It happened with every Bandage used between 65 and 85. It also happened with a Bandage
over a nearly spent Medkit: from 74.6 with 1.4 of the Medkit left, the block reached 96 while the heal stops at 86.4. All three read
the queue, which is everything poured in and knows nothing of the ceilings the drain obeys. The AUDIT.md row for v15.26 logged the
block as OPEN; the ring and the line had the same fault and were not on that row.

THE BUILD. Four places, all reading healReach, the one reader of where a running heal really stops that the drain and every refusal
already use since v15.26.
- drawHUD: the green block ends at healReach instead of health plus the queue.
- render2D, the call that draws him: what is left and the seconds over his head are healReach less his health, over the rate.
- tickPrepSlot: the seconds in the Bandage is healing you line are the same. The sentence itself is unchanged.
- applyHeal: healAmt0, which only the ring reads as its total, now stores healReach less his health after the item is queued,
  instead of everything poured in. Without this the ring would start three quarters full for a Bandage at 80 (5 left of 20).
No number, dial, ceiling, rate or loot table moved; the queue and the drain are untouched. No player text changed except the seconds
the existing line reports.

MEASURED. Check 15.40 deploys a raid at seed 4242 with the default dials and lands Bandages through tickPrepSlot, the path F and the
belt use. It wraps the HUD canvas fillRect to read the width of the green block (fill rgba 111,224,160), the world canvas fillText
to read the seconds over his head (fill #dff3e8, used only there) and the world canvas arc to read how full the heal ring is (radius
9, from the top, #7fc4a0 at width 3). Controls: full health 100, Bandage ceiling 85, Medkit ceiling 100. From 50 on both builds: the
block is 72 of 360, the line says 6 sec, 7s is drawn over his head, the ring is empty and the heal ends at 70. THE FIX from 80: the
queue is 20 and healReach 85 on both builds (control); the block must be 18 wide (72 on v15.39), the line must say 2 sec (6 sec on
v15.39), the seconds over his head must read 2s (7s on v15.39); after 20 ticks of 0.05 he is at 83.2 and the ring must be 64 percent
full (16 percent on v15.39); the heal must end at 85 (control). A Bandage over the last 1.5 of a Medkit from 30: the block must end
at healReach, 86.4, where the heal ends (control), not at 96 as on v15.39. Heal ceilings off from 80: the block is 72 and the heal
ends at 100 on both builds. Everything it wraps and every heal field it moved is put back, the dials reset and the raid abandoned.
No older fixture check reads the green block, the ring, the seconds or healAmt0, so none is restaged.
Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html and mkfixture.ps1 as they stand with p1539 and f1539 applied: p1540 made 5 edits plus
DEVNOW and f1540 1 edit, every anchor a whole line matching once, and a second p1540 run refuses. The check and the edited applyHeal,
tickPrepSlot, drawHUD and render2D parse in JScript. The heal math was replayed in JScript with the real applyHeal, tickPrepSlot,
tickHeal and healReach of both builds and the drawn block and ring formulas: v15.39 gives block 72, 6 sec, 7s, fill 0.16 and medkit
block 77.2; v15.40 gives 18, 2 sec, 2s, fill 0.64 and 42.7, equal to what the check wants, with every control the same on both.

Not verified: a real raid by hand with a Bandage at 80. The check itself has not been run in a browser yet.

## v15.37 - A CRATE ON THE FAR SIDE OF A WALL NEVER BLOCKS THE STALL

Peddler audit finding 9 (MEDIUM).

Stand beside the Peddler (within 74 units) with a thin wall or a stall slab next to you, and on its far side, within 46 units of
you, an unopened crate, cache or pillager body. Bodies from a fight near the stall and the loot at his landmark both make this
likely. The plate over him read THE PEDDLER (search the crate first), and E did nothing at all. Since the v8.x fix for his note "i
cant search a casher right next to the peddler", a crate within 46 units takes E from the stall, on the reasoning that the rule
clears itself: search the crate, it is marked opened, and the next E opens the stall. But that stall test was distance and nothing
else, while the search has also needed a clear line to the box since v4.06 ("i just looted through a wall"). Behind a wall the
stall test said a crate was underfoot and the search could not see it, so the stall refused, no search started, and the prompt
pointed at a box that cannot be opened from where he stands. The two tests stopped agreeing when the search got its sight test.

THE BUILD. One line in updatePlayer, the crate-underfoot scan before the stall opens. It now asks the search's own question: the
same 46 units and the same losClear on G.vseg. Only a crate, cache or body the search can reach from where he stands keeps E from
the stall; one on his side of the wall still wins E, as the v8.x rule intends. The plate reads G.pedBlocked, so it stops asking for
a crate he cannot search. The sight test only runs for a box already inside 46 units, so the cost is nothing. No player text, no
number, no dial and no seeded draw moved; the sentence on the plate is unchanged.

## v15.36 - SELLING FOUND BANDAGES NEVER TURNS ISSUED BANDAGES INTO FOUND ONES

Peddler audit finding 8 (MEDIUM).

Go up with no heal packed and the raid issues two Bandages, a loaner that is never banked (v13.54). Loot two or more Bandages,
open the Peddler's stall and press 1 (or A on the pad). Since v13.71 SELL BACKPACK keeps the issued pair and buys only the found
ones, which is right. But the issued count is also kept honest by a frame tick, trackIssuedBandages, which compares the Bandages
in the backpack with the number it saw last frame and, by the v13.67 rule, treats every fall as issued Bandages spent first. The
sale left that last-seen number alone, so on the very next frame (tickHeal runs it even with the stall open) the tick saw the
count fall by the number sold and took that many off the issued count. The two loaners the stall had just refused to buy now
counted as found: the panel read SELL BACKPACK (2) with a price, a second press sold them (the free money v13.71 took away), and
an extraction handed none back and banked them into the stash, against v13.54. dropItem already avoids this for a drop by moving
the last-seen number with it (v13.90); the sale did not.

THE BUILD. One function, pedSellAll, three lines. It counts the found Bandages the sale takes and, when it replaces the backpack,
lowers the last-seen number by that count, exactly as dropItem does. The next frame then reads no fall and the issued count stays
where it was. A use or a drop after the sale is still a fall and still spends an issued Bandage first. A Bandage picked up since
the last frame and sold in the same frame leaves the last-seen number below the real count, which the tick reads as a rise and
ignores, so it stays correct. The bot sells through the same function under the sim and gets the same honest count. No price, no
dial, no loot table and no player text moved; no seeded draw added.

MEASURED. Check 15.36 deploys a raid with nothing packed (control: two Bandages, both issued), leaves only a Peddler 40 units
away and opens the stall with a real E frame (control: open). Every step after that is a real updatePlayer frame and key 1 goes
through raidKey, as the keyboard sends it. Control: three plain finds sold at the stall leave both Bandages issued on the next
frame, on either build. Then three found Bandages go in (control: the frame reads five and still two issued) and key 1 is pressed
(control: two Bandages kept, three paid for). The frame after must still count two issued; on v15.35 it counts none. A second
press must sell nothing; on v15.35 it sells both loaners. Guard: a Bandage used after the sale spends one issued. Last, a plain
find goes in and the raid is extracted: the find must be banked (control) and no Bandage; on v15.35 the issued one left is banked.
So the check fails on v15.35 for the finding's own reason. The profile is restored through the loader afterwards. Dry run on
scratch copies of dark_raiders.html (at 15.27) and mkfixture.ps1, with p1528 to p1535 and f1528 to f1535 applied in order
first: every anchor a whole line matching once, the edited pedSellAll and the check both parse in JScript, and a JScript run of the
old and new sale with the real tick through the check's steps gave issued 0, a second sale of 2 and 1 Bandage banked on v15.35,
and issued 2, nothing sold, issued 1 after the use and 0 banked on the build.

Not verified: a real raid by hand, selling found Bandages beside the issued pair and extracting. The check itself has not been
run in a browser yet. Left alone: the v13.67 comment above trackIssuedBandages still lists a sale to the peddler among the falls
it counts; the new comment in pedSellAll says why a sale no longer reads as one.
## v15.35 - A MOUSE CLICK ON THE OPEN STALL NEVER FIRES THE GUN BEHIND IT

Peddler audit finding 7 (HIGH).

Walk up to the Peddler, press E, and his stall panel opens in the middle of the screen, over you and him. Its rows answer the
number keys and pad A; the panel is only drawn and takes no mouse input. The canvas mousedown handler already keeps a left click
away from the trigger when it lands on the map, a backpack tile, the open backpack, a belt cell or a HUD panel (the v3.64 rule,
a click on furniture does not pull the trigger), but nothing asked whether the stall was open. So a click on the panel set the
fire flag, and updatePlayer runs its fire and cook code before the stall's own early return. The gun fired toward the cursor
through the panel: a round spent and noise made, a Frag Charge cooked if its cell was selected, and with the cursor on his side
the round hit the Peddler, who bolts ("No trade while he is bleeding") and the stall shuts. Held on an automatic it could kill
him, a permanent point of Notoriety. Holding the trigger while pressing E did the same for the whole trade. The F strike
(meleeStrike checks G.trade) and pad A (v14.20, padRelease) were already blocked; only the mouse got through.

THE BUILD. Two lines, no numbers and no player text moved.
- The mousedown handler returns on a left click while the stall is open, right after the map block and before the right click
  line. The map still comes first, a right click still only aims and cannot fire, and a click on a belt cell no longer changes
  the selection behind the panel, which is what the pad already did. The canvas click listener still wakes the audio.
- Opening the stall lets go of the trigger (mouse.down=false), the way padRelease lets go of pad A. The next frame ends the
  hold, and a grenade being cooked is thrown, as on the pad since v14.20, rather than left to cook off in his hand.

MEASURED. Check 15.35 deploys a raid, leaves only a Peddler 40 units away, puts a fresh Scav Pistol in his hands with the
highlight on its cell, and picks a click point on the left half of the stall panel that no HUD panel or belt cell claims. It
drives the real mousedown and mouseup events and real updatePlayer frames, and takes every round fired out of the air before
it can move. Control: with the stall shut the click spends one round. The stall is opened with E the way he opens it (control:
it is open). A left click on the open stall must spend no round and leave it open; on v15.34 it spends one. Then, stall shut,
a Compact SMG trigger held and E pressed: the round on the opening frame is the control, and three more frames with the stall
open must spend nothing; on v15.34 they spend three. So the check fails on v15.34 for the finding's own reason. It puts the
mouse position back afterwards. Dry run on scratch copies of dark_raiders.html (at 15.27) and mkfixture.ps1: p1528 to p1534 and
f1528 to f1534 applied in order, then p1535 and f1535, every anchor a whole line matching once; the check and the edited
mousedown handler both parse in JScript.

Not verified: a real raid by hand, clicking the stall rows and holding the trigger into the stall. The check itself has not
been run in a browser yet.
## v15.34 - STANDING IN ANY LANDED EXTRACTION POINT SHOWS THE EXTRACT PROMPT

Extraction audit finding. Two extraction points can be called at once, and the window at a landed point is shared, so leaving on
whichever lands first is intended play. Calling a point moves the pointer (G.active) to it (v12.57), and standing in a point does
not move the pointer back while the point it names still has a live call. So with point A called and still inbound, then point B
called, the pointer sits on B. When A lands first and he stands in it:
- tryExtractTick finds him in A, whose window is running, and returns from the hold branch before any pointer change.
- the mirror in tickExtractPoints keeps G.active on B because B still has a call, and sets G.beaconT to B's inbound clock and
  G.shipHold to null.
- the centre verb in drawHUD read those mirrors: _shipDown (G.beaconT<=0 and G.shipHold set) was false and _inRing measured B, so
  the prompt to hold E and extract was never drawn.
A hold of E there still extracted him at A, so the key did something the screen never offered. The downed screen has read the
point he lies in since v12.94 (standingRing), and the uncalled-point prompt since v14.13; the standing verb was the one reader
left on the pointer.

THE BUILD. The two tests read the point he stands in: _sr=standingRing(), _shipDown=ringLanded(_sr), _inRing=!!_sr and his
distance to _sr under its radius. standingRing returns the open point he is inside and falls back to the pointer when he is in
none, so a single call, and standing outside every point, read exactly as before. ringLanded needs beaconT at or under 0 and a
window above 0, which matches the old test, including the 0.01 window a hold in progress keeps. A called point cannot close
mid-window, so A is still found. The outer guard (G.beaconT not null) still passes, because B's call keeps the mirror set. The
verb text is untouched, still 'HOLD '+keyLabel('KeyE','E')+' TO EXTRACT' from v15.32; no player text changes, nothing is a
TXSHIP key, and no balance number, dial, loot table or sound moves.

Left alone, outside this finding: the bottom strip (EXTRACT B INCOMING with its arrow and metres, var inRing=dist(p,G.active)) and
the compass still follow the pointer, so in this state they still name and point at the inbound point.

MEASURED. Check 15.34 deploys a raid, clears the machines, turns pillager waves off for the check (restored), picks two points
that do not overlap, and stages them: every point quiet, A landed (beaconT -1, a 20 s window), B inbound at 12 s or quiet, the
pointer set, him standing in the middle of one, then one tryExtractTick(0,false) down the real path. It records every string
drawHUD paints through txRecord. Controls: with one landed call at A and him in it, the pointer and mirrors reach A (window 20)
and the prompt is drawn, on either build; with B called after A, the tick leaves the pointer on B with its clock above 0 and no
window, A still landed, and standingRing on A. The finding: standing in A there, the prompt must be drawn; v15.33 draws none, so
the check fails there. Kept: standing in inbound B with A landed elsewhere draws no prompt. The needle is assembled from words
with keyLabel, so the check never matches its own source. Zones, the pointer and mirrors, the message and its queue, the
machines, his position, the wave dial and the text recorder are put back in finally before the raid is abandoned.

TWO OLDER CHECKS STAGED THE MIRRORS ALONE. Check 9.08 (its standing control, "the standing prompt is not drawing at all") and
check 10.79 (the standing extract prompt pulse, judged against its floor) stand him in the ring after a few frames and then set
only G.shipHold=8 and G.beaconT=0, with the point itself never called. The old verb read those mirrors and drew; this build reads
the point he stands in, which has not landed, so both would have gone red on v15.34 for a state the game cannot be in (the
mirrors are copied off the pointed point every tick). f1534 also lands the point in both (beaconT 0, hold 8, holdMax 30) beside
the same mirror lines, the way v12.94 restaged the surrender check on the ring. The old verb still reads the mirrors, so both pass
on v15.33 as before; the ring badge is skipped for the point he stands in, so the measured box should read the same on v15.34.
Neither restaged check has been run in a browser.

Dry run on scratch copies of the page and the fixture (1527 is already applied to both): p1528 to p1537 and f1528 to f1537
applied in version order, every anchor a whole line matching once, the version and DEVNOW moved to 15.34 and on to 15.37;
pollPad, drawHUD, tickExtractPoints and tryExtractTick from the patched page, the new check and the two restaged checks parsed
under JScript.

Not verified: check 15.34 has not been run in a browser, and no real raid has stood in a landed point while a second call was
inbound.
## v15.33 - A MISSED EXTRACTION OFFERS ANOTHER CALL ONLY WHEN ONE CAN ARRIVE

Extraction audit finding. When a landed extraction window runs out with him within 1400 units, tickExtractPoints clanks and says
"Extraction left without you. Hold E to call for another, 0:25 out." It said that on every missed window, and in two cases the
call it offers cannot work:
- THE CLOCK. The window is clamped to the raid clock (z.hold is at most timeLeft-1), so a call made with 0:50 left lands at 0:25
  with a 24 s window that ends with 0:01 on the clock. A new call takes extractWait (25 s by default), and the frame loop ends the
  raid on the timer long before it could arrive. The call line already knows this case and warns that the raid clock runs out
  first. Every missed window that ends with less than extractWait on the clock hit this, which is any call made with under about
  80 s left.
- THE CLOSING. A point past its closing time stays open only while it is called. The missed-window branch clears the call, so the
  close loop later in the same tickExtractPoints shuts the point in that same tick and queues "Extraction A is closed." behind the
  wrong line. Holding E there only gets "This point is CLOSED."
Neither sentence is a key in the TXSHIP table.

THE BUILD. The line keeps its first sentence, "Extraction left without you.", and then:
- past the point's closing time (closeAt set and timeLeft at or under it), nothing more, so the queued closed line that follows is
  the news and he does not read it twice;
- with the raid clock on and less than extractWait left, " Another call cannot beat the raid clock.";
- otherwise the old " Hold E to call for another, 0:25 out." exactly as before.
closeAt is undefined with the clock off (buildRaid), so a raid with no clock always gets the old line. The clank, the counters and
the clearing of the window are untouched. No balance number, dial, loot table or sound moves.

Left alone, outside this finding: "Hold E" in this line still names E on a controller (listed open at v15.32).

MEASURED. Check 15.33 deploys a raid, clears the machines, records say, sayWhenFree and blip, and stages one point at a time: every
point quiet, this one landed (beaconT -1) with 0.01 s of window left, him 300 units off its middle, the raid clock set, and one
tickExtractPoints(0.05). Controls: the raid clock is on; at 200 s on a point with no closing time the window ends (window cleared,
clank, the point still open) and the missed extraction line is said, on either build; past a closing time the point is shut in the
same tick and its closed line queued. Kept: at 200 s the line still offers another call. The finding: with half an extraction wait
on the clock (12 s) the line must not offer a call and must name the raid clock; 5 s past another point's closing time it must
offer no call and not blame the clock. v15.32 offers the call in both, so the check fails there. The needles are assembled from
words, so the check never matches its own source. Everything staged (zones, the pointer and mirrors, the clock, the message and
its queue, the machines, his position, the missed-window counter) is put back in finally before the raid is abandoned.

Dry run on scratch copies of the page and the fixture (1527 is already applied to both): p1528 to p1533 and f1528 to f1533 applied
in order, every anchor a whole line matching once, the version and DEVNOW moved to 15.33, and the patched block and the new check
parsed under JScript.

Not verified: check 15.33 has not been run in a browser, and no real raid has missed a window with the clock short or at a closing
point.
## v15.32 - ON A CONTROLLER THE EXTRACT PROMPT NAMES THE X BUTTON

Extraction audit finding. On a controller the X button holds E in a raid (PADHOLD 2, and pollPad holds E whenever no search is
starting), and keyLabel turns KeyE into X while a pad is connected. Every call prompt already asks keyLabel: HOLD X TO CALL FOR
EXTRACTION standing and down, and the ring badge reads [X] EXTRACT. Two extraction lines did not, and said E on every input:
- the centre banner in drawHUD, drawn standing in a landed ring. The ring badge is skipped for the ring he stands in (v6.57), so
  this was the only verb on screen, and on a pad it named a key the pad does not have, for the same button he had just called
  with.
- the downedVerb line, drawn at the huge size down in a landed ring with automatic pickup off (hauledAboard 0, the shipped
  default). The ring badge is not drawn while he is down, so nothing on screen named X there either.
Neither line is a key in the TXSHIP table, and nothing rewrites it.

THE BUILD. Both lines build the verb as 'HOLD '+keyLabel('KeyE','E')+' TO EXTRACT', the same helper and the same fallback the
call prompts use. On the keyboard keyLabel returns E, so the keyboard text is exactly what it was, and the existing checks that

the missed window ("Hold E to extract", "Hold E to call for another") still name E on a pad.

MEASURED. Check 15.32 deploys a raid, fakes a connected pad with every button up through navigator.getGamepads and one pollPad,
stages the ring (every ring quiet, this one landed with beaconT -1 and a 20 s window, or uncalled), puts him in the middle of it,
runs tickExtractPoints(0) so the HUD mirrors come from the ring, and records every string drawHUD passes to ctx.fillText.
Controls: the pad turns padOn on and labels KeyE as X; standing in an uncalled ring the HUD draws HOLD X TO CALL FOR EXTRACTION,
and down in one the downed screen does too, on either build; the landed ring reaches G.beaconT and G.shipHold. The finding:
standing in the landed ring, and down in it, the HUD must draw HOLD X TO EXTRACT and never the E line; v15.31 draws the E line in
both, so the check fails there. The keyboard: with the pad let go, the same landed ring still draws the E line standing and down.

## v15.31 - A HELD X ON A CONTROLLER SEARCHES ONE BOX, THEN CALLS OR EXTRACTS

Extraction audit finding. On a controller, X in an extraction point searches first (v13.48) and, with no search started 0.35 s
into the press, holds E for the call or the extraction (v13.51). A search that has started in the hold keeps X "until the box is
done", through a latch, PAD.xSearched. That latch was only cleared by letting go of X. So when the box was done the same hold went
on to search the next box in reach, then the next, and only held E when nothing was left: fight a siege from inside the ring, two
crawlers die at his feet, hold X when EXTRACT NOW shows, and he searches both wrecks (about a second each) before the 1.4 s hold
even starts. With the window nearly shut, or the raid clock at zero, he searches instead of leaving. The 1.6 s call in an uncalled
ring waited the same way. A second path: a backpack that filled part way through a hold refused the next search, and the latch
kept X on that refusal for as long as the button was held, so he could not call at all. The keyboard was never affected, because
E and X are separate keys there.

THE BUILD. One line in pollPad. While X is held and no search is running, a latch that was set means a search in this hold has
ended, so the latch is spent and the 0.35 s grace with it (PAD.xDownAt goes far into the past), and the same hold turns to E: the
call or the extraction hold starts, the way the keyboard E would. The press frame is unchanged, since the latch is not set yet,
so X still searches the box in reach first. The full backpack grace from v13.51 is unchanged, since that path never sets the
latch. Letting go still resets both, so a fresh press searches the next box first, as v13.51 intends. No balance number, dial,
loot table or player text moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.31 deploys a raid, fakes a pad through navigator.getGamepads, lands the ring (beaconT -1, a 20 s window,
G.active on it), clears the map of machines and boxes, and steps pollPad and updatePlayer at 60 frames a second. Control: one
Scrap Metal wreck (0.6 s search) at his feet; X held opens it, and half a second later the extraction hold is running (above
0.3 s of 1.4), on either build. Control: a second wreck 30 units off is found in reach on its own. The finding: both wrecks, X
held; the nearer opens, and half a second later the second wreck must be untouched and the extraction hold running. On v15.30 the
second wreck is half searched and the hold has not started, so the check fails there. Kept from v13.51: let go and pressed again,
X searches the second wreck. Dry run on scratch copies of the page and the fixture (1527 already in both): p1528 to p1537 and
f1528 to f1537 applied in version order, every anchor a whole line matching once, and the patched pollPad and the new check both
compiled under JScript. The existing pad checks 13.48 and 13.51 hold X for a few frames over one box or a refused one, so the
latch never ends a search inside their holds and they read as before. A JScript model of the latch and the search with the check's own sequence gave, on
the old code, the second wreck at 0.50 of its search with no hold, and on the new code the second wreck untouched with the hold
at 0.50 s; both controls passed on both.

Not verified: check 15.31 has not been run in a browser, and no real controller has held X over two wrecks in a live ring.
## v15.30 - AN AUTOMATIC GUN THAT RUNS DRY ON A HELD TRIGGER CLICKS ONCE

Sound audit finding (LOW). Since v10.56 an empty gun plays one dull dry click and says "Out of ammo." when the trigger is
pulled with nothing left in the backpack. In updatePlayer the empty-magazine branch lets a pull in with
if(!p.fired||p.wep.auto), so automatics get in on every rate-of-fire tick, but the click itself was gated on !p.fired. An
automatic sets p.fired on every round it fires and only letting go of the trigger clears it. So holding the trigger of the
Sputter, the Chatter, the Compact SMG or any other automatic through its last rounds with no ammo in the backpack just stopped
the gun: no click, no line, only the NO AMMO text by the crosshair. A single shot gun was never affected, because it needs a
fresh pull, and an automatic with spare ammo reloads on the held trigger. Only the empty automatic was silent.

THE BUILD. The click keeps its own flag now, p.dryTold. The empty branch plays the click and the line when the flag is off and
sets it; letting go of the trigger clears it, next to p.fired. So an automatic run dry on a held trigger clicks and says Out of
ammo once, neither repeats while the trigger stays held, and the next pull clicks again. A single shot gun still clicks once on
each pull, as before: its way into the branch is unchanged. The same sound, the same line (not reworded), no new text, no
dial, no balance number and no seeded draw. The flag starts unset on a new player, which counts as off.

MEASURED. Check 15.30 deploys a raid, empties the entity list and puts a copy of an automatic in his hands (his own gun if it
is one, else the Sputter) with the jam roll off, no ammo in the magazine and none in the backpack, and records every blip and
every line said. It drives updatePlayer with the trigger held, staging the rate-of-fire clock as run out on each frame.
Controls: the selected belt cell is a gun cell; a fresh pull held three frames clicks and says Out of ammo (exactly once, or
it fails); two rounds loaded and held for six frames fire both and leave the magazine empty with no reload. Then the four
empty held frames must give exactly one dry click and one Out of ammo line; on v15.29 they give none, so the check fails there.
After letting go, a fresh pull must click once again. Everything it changes (blip, say, the trigger and keys, the entity list,
the selected cell, the gun and the player fields, the raid) is put back in finally.
A JScript run of the real fire block cut from scratch copies of v15.29 and the build, with a stand-in player: v15.29 fails on
the held run dry, the build passes; a mutant that clicks every frame fails (4 clicks), a mutant that never clears the flag
fails; a single shot gun gives the same result on both builds (last round held: no click; each later pull: one click and one
line). Dry run on scratch copies of v15.27: p1528 and f1528, p1529 and f1529, then p1530 and f1530, all applied, every anchor
whole lines matching once, and the new check compiles.

Not verified: a live raid by ear, holding an automatic through its last magazine.
## v15.29 - A PILLAGER GOING DOWN SOUNDS WHERE HE FALLS

Sound audit finding (MEDIUM). A pillager who takes lethal damage goes down (raiderDown, on by default), and the downed branch
in updateEnts draws the DOWNED label out in the world and called blip('hit') with no distance and no pan. blip plays a call
with no distance at full volume and a call with no pan centred, so this was the square 240 to 70 Hz hit at gain 0.10: the
same call damagePlayer makes when you are hit. Machines fight pillagers anywhere on the map (machVsRaider, on by default, and
machHuntRaider has no check on distance from you), so a sentry dropping a pillager 2000 units away played your own hit sound
with nothing on screen and no health lost. It taught you to ignore the one sound that means you are being hit.

THE BUILD. The hit sound now plays at his distance and pan from you, read with earsOf, the helper the enemy voices already
use (it returns d, the distance from the player, and pan, dx/520 clamped to -1..1). blip fades it with distance and it goes
silent past about 880 units, so a man downed beside you is still heard, on his side, and one downed out of earshot is not.
The DOWNED label, the sound itself, the downed rules and every number are unchanged, and it stays inside the existing !G.sim
guard with no seeded draw. It stays blip with earsOf rather than sfx, because sfx would also leave a noise ring, which is a
separate change. One side effect: a pillager you down yourself at range is now quieter by his distance (about half volume at
450 units), where it was always full volume before.

MEASURED. Check 15.29 deploys a raid, takes one pillager, leaves him alone in the entity list and records every hit sound.
Near arm: at no health 60 units west of the player, one entity update. Controls, on either build: he goes down, the player
loses no health, and exactly one hit sound is heard. That sound must carry a distance of about 60 and a pan to the left. Far
arm: 1400 units east, the same controls for going down and health; a hit sound, if any, must be at 882 units or more (silent)
and on the right. On v15.28 both arms fail: the hit sound carries no distance and no pan. A JScript run of the check against
the old and new downed branch with a stand-in raid failed on v15.28 and passed on the build; a sound with no distance, no pan,
a flipped pan or a zero distance all fail; leaving the far sound out entirely passes; a build with no downed sound at all
skips on the recorder control. Everything it changes (blip, the entity list, the pillager, the raid) is put back in finally.
Dry run on scratch copies of v15.27: p1528 and f1528, then p1529 and f1529, all applied, every anchor a whole line matching
once.

Not verified: a live raid by ear, a machine downing a pillager out of sight.
## v15.28 - A GRENADE A PILLAGER THROWS SOUNDS WHERE IT LANDS

Sound audit finding (HIGH). A pillager carrying a Frag Charge throws it from 242 to 520 units away (at the default blast

## v15.26 - A BANDAGE ON A RUNNING MEDKIT STOPS AT 85

His ruling of 2026-09-16, verbatim: "bandages should only let players heal to 85 HP -- only medkit gets player back to 100".

v15.23 closed the biggest way past the Bandage ceiling (out-of-combat regen) and left this one for its own build. A heal runs
over seconds, and since v11.82 a second item put on while one is still running adds its health to the queue, takes the faster
rate and the higher ceiling. So a Bandage put on while a Medkit was still healing shared the Medkit's ceiling of 100: from 30,
a Medkit and then a Bandage with about 6 of the Medkit left ended near 96, where the Medkit alone stops near 76 and a Bandage
after it can only add up to 85 plus those 6 (about 91).

THE BUILD. Stacking, the faster rate, the higher ceiling, every heal amount and rate, and the 85 and 100 ceilings all stay. The
queue now also remembers the lowest ceiling in it (a Bandage's 85) and how much of it may go past that ceiling (the health a
Medkit brought). Past 85 only that Medkit health goes on; once it is spent, whatever is left of the queue cannot raise him and
is dropped. In practice: a Bandage over a running Medkit ends at 85 plus what the Medkit still had to give, capped at 100 and at
what was actually queued, which is the same place a Bandage put on first and a Medkit after it would end. A Medkit over a
Bandage still reaches 100. Going down clears the new fields with the rest of the queue.

The four places that ask how high a running heal will go before refusing an item (the heal verb's "Already healing", the item
picker, and the two belt-key refusals) now read one helper, healReach, which gives the same answer as the drain. Without it a
Medkit could be refused as "Already healing" by a queue that would really stop at 91. The refusal sentences are unchanged.

With the heal ceilings dial off every ceiling is full health, so nothing is tracked and healing stacks exactly as before.

MEASURED. Check 15.26 deploys a raid and drives applyHeal and tickHeal directly: three Bandages from 50 end at 85 (control); a
Medkit from 60 ends at 100; a Medkit from 30 drained to about 6 left, then a Bandage, must end no higher than 85 plus what was
left (it ends near 96 on v15.25, so the check fails there); a Bandage from 70, part spent, then a Medkit still reaches 100; and
with the ceilings off the Medkit then Bandage case stacks past 85 plus the remainder again. Dry run on scratch copies: p1514 to
p1523 and their f scripts, then p1526 and f1526 with the version anchors pointed at 15.23 (1524 and 1525 were not drafted yet),
all applied, every anchor a whole line matching once; a JScript run of the old and new heal code gave 96.00 on v15.25 and 90.91 (limit 90.91) on the
build, and over 32,000 random stacked heals behind the game's refusals the helper matched where the drain ended to within 0.001.

Not verified: a real raid by hand, a Medkit then a Bandage from low health. Also left alone: the green incoming-heal block on the
health bar still draws health plus the whole queue, and has never stopped at a ceiling, Bandage alone included.
## v15.25 - KEY 1 NEVER GOES BLACK WHILE HE HOLDS A GUN

His note, verbatim: "when i pick up a gun from the hotbar in game, the other gun in spot 1 goes black for some reason -- is this
intended behavior". It was not. hotbarSlots builds cells 1 and 2 from the two guns in his hands, and a gun bound to a belt key
that he is holding is drawn on that key as the equipped gun (v6.70). A second pass (v6.70) then blanked any
derived cell showing the same thing as a bound key, and for guns that meant the gun cell showing that gun. Press a key holding a
gun from the backpack with two guns carried: equipFromBag puts it in his hands in place of the gun on cell 1, cell 1 now shows
it, the key shows it too, and the pass turned cell 1 into an Empty slot while he held the gun. With one gun carried the new gun
goes to the empty second slot and comes up, and cell 2 went black instead. A stowed gun bound to a key blanked its cell the same
way, so key 2 answered Empty slot for a gun he was carrying.

THE BUILD. The gun branch of the dedupe pass is removed; heals, plates and throwables keep theirs. Cells 1 and 2 always show the
two guns in his hands. A key he bound to a gun he holds keeps drawing it, so that gun shows twice, which matches the rule that
keys he set never move.

WHAT ELSE LEANED ON THE BLANK CELL, AND IS KEPT. Two loops found the gun in his hands as the first gun cell marked in hand, and
with the derived cell blanked that was always the key he bound:
  gunCell (v12.31, v13.42): the raid starts on the gun cell, and every empty cell says Press N for your gun. With the gun on key 5
  it said Press 5 and the raid started on key 5; without a change it would have become cell 1.
  swapGuns (v8.31): the highlight follows the gun. Pressing key 5 to bring up a stowed gun bound there kept the highlight on key 5;
  without a change it would have jumped to cell 2.
Both now go through heldGunCell, which takes a key he bound holding the gun in his hands first and the first cell holding it
second, so both answer exactly what they answered while the cell was blank. swapGuns also leaves the highlight on the pressed
cell when that cell holds the gun that came up, which is what makes key 2, newly usable for a bound stowed gun, keep its own
highlight. Nothing else reads the blank: the drag code tells the two gun cells apart by gunA and gunB and treats a bound key as
an ordinary belt slot either way (v8.14, v11.97), and the belt draw and the trigger read the cell kind, which is now gun. A drop
of a gun from the backpack onto cell 1 was, while cell 1 was blank, an ordinary binding over the gun slot; it is the weapon slot
drop again (v3.21). Two comments that said the dedupe blanks a gun cell (setHot, autoBelt) are annotated.

TWO CHECKS ASSERTED THE BLANK AND ARE REPAIRED. Check 12.31 required cell 1 to be Empty with the held gun on key 5 as its premise,
and its ARM A clicked the blank cell 1 and required no shot and Press 5. The premise now requires cell 1 to show the gun in his
hands, and ARM A requires a click on cell 1 to fire and keep cell 1 (the same staging as check 13.42 ARM D). Its ARMS B and C are
unchanged and still require Press 5, the key he bound. Check 13.42 ARM E required cell 1 to be Empty as staging; it now requires
key 5 to hold the gun in his hands, and still requires the raid to start on key 5.

MEASURED. Check 15.25 deploys at seed 4242 with a pistol in his hands. ONE: a carbine stowed and the SMG in the backpack on key 3
(controls: cell 1 is the pistol and key 3 the backpack SMG), equipped the way the key does it with equipFromBag (controls: the
SMG is in his hands and key 3 shows it); cell 1 must show the SMG. TWO: one gun carried, key 3 pressed through setHot (control:
the SMG is up and the pistol stowed); cell 2 must show the SMG and the highlight stay on key 3. THREE: the carbine stowed on key 5
(control: key 5 shows it); cell 2 must show the carbine, and key 5 must bring it up (control) with the highlight left on key 5.
FOUR: the same room, and key 2 brings the carbine up with the highlight left on key 2. A control that cannot run after a failure
keeps the failure. It fails on v15.24, where cells 1 and 2 are Empty slots.

Not verified: by eye in a raid; a controller walking the belt with the bumpers; the Undercroft belt, which builds the same cells
from the equipped guns and now shows a bound equipped gun on cell 1 as well.
## v15.24 - THE RAID CLOCK WARNS IN ITS OWN VOICE

His note: "i got kileld by the timer and i never got any type of sound warning". The raid clock warnings at five, four, three,

sfx('alarm') plays when a machine or a pillager raises an alarm, and the one a call for extraction plays as the siege is
roused. In a fight a clock warning sounded like one more machine, the line sits on screen 3.2 s and any
other line writes over it, and from thirty seconds to zero nothing else sounds until MERIDIAN IS BURNING THE SITE. The warnings
also fired only when Math.ceil(timeLeft) EQUALLED a mark. The loop caps a frame at 0.05 s, so a live frame cannot skip a whole
second today; the equality test is a latent gap, not the cause of his death.

2600 Hz, at gain 0.12 (twice the alarm), centred, through the same OUT bus. clocktick: one 0.1 s square knock at 1320 Hz, gain
0.09. The warning block in the loop moves to tickClockWarn(prev, now) beside outHint, called once per raid frame with G.warnPrev
(the clock at the end of the last frame, written on every call) and G.timeLeft. A mark in 300, 240, 180, 120, 60, 30 fires when
prev > mark >= now; for a whole number mark this is exactly the old rule on every frame of a falling clock (checked by simulating
a 540 s raid at 60 fps through both: same lines on the same frames), and a frame that jumps past a mark still fires it. The
latest mark crossed speaks with the same say lines as before, unchanged, and plays clockwarn in place of the alarm. Each whole
second from 10 to 1 that is crossed plays one clocktick, and crossing 10 also says TEN SECONDS. followed by outHint(1), the same
hint the thirty second line uses. On the first frame of a raid prev is taken as one whole second above now, which keeps the old
rule of warning when a raid starts on a mark. G.lastWarn is gone; nothing else read it. The bot sim never calls it (the sim
steps the clock in its own path, and blip returns in a sim). No number moves: raid length, the burn and ring timings are as they
were. Player text: one new line, TEN SECONDS. and the hint; no existing sentence changes.

MEASURED. Check 15.24 deploys at seed 4242 (control: the raid runs a clock) and wraps say and blip to record, then steps real
frames of 0.016 s through the loop, staging the clock the frame before (G.warnPrev on this build, G.lastWarn on the old one).
Control: a frame at 100 s runs the clock and records no siren, no tick and no thirty second line. Control: a frame from 30.02 to
29.99 says the thirty second line on either build. The fix: that line plays clockwarn, not the alarm; a frame from 31.2 to 28.9
says the thirty second line and plays clockwarn; a frame from 10.4 to 9.6 plays clocktick and says TEN SECONDS. Then, on a
stand-in audio context through the real blip (control: the alarm starts at 0.06), clockwarn builds sound sources and starts at
least 1.5 times the alarm level, and clocktick builds a sound source. A control that cannot run after a failure keeps the failure.
It restores say, blip and the audio holders, ends the raid and cleans the profile. It fails on v15.23.

## v15.23 - ONLY A MEDKIT GETS HIM BACK TO 100

His ruling of 2026-09-16, verbatim: "bandages should only let players heal to 85 HP -- only medkit gets player back to 100".

The Bandage ceiling of 85 has existed since v9.62 (ITEMS.bandage capHp 85 through healCeil, heal ceilings dial on by default),
and every Bandage use path goes through it. The biggest way past it was out-of-combat regen: after 10 seconds without firing or
being hit, health crept back one point every 3 seconds, all the way to 100. A Bandage to 85 and about a minute of quiet did what
only a Medkit may.

THE BUILD. Regen stops at the Bandage ceiling (85). It never takes health away: at 92 after a Medkit it simply does nothing. With
the heal ceilings dial off it runs to 100 as it did. The regen delay and rate are unchanged.

A second, smaller leak is left for its own build: a Bandage put on while a Medkit heal is still running shares the Medkit's
ceiling, so their shared total can end above what the Medkit alone would reach (from 30, about 96 where the Medkit alone gives 91).

MEASURED. Check 15.23 deploys a raid and runs regen from 80 for two minutes of quiet: with the ceilings off it reaches 100
(control); with them on it must stop at 85, and from 92 it must not move. It fails on v15.22.

Not verified: a real raid, Bandage to 85 and a minute of quiet, by hand.

## v15.17 - A RESTOCKED CRATE OR LOCKER DROPS OFF THE DATA CORE KEY MARKS

Mainframe audit finding 2 (MEDIUM). Slot a Data Core at RACKS (or Arm it on the ascent check) and ascend. startRaid burns the
core and fills G.intelKeys once with every container holding a key_ item, and the sector map (M) draws a gold KEY on each entry
that is not opened. The locked room guarantee skips only caches, strongboxes and containers inside the room, so the key can sit
in a crate or locker. Open that crate, or let a pillager loot it: opened goes true and the mark hides, as intended. About 170 s
later the restock loop in updateEnts rebuilds the crate in place through mkContainer, which rolls only LOOT.crate or LOOT.locker,
and neither table holds a KEY entry. It sets opened back to false, and nothing ever took the crate off G.intelKeys, so the KEY
mark came back on a crate with no key in it and sent him across the map for nothing. The same happened when he opened the crate
and left the key inside: the restock throws that loot away.

THE BUILD. The restock branch in updateEnts, right after it rebuilds the loot and shuts the container, takes that container off
G.intelKeys with indexOf and splice. The guard skips raids with no core burned, where G.intelKeys is unset. The restock rebuilds
the same object, so the reference pushed at the ascent is the one found. The draw loop runs in a different function, so removing
an entry here never skips one mid-draw. Containers opened but not yet restocked, and shut containers holding a key, stay on the
list exactly as before. No player text changes and no number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.17 arms a core and ascends at seed 4242 through __deploy (control: the raid carries intel, the key list is an
array, and the profile core was spent). It takes the first shut crate and the first shut locker, plus a third shut container
apart from both, preferring one the game already listed, gives each a key id the game placed and puts each on the list. The crate
and the locker are opened 200 s back on the raid clock, past the 170 s restock, and one updateEnts frame runs (controls: both got

## v15.16 - AN IMPORTED FRIEND KEEPS THEIR FAVOURITE GUN FOR THE RAID

Mainframe audit finding 1 (MEDIUM). Import a friend's run report at the Mainframe where most runs used the Scav Pistol. The
import line says they favour the Scav Pistol, and the Mainframe hint promises a pillager with their favourite gun. Ascend.
applyGhost takes the first pillager that is not your hire, renames it and hands it the pistol, but mkRaider already pushed that
body's own rolled gun into e.bag as 'gun_'+wk, and that roll is an SMG, Auto Rifle, carbine or scattergun six times in nine. On
the first updateEnts frame raiderUseKit runs for every pillager (raiderKit defaults to 1). kitT starts unset, so the equip test
runs at once, finds a gun of a higher WTIER than the pistol, equips it and drops the pistol into the bag. The friend then
fights the whole raid with the body's gun: its damage, range, sound and tracer. An SMG favourite on a tier-3 body goes the
same way, as does any favourite beaten by a gun the friend loots later.

THE BUILD. The equip test in raiderUseKit now opens with !e.ghost, so the imported friend never swaps guns. Only the equip block
is skipped: it closes before the HEAL section, so the friend still heals from what they carry, and raiderThrow is a separate
function, so they still throw. The body's gun stays in e.bag and is still worth taking off the friend's body. applyGhost is the
only other path that sets a ghost's gun, and blessElite runs at build time before it. Your hire and every other pillager swap
exactly as before. No player text changes and no number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.16 imports a friend favouring the Scav Pistol and ascends at seed 4242 through __deploy (controls: the kit dial
is on, the friend was placed holding the Scav Pistol, and a plain pillager is in the raid). It stages the friend carrying an
Auto Rifle and a Bandage at 40 percent health, and the plain pillager holding a Scav Pistol and carrying an Auto Rifle, both with
kitT at zero, then runs one updateEnts frame (controls: the plain pillager now holds the Auto Rifle with two guns between hand
and carry, so the swap ran on that frame; the friend is still in the raid and up). The friend must still hold the Scav Pistol,
still carry the Auto Rifle, and have started the Bandage. It restores the profile through the loader and puts the ghost back.
It fails on v15.15.

arm drives; the sim, where applyGhost never runs.
## v15.15 - THE SUPERHOT KEY REDRAWS AN OPEN SETTINGS ROW

Dials audit finding 7 (LOW). In the Undercroft open Settings (the SETTINGS station, or T at the DEV BOX): Superhot mode reads Off.
With Settings still open, press the backquote key. The Backquote branch of the window keydown handler runs
cycleGameOpt('superhot'), which writes CFG.superhot=1 through applyGameOpts and saves, and the toast says SUPERHOT ON. The Settings
rows are drawn only by renderSettings and nothing on that path called it, so the button still read Off. Closed on that word, his
next raid ran in Superhot and time stopped whenever he stood still. Clicked to turn it on, the row handler steps from the live dial
(gameOptLive reads On), so the click turned Superhot off and the row redrew as Off: the click looked like it did nothing. The same
held the other way, a row still reading On after the key had turned Superhot off.

THE BUILD. Right after cycleGameOpt in the Backquote branch, renderSettings runs when #settingsmodal carries on, inside a try: the
guard toggleTune already uses when the console closes over Settings (hudSizeStep also redraws inside a try). SHIFT and the
backquote key (the tuning console) are untouched, and nothing redraws while Settings is closed. No player text changes and no
number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.15 skips on a live raid. It stages Superhot and the word editor off in P.gameOpts and applies them (control: the
dials read 0), then opens Settings through openSettings('display') (controls: the window is on, the go_superhot row exists and
reads Off). It clicks the row twice (controls: the dial goes to 1 with the row reading On, then back to 0 reading Off), so the id
and the redraw are live. It dispatches one keydown with code Backquote on window only, with say and say2 wrapped (controls: the
dial is 1, the game said SUPERHOT ON, and Settings is still open); the row must read On. It clicks the row (control: the dial is 0
and the row reads Off); the word must have changed. It clicks the row on again (control: On with the dial at 1) and presses the key
(control: the dial is 0 and it said SUPERHOT OFF); the row must read Off. A control that cannot run after a failure keeps the
failure. It restores say, say2, the windows that were open, CFG and the profile through the loader. It fails on v15.14: the row
reads Off after the key turned Superhot on, the click after it leaves Off reading Off, and the row reads On after the key turned

Not verified: the key pressed over Settings during a raid (the say branch), which the check does not reach; the row's amber
not-default colour by eye.
## v15.14 - A RAID KEEPS THE CLOCK IT STARTED WITH

Dials audit finding 6 (HIGH). In the tuning console (SHIFT and the backquote key) drag Raid timer (s) to OFF and ascend: buildRaid
sets timeLeft and raidLen to 0 and the HUD counts up. Mid-raid, open the console again (the raid pauses under it), drag the same
dial, which is marked NEXT RAID, to any number and close it. Reset all or any preset does the same, since each puts CFG.raidSec
above 0. Every live reader of the clock asked CFG.raidSec rather than the raid, so the first unpaused frame took 0 minus a frame as
an expired clock: MERIDIAN IS BURNING THE SITE, tickNuke downs him at 1.15 s, the raid ends dead with the timer as the killer and
he comes back empty (with a beacon called, endRaid runs on that same frame). The other way, a running 540 raid with the dial moved
to OFF stopped its clock, froze the closing rings and turned the HUD readout to counting up.

THE BUILD. A new raidClockOn() beside elapsed() answers from G.raidLen, which buildRaid sets once beside timeLeft and nothing
changes after, and falls back to CFG.raidSec only when no raid carries one. It replaces CFG.raidSec in the live loop (the
countdown, the clamp to zero while a pull hold is running, and both expiry branches), in elapsed(), in the HUD count-up switch,
and in the three extraction readers (the Pulled line, the 30 second extraction window and its clamp to the clock left). The name
keeps it apart from the clockOn parameter in check 12.44. The bot's simStep, the unused total in the ring closures and the SHORT
WINDOW board text read before a raid are unchanged. No player text changes and no number moves.

CHECK 12.44. Its clock-off arm deployed a 540 raid and wrote CFG.raidSec=0 into it, which is the live read of the dial this build
removes, so after this build that arm would read a 540 raid with 0 left and get a 0.5 s window. f1514 also sets g.raidLen=0 in
that arm, as check 12.24 already does for its clock-on arm. On v15.13 the added line changes nothing that arm reads.

MEASURED. Check 15.14 claims the raid timer in the console and sets it to 0, then ascends at seed 4242 (control: raidLen and
timeLeft are 0). It opens the console over the raid (controls: the console is on, the raid is paused, and the row found is the
raid timer by its maximum), sets that range to 540 and fires its input event so the console's own handler writes the dial, and
closes the console (controls: CFG.raidSec reads 540 and the raid is running). It steps the live loop 12 frames at 16.7 ms from a
timestamp past the last frame (control: G.t rose by more than 0.1 s). The site must not be burning, the raid not over, the player
up with health, timeLeft still 0, and elapsed() equal to G.t. It restores CFG, the console and the profile through the loader. It
fails on v15.13: the first frame starts the burn with the timer as the killer, and timeLeft falls below 0 after it.

Not verified: the reverse direction (a 540 raid with the dial moved to OFF keeps counting down) by reading only, since the check
has one deploy; Reset all and a preset mid-raid, which write the same CFG value; the Settings Raid length row mid-raid; the HUD
readout by eye.

## v15.11 - AN INSTANT QUIT OR A RELOAD FORGETS THE FREEBIE KIT PACKING

Quit audit finding 9 (LOW). Pack a Medkit and Bandages, choose TAKE THE FREEBIE KIT and ascend. commitKit sets that packing

shots takes the instant-quit branch, which saves and returns before the clear. A raid that ended with the page going away (a
closed tab, F5, a crash) left the list saved, and nothing cleared it at load. Next session, pack your own kit, choose MY
LOADOUT, ascend and die: the card counted the old list against the stash and said the items packed before choosing the freebie
kit were in the stash, on a raid where no freebie kit was taken. The stale list also stuck: commitKit keeps a list that is not
empty, so a later freebie kit taken at the stash was counted against the old packing rather than the new one.

THE BUILD. The instant-quit branch clears P.kitBeforeFree, P.hotBeforeFree and P.gunBeforeFree before its save, as every other
raid end already does. applyLoadedProfile clears the same three beside the v14.03 raidSpliced cleanup, where no raid is running;
its callers are boot and the Settings restore from a backup file, which replaces the whole character (restoreApply already
clears the list the same way). hotBeforeFree and gunBeforeFree are written but never read and are cleared so no stale copy is
left. No player text changes and no number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.11 runs three arms in order. One: a save holding a three-item list is loaded through the loader (control: the
loader replaced the profile and deleted a staged raidSpliced, so the block with the fix ran); the list must be gone. Two: the
freebie kit is taken through commitKit over the same packing (control: the list is set aside), the raid goes up at seed 4242
through startRaid with the clock zeroed (controls: the raid carries the freebie kit, the list survived the ascent, and it is an
instant quit by clock, distance, containers and shots) and is abandoned (controls: the run ended as an abandon, G is null and the
run count did not move); the list must be gone. Three: his own kit goes up with no freebie kit at seed 4242 and he dies (controls:
the stash holds copies of the old packing, the raid is not a freebie raid, and the death card is drawn); the card must not carry
the line about items packed before the freebie kit, read with an assembled needle. A control that cannot run after a failure
keeps the failure. It restores the profile through the loader. It fails on v15.10.

## v15.10 - A NOTE TYPED IN THE PAUSE BOX SURVIVES AN INSTANT QUIT

Quit audit finding 8 (MEDIUM). Ascend and, before moving, press ESC or P, which is how a new player reads the controls in the

your next run report." A new call of an existing line: no baked key is reworded, and no number moves.

the YES confirm. Controls: before the click the raid is an instant quit (clock, distance, containers, shots); after it the close
has banked the note into the raid, the run ended as an abandon, G is null and the run log did not grow. It then requires the note
under the floor notes, filed after the unchanged run count, and the noted line. It restores the profile through the loader. It

notes banked in one pause.

## v15.08 - A COOKED FRAG CHARGE KEEPS BURNING THROUGH A ROLL

Throwables audit finding 6 (LOW). Select the Frag Charge cell and hold the trigger: COOKING counts down from 1.1s. At about
0.3s left, press Space. tryRoll has no cooking check, and the roll branch of updatePlayer returns before both places the fuse
burns, so the countdown sits at 0.3s for the whole 0.38s roll. The Frag Charge that should have gone off in his hand during the
roll goes off 0.38s late, and two rolls in one cook hold it about 0.76s past its fuse. This breaks the v13.62 rule that a cooked
grenade keeps burning, and it is the same shape as the v8.59 heal and v13.83 reload fixes in that branch.

THE BUILD. The roll branch now burns a cooking Frag Charge's fuse next to the reload tick, and cooks it off in his hand when the
fuse runs out. It is not gated on the trigger: a release cannot throw mid-roll (the release, doThrow and startCook all wait for
the roll), so the grenade is still in hand. The roll's invulnerability is cleared at the cook-off, because damagePlayer ignores
a hit while p.iv runs and the blast would otherwise do nothing to him. One side effect: rolling within 2s of a revive loses the
rest of that protection if his own Frag Charge goes off in his hand. FRAG_FUSE, the blast and the damage are unchanged, and the
tick makes no seeded draw, so the bot's stream is untouched.

MEASURED. Check 15.08 deploys at seed 4242, puts the Frag Charge cell in hand and stages a cook at 0.5s with the trigger held.
Control: standing, four 0.05s steps of updatePlayer move the fuse to 0.70. Through a 0.38s roll the same four steps must also
reach 0.70 with the roll still running, and a cook 0.03s from its fuse must go off within two roll steps with the roll cover at
zero (explodeFrag is stubbed to record the cook-off, so nothing is hurt). It ends the raid with abandon. It fails on v15.07:
the fuse stays at 0.50 through the roll and the spent cook is still in hand.

Not verified: the COOKING countdown on screen through a roll by eye, a real cook-off mid-roll with the blast damage applied,
and the check has not been run in a browser in this pass.

## v15.03 - THE LIMITED TIME OFFER CARD KEEPS TIME WHILE THE PANEL IS OPEN

Wirt audit finding (MEDIUM). renderWirtLot reads the clock once, when it draws: the minutes under the offer, the lot on the card,
and whether this window's lot is bought. Only renderGamble calls it, and renderGamble runs only on E at the counter, a roll and a
buy. The file has no setInterval and no timer touches the panel. Steps: buy the Limited Time Offer, so the card reads "Bought. New
item in 3 minutes". Leave the panel open for 4 minutes. It still says 3 minutes, a new lot is on sale, and there is no Buy button
until he closes and reopens the panel or pays for a roll. Unbought, "New item in 2 minutes" stays at 2 and the old lot stays on the
card after the window turns. The countdown promises an item that never arrives on screen.

THE BUILD. A new closure function, wirtLotTick, redraws the card only while #gamblemodal is open; with the panel closed it cancels
its timer and stops. renderWirtLot arms it with setTimeout for 50 ms past the moment its minute drops, and at one minute that is 50
ms past the window turn, so the next lot and its Buy button draw. It is armed after the empty-counter return and before the bought
branch, so both cards keep time. renderGamble is not called, so Wirt's line does not rotate, and a rebuilt Buy button keeps its
place in the pad order. No player text changes ("New item in" is untouched) and no number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.03 stubs Date.now to 60.5 seconds before a window turns, calls renderGamble, opens the panel and draws the card
again with setTimeout recorded instead of armed. Control: the card reads 2 minutes, which proves the stubbed clock reached the card.
The draw must arm a redraw due just past the minute turn (500 ms to 1.5 s ahead); the check moves the clock to that moment, runs the
armed redraw, and requires 1 minute and a further redraw armed. A bought card half a second before the turn (control: no Buy
button) must arm a redraw just past the turn that shows the next item and its Buy button, and with the panel closed the next armed
redraw must leave the card as it was and arm nothing more. It restores Date.now, setTimeout, the lot mark and Wirt's line, closes
the panel and cancels the timer. It fails on v15.02: drawing the card arms nothing, so nothing in that build can redraw it.

Not verified: the real timer firing with the panel open in a visible tab (the check runs the armed redraw itself, and a hidden tab
throttles timers); the pad focus staying on a rebuilt Buy button, by eye.
## v15.02 - A RESTORE CODE OPENS WIRT'S OFFER TO THE RESTORED CHARACTER

Save audit finding 3 (LOW). Buying Wirt's limited offer marks the current five-minute period as bought (P.wirtLotBought), which
hides the offer and shows "Bought. New item in N minutes". A restore replaces the character (v14.04 cleared what belonged to the
replaced one) but left this mark, so a restored character who had bought nothing could not buy the offer until the period turned.

THE BUILD. A restore clears the mark with the other per-character state. Restoring a code onto yourself can therefore let the same
lot be bought twice in one five-minute period; the offer turns over within five minutes either way, and no number moves.

MEASURED. Check 15.02 makes a code, marks this period's lot bought (control: it reads as bought), restores the code and requires the
mark gone. It restores the profile through the loader. It fails on v15.01.

Not verified: Wirt's counter after a real restore by eye.

count against the new standing, and the restored character's own count was lost.

THE BUILD. The code carries the count and a restore sets it. An older code without it starts at 0.

## v14.96 - THE GUN HOVER PRINTS ITS REAL RATE OF FIRE

Unit audit finding 1 (HIGH). In WEAPONS, rof is the milliseconds between shots: the trigger fires when now minus the last shot
is greater than rof, now is G.t in milliseconds, and machines wait rof/1000 seconds. The item hover shown in the stash and the
in-raid backpack printed rof as rounds per minute, and worked out the damage a second held as rof/60. So the Compact SMG, 88 ms
between shots, read 88 rpm; the Whisper, 520 ms, read 520 rpm and 121 damage a second held. The order was backwards: the slowest
gun read fastest, on the panel used to choose a gun. The comment above the function said rof was rounds per minute.

THE BUILD. Words only. RATE is 60000/rof rounds per minute and the damage a second held is damage times 1000/rof. The comment
says milliseconds. No weapon number moves.

MEASURED. Check 14.96 takes the gun items with the shortest and longest gaps (control: both hovers print a rate in rpm): the
fastest must read more rpm than the slowest, and its rate must be its gap turned into shots a minute. It fails on v14.95.

Not verified: the hover by eye; shots counted in a live raid.
## v14.95 - THE SHORT WINDOW TERM DOES NOT PROMISE TO CUT A RAID CLOCK THAT IS OFF

Falsy-zero audit finding 1 (LOW). The tuning console's raid timer slider reaches 0, shown as OFF, and every raid reader treats 0
as no clock at all. The SHORT WINDOW term's words read the clock with `CFG.raidSec||DEF.raidSec`, so 0 counted as unset and the
Terms board said the whole raid clock is cut by a third, about 356 seconds instead of 540, on a raid with no clock.

THE BUILD. Words only. The term reads the dial as a number, and with the clock off it says there is no clock to cut. What the term
pays is unchanged: with the clock off it still pays its bonus for a cut that changes nothing, which is a number and is left for
his call.

MEASURED. Check 14.95 reads the term with the clock at its default (control: the words name the full clock) and with the clock off:
the words must name neither the full clock nor the cut one. It fails on v14.94.

Not verified: the Terms board by eye with the clock off.

## v14.59 - UP AND DOWN REACH EVERY BACKPACK STACK

Backpack audit finding 4 (MEDIUM). With the backpack open the arrows select a stack: left and right step one, up and down

the backpack with up and down alone (left is drop, A is blocked there), so a pad player could select, drop or inspect only
the first stack. On the keyboard with seven stacks, down from the first jumped to the sixth.

and after the last column back to the first, so it visits every stack. Up mirrors it. Left and right are unchanged.

## v14.55 - A BOOT CRASH REPEATING EVERY FRAME IS ONE ENTRY TOO

Report audit finding 7 (LOW). A crash before the profile has loaded cannot save the profile (that would write the default
character over a real save, v11.47), so it goes to its own list in storage and is merged in after the load. That list never
merged a repeat. On a host with slow async storage, a title-screen drawing error repeating every frame while the profile
loaded wrote a new entry and a storage write every frame, and after the load up to twelve identical entries pushed real
saved crashes out of the crash list.

THE BUILD. A boot crash that repeats the last boot entry within the same window, with numbers ignored as in v14.49, is
counted on that entry. The list is read back from storage on every call, so every call still writes it; what stops is
the list filling with copies.

MEASURED. Check 14.55 clears the boot list, marks the profile not loaded, reports one error eight times with a changing
number, restores the flag and reads the list: the crash must be there (control) as one entry counted eight times. It fails
on v14.54.

Not verified: a slow host storage load with a repeating title error.

## v14.49 - A CRASH REPEATING EVERY FRAME IS ONE ENTRY, NOT TWELVE

Report audit finding 1 (HIGH). The crash catcher merges a repeat into the entry it repeats, counts it, and since v14.05
saves at most once a window for repeats. A repeat had to match the message exactly. Chrome puts the key it tried to read
into the message, so a grid read out of range reports "reading '37'", then '38', and so on as the player or an enemy moves.
None matched: every frame added a new entry, a new entry always saved the whole profile (about sixty saves a second, and
the game stutters while the fault lasts), and the list holds twelve, so within twelve frames every earlier crash, the root
cause included, was pushed out. The report showed twelve near-identical lines from the last fifth of a second.

THE BUILD. A repeat matches with every run of digits ignored; the entry keeps the first message it saw. A new entry saves at
most once a second, so a burst of different errors cannot save every frame either; repeats still save at most once a
window.

MEASURED. Check 14.49 replaces saveProfile with a counter and reports ten errors that differ only in the key they read,
then one different error: the different one must have its own entry (control), the ten must be one entry counted ten
times, and the burst may save at most twice. It fails on v14.48.

Undercroft floor audit finding 1 (LOW). SPACE rolls on the floor for 0.38 seconds, and station actions still fire during a

with the floor frozen mid-roll. Coming back, the arrival places him at the lamp in the lower left corner, the spot he is
always meant to arrive in, but never ended the roll: on the first free frame he rolled up to about 160 units out of the
lamp in the old direction.

THE BUILD. Arriving on the floor ends any roll, beside the E lock and the cleared keys the arrival already sets.

MEASURED. Check 14.45 arrives on the floor, sets a roll with 0.3 seconds left and the E lock off, then arrives again: the E
lock must be set (control) and the roll over. It fails on v14.44.

Not verified: a roll into R and back from a raid by hand.
## v14.44 - THE FULL SAVES LABEL CLEARS WHEN A SAVE IS FREED

Title and saves audit finding 4 (LOW). Pressing CREATE A NEW SAVE with all eight saves in use replaces the button's label
with ALL EIGHT SAVES HAVE PILLAGERS IN THEM. Nothing ever put the label back. Delete one save and the button still said all
eight were full, although pressing it now worked.

THE BUILD. Drawing the save list, which happens after every delete and every title refresh, puts the button's own label
back. With all eight still full, pressing it says so again.

MEASURED. Check 14.44 sets the full label, redraws the list through titleRefresh (control: a save row is drawn) and
requires the label gone. It fails on v14.43.

Not verified: filling all eight saves and deleting one by hand.
## v14.43 - A SAVE THE GAME CANNOT READ IS NOT QUIETLY REPLACED

Title and saves audit finding 3 (LOW). When a save holds data that will not parse, or has no numeric credits, the loader
ignores it and keeps the fresh default character, and boot then saves that character over the save's key, the thing the
v11.47 crash guard exists to prevent. On the title, a save whose data will not parse was listed as nothing at all, so
CREATE A NEW SAVE treated it as empty and picked it. Either way the old data was gone with no message. It needs a damaged
value in storage, or a host whose storage read fails.

THE BUILD. Before ignoring data it cannot read, the loader copies the raw value aside under the save's key plus :unreadable.
The title lists a save that holds unreadable data as UNREADABLE, with its DELETE button, so CREATE A NEW SAVE passes it by.
Readable saves load and list exactly as before.

MEASURED. Check 14.43 gives the loader unreadable data (the raw value must be kept under the :unreadable key), then writes
unreadable data into save 8 and refreshes the title (save 8 must be listed). It fails on v14.42.

Not verified: recovering a character by hand from a kept :unreadable value.
## v14.42 - ENTER ON THE TITLE STARTS THE GAME AND NOTHING ELSE

Title and saves audit finding 2 (MEDIUM, browser dependent). Any key on the title starts the game; the listener called go()
for Enter and Space but did not cancel the key. A mouse click on GO FULLSCREEN leaves that button focused, and a focused
button's default action on Enter is a click. So click GO FULLSCREEN, press Enter: go() opened the Undercroft, then the
browser clicked the now hidden GO FULLSCREEN and fullscreen toggled off. He landed in the Undercroft windowed. The floor
handler already cancels Space; nothing cancelled Enter.

THE BUILD. Enter and Space on the title cancel the key's default action before starting the game.

MEASURED. Check 14.42 presses a cancelable Enter with the title hidden (control: nothing cancels it) and with the title
showing (the game must start, and the key must be cancelled). It fails on v14.41.

Not verified: GO FULLSCREEN then Enter in a real browser window.
## v14.41 - ERASING A SAVE ERASES ITS UNDO COPY

Title and saves audit finding 1 (MEDIUM). Since v14.06 each save keeps its own restore backup beside it, under the save's
key plus :prerestore, and Settings shows UNDO whenever that backup exists. DELETE on the title screen, after the typed word
and ERASE, removed only the profile key. So:

1. restore a character in save 2 (which writes save 2's backup),
2. switch to save 1 and erase save 2,
3. CREATE A NEW SAVE lands in save 2, the first empty one,
4. Settings shows UNDO on a character that never restored anything, and UNDO writes the erased character over it.

A save the screen says is erased forever was still sitting in storage.

THE BUILD. ERASE removes the save's restore backup as well as the save.

MEASURED. Check 14.41 writes save 7 with a backup, refreshes the title list, presses save 7's DELETE, types the word and
presses ERASE through the page's own buttons: save 7 must be gone (control) and so must its backup. It fails on v14.40.
