## v11.20 - THE FOLLOWER AND SEEKPOINT DISAGREED ABOUT ARRIVING

Found by reading v11.19's measurement instead of filing it. The robot ran out
the clock 5 times on the old rules and 12 on the new, and a machine that runs
out the clock is a machine standing somewhere.

**REPRODUCED.** Batch outcomes cannot be replayed one seed at a time, because
the robot's profile drifts across a run and every raid after the first sees the
drift; so a seeded sim trace hook was added to the fixture, built the way the
batch builds, and seed 9071 was walked. On the shipping rules **the bot stood at
490,1157 inside building 6 from 45 to 120 seconds, moving nothing**, with a nine
point route in hand, its next waypoint 24 units away, no stall timer running and
no slide. Seventy five seconds of a raid, gone.

**THE CAUSE IS MINE, from v11.15.** That build made a waypoint count as reached
at 10 units, or at 30 when the next one can be walked straight to, so a body no
longer turned inside a door. One call down, seekPoint treats a target inside
ONE STEP as already reached and returns without moving. At the live frame a
step is about 3 units and the two never meet. At the sim's 0.15 second step a
150 unit body steps 27, so a waypoint between 10 and 27 units away is "not
reached" to the follower and "reached" to seekPoint, and the body does nothing
until something else changes its mind. A slow live frame of 0.1 seconds steps
18 and can do the same to a machine on a laggy night.

**THE FIX.** A waypoint counts as reached at one step, whatever the step is,
floored at the 10. One expression, both follower sites.

**MEASURED, the same 320 paired seeds as v11.19, both arms now carrying the
fix.** Old rules extract **32.2 percent**, new rules **40.0 percent**; both on
47 seeds, neither on 136, old alone 56, new alone 81, z 2.05, two sided p
0.040. Where v11.19 read the seven building builds as no change to the robot's
odds, they were a gain hidden under this stall: **timeouts on the new rules 12 to
0**, on the old rules 5 to 4 (those four are the old world's own wall-hug
stalls, the ones v11.15 fixed). The average raid on the new rules now runs 87
seconds against 122 on the old, crawler kills 117 to 100, sentry 68 to 49,
pillager 10 to 17, mean haul 2,017 to 1,960. Read plainly: on honest routes the
robot gets where it is going faster than the freed machines can punish it.
This is a bug fix's side effect and not a dial, and every one of the seven
rules still has its switch.

**NEW CHECK v11.20** replays seed 9071 through the seeded trace and requires the
bot never to stand still for fifteen seconds with a route in hand and health
left. Controls: the raid must run at least sixty seconds and move at least five
hundred units, or nothing was measured; and with the old follower, navBody 0,
the bot must not stand still either, since its fault was the jamb and not this,
so a stall there would mean the trace reads something else. On a v11.19 fixture
the finding fires: seventy five seconds ending at 120.

Not verified: THE COLD MILE by the paired run, and his own play. The seeded
trace hook and the paired runner stay in the fixture.
## v11.19 - THE MEASUREMENT THE LAST SEVEN BUILDS OWED

Nothing in the game changes in this build. Seven builds in a row, v11.12 to
v11.18, ended with the same line: the extract rate was not measured, because a
paired run at the 320-seed standard was several hours in this environment. This
tick it was not, and it ran.

**THE RUN.** 320 seeds, 9001 to 9320, COLD STORAGE, the bot at its pinned
greed of 14, each seed raided twice: once with every building rule since v11.12
switched off (winWalk, furnDoor, navBody, doorClear, furnIDoor, furnGap,
partDoor, all 0), which is the world of v11.11, and once with all seven on,
which is the world that ships. Same seed, same map, same drop, same robot; only
the rules differ. About thirty five minutes in two batches.

**THE RATE DID NOT MOVE.** Old rules extract **34.7 percent**, new rules **35.0
percent**. Both arms extract on 55 seeds, neither on 152, the old arm alone on
56 and the new arm alone on 57. That is 113 discordant pairs splitting 56 to
57, z of minus 0.09, which is as close to no difference as a run of this size
can read. Machines getting out of buildings, routes that respect windows and
body width, doors clear of furniture and walls: **none of it changed how often
the bot comes home.**

**WHAT DID MOVE IS WHERE IT DIES, and by how long it lives.** Killed by a
pillager: 20 to 9. Ran out the clock: 5 to 12. Warden 4 to 9, Bulwark 5 to 8,
sentry 70 to 66, crawler 88 to 90. Mean raid length, extract or death, 124
seconds to 141. Mean haul 2,083 to 2,065. Read together: on honest routes the
bot walks further to get anywhere, so its raids run seventeen seconds longer, it
meets the big machines more and the pillagers less, and it runs the clock out
more than twice as often. The crawlers, which every one of the seven builds was
about, kill it the same number of times either way; they could not reach it
before and mostly still do not, because the bot does not go into buildings the
way he does.

**WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SAY.** It says the alpha's difficulty for the
robot is unchanged by seven builds of geometry and routing work, which is the
thing I could not say before. It does not say what the changes do to HIM: the
bot never hides and never fights pillagers, so the crawler that could not see a
hidden man through a window, the one that stood in a doorway plugged by a
table, and the one that caught on a partition corner were all bugs a person met
and the bot did not. The measurement is of the machine's world, which is what
the sim measures.

**NEW CHECK v11.19** pins the seven rules on by name in the shipping defaults,
and requires that switching all seven off builds a different world for the same
seed, different walls and furniture and a different route grid, while entities
and containers stay identical, which is what makes a paired seed a fair
comparison. Its message names the rule that ships off, if one ever does.

Not verified: THE COLD MILE, which was not run, and his own play, which no sim
covers. furnIDoor 0 and the other six put the old world back for any seed.
## v11.18 - NO INTERIOR WALL ENDS INSIDE A DOORWAY

The map generation fault v11.16 found while walking THE COLD MILE, and closed.

**MEASURED FIRST, on v11.17 at seed 4242.** A spine corridor wall runs from
side wall to side wall, an L split runs from top wall to bottom, and an alcove
hangs off a wall at a rolled height, and none of the three plans ever knew where
the shell had put its doors. A door is touched when a partition reaches into its
opening zone, the gap grown 40 units through the wall, and dead when that
partition leaves under 30 units on both sides of itself. **COLD STORAGE: 3 of 37
doors touched, none dead. THE COLD MILE: 19 of 151 touched, 4 dead**, among them
the door at 2960,3167 that v11.16 traced, 26 units above the wall and 22 below.
A dead door is a door nothing 30 wide can use, and every route was already
being planned round it.

**THE FIX.** Every partition that reaches into a door's zone on its own building,
the gap grown 30 along the wall and 40 through it, has that part cut away, so
the door opens onto floor. A cut in the middle of a partition splits it in two,
each half a clone that keeps every tag the wall had, and an end shorter than 3
units is dropped.

**MY FIRST CUT MOVED THE WORLD, AND THE CHECK SAID SO.** I ran the trim inside
makeBuilding, before anything was placed, and the mile's 374 entities became
369: crawlers are counted into the rooms the partitions make, and a corridor
wall cut back from a door is a corridor joined to a room. The trim now runs at
the END of the map build, after every roll, where the ruin pass runs, so
placement sees the walls it always saw and only the finished geometry changes.
Entities 85 and 374 both ways, containers 165 and 593 both ways, furniture
identical both ways because it was placed before the cut.

**MEASURED AFTER:** touched 3 to 0 and 19 to 0, dead 0 to 0 and 4 to 0. Walls
552 to 551 and 2206 to 2205, one segment a map net, and v9.81 re-pins to that
with the reason in its text. Lamps 59 to 58 and 265 to 262, since the lamp pass
asks the finished walls where it may stand; the sky for the seed did not roll
this time.

**NEW CHECK v11.18** surveys every door on both maps with the rule on and
requires no door touched and none dead. Controls: entities and containers must
be identical with the rule off, or the cut drew a random number, which is the
control that caught my first cut; and with the rule off the mile must still
show at least 3 dead doors and 12 touched, or the dial does not restore the old
partitions. v11.16's old arm switches this rule off as well as its own, because
the partition it stood the crawler against is the one this build cuts back. On a
v11.17 fixture the finding fires for both maps.

Not verified: the extract rate, still. And the cut is judged by geometry and by
routes, not by eye: a corridor that now opens at its end next to a door reads
differently from one that met the wall, and no picture was taken. partDoor 0
restores the old partitions.
## v11.17 - THE DOORWAYS INSIDE BUILDINGS ARE CLEAR OF FURNITURE TOO

The fifth build on machines getting out of buildings, and the first about
getting INTO them. v11.14 kept furniture out of the shell doorways and nothing
in the game knew that the plans cut doorways in the partitions as well.

**MEASURED FIRST, on v11.16 at seed 4242.** A building is sealed inside when no
route on the route grid runs from just inside any of its own front doors to its
middle. **COLD STORAGE 0 of 20. THE COLD MILE 5 of 84: buildings 32, 33, 37, 38
and 74**, every one of them open with the furniture stripped from the wall list,
and two of them shut to the player's own padding as well, so those rooms and
what was placed in them could be seen and never reached, by him or by anything
hunting him.

**TWO CAUSES, TRACED.** Four of the five are furniture parked in a partition
doorway, the gap a spine, a strongroom or an L split cuts in an interior wall,
which v11.14's rule never saw because only the shell doors were recorded. The
fifth, building 74, is a free standing piece that landed between the ends of two
alcove partitions, 8 units below one and 14 beside the other, and split the
building in two for anything wider than 8. The sealed room repair pass never saw
either, because it floods a grid with no body in it and an 8 unit sliver reads
as a corridor there.

**THE FIX, two rules, neither drawing a random number.** The plans now record
the doorways they cut, the way the shell records its doors, and furniture keeps
the same zone clear of them. And a piece that would leave a gap between 2.5 and
30 units to any wall or partition of its building is not placed: flush is fine,
overlapping is as it was, a body's width or more is fine, and the band between is
where a room gets sealed. Furniture against other furniture is left alone,
because a sliver between two pieces is the v10.40 niche, cosmetic, and cannot
close a room on its own.

**MY TWO WRONG CUTS, both caught by measuring before shipping.** The gap rule
first read a one unit gap as a gap, and the hug places every piece one unit off
its wall on purpose: 136 pieces became 9 and 440 became 33. Touching is under
2.5 now. Then, counting every neighbouring piece as well as every wall, it still
cost three pieces in ten, 136 to 96 and 440 to 310, and he asked for MORE
furniture, not less. Walls and partitions only is what ships.

**MEASURED AFTER, both maps, the dials off against on:** sealed interiors 5 to 0
on the mile and 0 to 0 on COLD STORAGE. Entities 85 and 374 both ways,
containers 165 and 593 both ways. **Furniture 136 to 108 and 440 to 336**, about
one piece in four, each of them either in a doorway or wedged where a body could
not pass it. Walls 580 to 552 and 2308 to 2206, mile lamps 265 to 269, and so the
sky for seed 4242 rolled again, COLD STORAGE back to noon in fog and the mile to
morning fog, for the reason v11.14 wrote down. The crawler in the middle of
building 32 on the mile, whose front room was sealed off, now walks out and
reaches a player outside inside 60 units; with the rules off it never leaves.

**NEW CHECK v11.17** surveys both maps with the rules on and requires zero
sealed interiors, the target being the nearest open route cell to each middle
rather than the exact centre, which can sit inside a table's padding. Controls:
the map must record interior doorways at all; entities and containers must be
identical with the rules off; the rules off must still seal at least 4 on the
mile; and the building 32 crawler must reach a player outside with the rules on
and never leave with them off. On a v11.16 fixture the finding fires for the
five and the map records no interior doorways.

**THREE OLDER CHECKS MOVED WITH IT, each saying why in its own text.** v9.81 re-pins
the wall count to 2206 and 552 and v9.65 the mile cover to 490, the way they
followed v11.14. And v11.14 itself: its dial-off arm is all three furniture
rules off now, because the gap rule alone clears a doorway piece, so its plugged
count control reads the old placement again; and its furniture floor, which
now spans the three rules together, sits at a half against the 0.64 and 0.62
measured.

Not verified: the extract rate, still, and what a quarter fewer pieces looks
like to his eye; every one removed was in a doorway or in a gap a body could not
pass, and no picture was taken. furnIDoor 0 and furnGap 0 restore the old
placement piece for piece.
## v11.16 - A DOOR CELL SITS CLEAR OF EVERY WALL, NOT ONLY THE DOOR FRAME

Fourth build on machines getting out of buildings, and the first walked on THE
COLD MILE.

**THE FIRST MAP, RE-READ WITH A FAIR HARNESS.** Two of the three COLD STORAGE
buildings I called short last build were my harness. Building 19's player was
placed at x 4250, outside a world that ends at 4200, so the crawler stood at the
border wall 109 units from a man it could never reach; placed inside the world
it is on him at 34. Building 5's target is a pocket of open ground on the map's
east side that nothing can route into from the drop, the player included;
the building itself is reachable. Building 6 is a 1,900 unit walk round a
neighbour and simply needs more than fifteen seconds. **So COLD STORAGE is 12 of
13 buildings delivering their crawler, and the thirteenth is my target choice,
not a box.** The v10.84 line "building 3 finds a route and does not walk it" is
closed the same way: building 3 has no open ground outside it at all, which is
why that check never tested it.

**THE MILE, SAMPLED.** Ten buildings with open ground, fresh deploy each,
fifteen seconds: **9 deliver the crawler onto the player at 34 to 36 units.**
Building 20 leaves its own building at one second and then stands at 2985,3178
for the rest of the trial, 313 units off.

**TRACED.** Its route runs west, through the building next door, in at that
building's east door and out at its west door at 2960,3167. A partition at
2976,3193 runs from inside that building straight into the doorway, leaving 26
units of gap above it and 22 below, neither wide enough for a body. The route
grid should have said so. It did not, because carveDoors, which opens the cells
a route needs to pass through a doorway, rejected only cells whose centre was
INSIDE a wall; a cell one unit above the partition was opened as a waypoint,
3000,3192 with 2984 and 2968 beside it, and the crawler steering at it stood
against the partition fourteen units inside its padding.

**THE FIX.** The carve asks every door cell to sit the body's padding clear of
every wall that is not on the door's own line; the jamb band already handles
those. If that opens nothing for a door the old rule is used for that door, so
no door that was open before is closed by it. **MY FIRST CUT WAS INERT AND THE
CHECK SAID SO**: it counted only the cells it newly opened, and a door whose
clear cells were already open in the body sized base grid counted as opening
nothing, so the fallback undid the strict pass every time and both arms read 58
cells and the same route. A cell already open is a door cell too; counted, the
strict pass opens 0 extra cells on the mile, because the pad 15 grid of v11.15
already keeps door gaps 15 clear of their jambs, and the only doors that ever
needed the carve are the ones with something in the way, which is exactly where
it must refuse.

**MEASURED AFTER.** With the door next door closed to it, building 20's route
goes round the north, about 2,200 units, the crawler leaves at frame 63 as
before and **is on the player at 35 units by twenty five seconds**; with the old
carve it stands at 2985,3178 at fifteen seconds and at twenty five, 313 off.
Route existence across both maps is unchanged.

**FOUND ON THE WAY, FOR THE NEXT BUILDS, both written into AUDIT.md.** The
partition running into a doorway is a map generation fault of its own. And the
three mile buildings whose interiors no route reaches, 32, 33 and 38, are
interiors whose PARTITION doorways hold furniture: strip the furniture and all
three become reachable at the crawler's padding; two of them are shut to the
player's padding as well. v11.14 cleared the exterior doorways only.

**NEW CHECK v11.16** drives the crawler out of building 20 on the mile by its
fingerprint and requires it to be on the player inside 60 units in twenty five
seconds. Controls: with doorClear 0 it must be no closer than 150, or the old
carve does not show the fault; the strict pass must open fewer cells than the
old rule; and the building 8 crawler on COLD STORAGE must still reach the
player. On a v11.15 fixture the finding fires at 313.

Not verified: the extract rate, and the other forty nine buildings on the mile
by walking. Ten were walked and one was traced. The paired run at the 320-seed
standard is several hours here and was not run. doorClear 0 restores the old
carve.
## v11.15 - THE ROUTE GRID IS PADDED FOR THE BODY THAT WALKS IT

The third build in a row on machines getting out of buildings, and the one that
closes the v10.84 line "finds a route and does not walk it".

**MEASURED FIRST, on v11.14 at seed 4242.** One crawler in the middle of each
building on COLD STORAGE with open ground outside it, the player on that ground,
the chase held on, a fresh deploy per trial, fifteen seconds each. **7 of 13
buildings deliver the crawler onto the player.** Building 5 has no route.
Buildings 15 and 18 HAVE a route and the crawler never leaves the building.

**TRACED, both of them.** Building 18: the door runs 2695 to 2759 on the east
wall and the route's waypoint sits at 2728,2696, one unit inside the top jamb. A
body of radius 15 steering at it walks into the wall beside the door and stands
there. Building 15: the string pull straightens the route from 3176,1934 to
3240,1976 with a zero width line that grazes the end of a partition at
3216,1960; the body catches on that corner at 3226,1949 and stays.

**WHY.** The route grid is padded 12 for bodies of radius 15, so a route cell
can be a place the body cannot stand; door cells were opened with no padding at
all, so a waypoint could sit on a jamb; and the pull tested a line with no width,
so it straightened across corners the body cannot round. Three places that did
not know how big the walker is.

**THE FIX, and why the world does not move.** The ROUTE grid, map.navD, is now
built padded 15 while map.nav stays at 12 and keeps deciding what the map places
where, so entities and containers are untouched. Door cells must sit 15 clear of
both jambs. The pull tests three lines, the centre and one a body's width either
side, with the edges asked only when the centre passes so the cost lands on
accepted corners. And the follower counts a waypoint done at 10 units, or at 30
only when it can go straight to the next one; at a plain 30 it turned for the
next waypoint while still inside the door and walked into the jamb, which the
building 8 guard caught on my first cut.

**MEASURED AFTER, the same sweep on v11.15: 10 of 13.** Buildings 15 and 18 walk
out and are on the player at 36 and 34 units, building 11 joins them, and every
building that delivered before still does. Building 19 leaves at four seconds
and is still 109 units off at fifteen, as before; building 6 leaves and is far
off, as before; building 5 has no route either way. Route existence is
unchanged: the same three buildings across both maps have no route with either
grid, so nothing was closed by the wider pad.

**NEW CHECK v11.15** drives the crawler out of buildings 15 and 18, each by its
fingerprint, and requires it to leave and be on the player inside 60 units in
fifteen seconds. Controls: with navBody 0 neither crawler may leave its building
in ten seconds, or the old grid does not show the fault; the route grid must open
a different number of door cells with the dial on and off, or the dial builds
nothing different; and the building 8 crawler must still reach the player, which
is the guard that failed on the first cut at 255 units. On a v11.14 fixture the
finding fires for both buildings.

Not verified: the extract rate, for the third build running, and THE COLD MILE by
walking. Route existence was measured on both maps; the walk sweep was COLD
STORAGE only, thirteen buildings, and the mile has fifty nine. The paired run at
the 320-seed standard is several hours here and was not run. navBody 0 restores
the old grid, the old door cells, the zero width pull and the plain 30, all at
once.
## v11.14 - NO PIECE OF FURNITURE SITS IN A DOORWAY

The second half of the thing v11.12 found. That build stopped machines walking
into windows and then said plainly that it freed nobody on COLD STORAGE, because
the doors themselves were blocked. This is the doors.

**MEASURED FIRST, on v11.13 at seed 4242.** A doorway is plugged when the longest
clear run across its 64 unit gap, counting furniture within 40 units of the wall
on either side, is under the 30 units a body needs. **11 of 37 doorways on COLD
STORAGE and 35 of 151 on THE COLD MILE were plugged**, and 2 and 27 more were
tight, under 44. Building 8 on COLD STORAGE is the case traced at v11.12: a 36 by
26 piece inside the doorway, 10.5 units one side and 17.5 the other, and the
crawler inside never came within 240 units of a player standing outside, at seven
seconds or at thirty. This is the v10.40 "niches plugged by furniture" line, and
it was never cosmetic; it sealed machines in and it is the last piece of
"crawlers aren't attacking properly" I can find.

**WHY IT HAPPENED.** The furniture pass shoves every piece after the first flush
against the nearest wall, on purpose, so that a piece cannot split a room and
seal it. A wall with a door in it is still the nearest wall, and nothing in that
pass had ever heard of doors. The doorways are recorded before the furniture is
placed, in the same function, so the information was there all along.

**THE FIX.** Each doorway owns a zone: the gap grown 40 units through the wall
both ways and 12 along it. A piece landing in a zone is not placed. Re-rolling
it would have drawn from the seeded stream and moved every wall, crawler and
container placed after it, which is the mistake v10.81 made and measured. Not
placing it draws nothing.

**MY FIRST CUT SLID THE PIECE ALONG ITS WALL INSTEAD, AND THE CORPUS CAUGHT IT
SEALING TWO ROOMS.** Buildings 26 and 51 on THE COLD MILE held floor nothing
could reach, because the interior partitions have doorways of their own that the
door list has never heard of, and a slid piece lands wherever the zone ends. A
piece that is not placed cannot seal anything, so that is what ships. The cost is
the doorway pieces themselves: **furniture 169 to 136 on COLD STORAGE and 540 to
440 on THE COLD MILE**, four fifths kept on both. That is one piece in five, and
every one of them was standing in a door.

**MEASURED AFTER, both maps, the dial off against on:** plugged doorways 11 to 0
and 35 to 0, tight doorways 2 to 0 and 27 to 0. Entities 85 and 374 both ways,
containers 165 and 593 both ways. Walls 610 to 580 and 2403 to 2308, outdoor
cover on the mile 483 to 488. **The crawler in building 8 now reaches the
player**, inside 60 units at eleven seconds, against never in thirty before.

**AND THE WORLD DID MOVE, IN ONE PLACE I DID NOT EXPECT, WHICH THE JERSEY CHECK
FOUND.** v10.46 reads the pale numeral on the 23 jersey at the drop point and it
went from 20 pixels to 2. Not the jersey: the light. Lamps are placed by asking
the wall list where one may stand, so with thirty fewer walls one more lamp fits
on COLD STORAGE, 59 to 60, and each lamp draws four numbers from the seeded
stream. The time of day and the weather are rolled AFTER the lamps, so seed 4242
went from noon in fog to six in the evening under a clear sky, and the golden
light pulled the white numeral under the check's brightness line. Entities and
containers are placed before the lamps and did not move. So: **for any given
seed the sky may be different from what it was; nothing on the ground is.** Same
mechanism as the cover count that v9.77 and this build re-pin, and it is why a
check that measures colour must pin the light it measures under, which v10.46
now does.

**THREE OLDER CHECKS MOVED WITH IT, and each says why in its own text.** v9.81
pins the wall count and v9.65 the cover count, the way v9.77 moved them before;
both now carry 2308 and 580, and 488, with the entity line beside them as the
half of the fingerprint that says the seeded stream did not move where it
matters. v9.79 asked for no unreachable floor anywhere with no size floor at
all, and had only ever passed because the buildings holding slivers between
furniture pieces were the same buildings whose plugged doorway got them stripped
bare. With the doors open those slivers show. v10.40 already ruled a pocket
narrower than a body cosmetic and its own line, so v9.79 now asks for a room,

**NEW CHECK v11.14** builds both maps twice, dial off and on, and requires zero

plugged counts and on the crawler, at 273 units.

Not verified: the extract rate, again. This is the build that actually lets
machines out of buildings, so it is the one that changes what a raid feels like,

## v11.13 - HIS RULING ON THE CROWD: THE GHOST MASK AND THE SPARTAN HELMET ARE HIS

that is a better than even chance one of the two is in the room at any moment,

in those rolls, or the crowd has stopped dressing rather than left two pieces
alone. Both pieces must still be on the rack itself, since they were only ever
to come off the crowd. And the rule must be the flag and not the two names: the

must come back. On a v11.12 fixture the finding fires for both pieces and the

## v11.12 - A WINDOW IS SEE-THROUGH AND IT IS NOT WALK-THROUGH

This is the other half of "crawlers aren't attacking properly", and it is not
about crawlers. **Every movement decision in this game asked the SIGHT geometry
whether the way ahead was clear**, and the sight list skips windows on purpose,
because you can see through a window. Nothing can WALK through one: collide()
has never skipped a window and never will.

So a machine standing inside a building with a window facing the player was told
the line was clear, **threw its route away**, walked at the window, and stood
there pressed against the glass for the rest of the raid, moving a fraction of a
unit a frame, while a door stood open twenty feet away.

**REPRODUCED FIRST, on COLD STORAGE at seed 4242**, one crawler placed in the
middle of each building with the player outside it and the chase held on. The
crawler in building 8 walked straight west from x 2702 to x 2551 and stopped
dead: wall 234 at x 2520, 16 by 61, flagged win. It then moved between 0.07 and
0.98 units a frame, forever, while a route appeared and was thrown away every
couple of seconds.

**FOUR PLACES ASKED THE WRONG QUESTION, and the fourth was the one that
mattered.** The shortcut in navSeek that drops the route and walks straight; the
wall hug leaving the wall because it can see past it; the choice of which way
round, which counted a window as room; and the string-pull inside navPath
itself, which took a perfectly good grid route out of the door and pulled it
tight through the window because it could SEE from the start to the goal. With
the first three fixed the crawler still walked into the glass, because the route
it was handed was two points long and the first one was the target.

**THE FIX IS TO ASK THE RIGHT QUESTION.** The map keeps the window segments now
instead of dropping them, the raid carries a grid for them so the test is a
cell lookup and not a scan of 488 segments per body per frame, and all four
tests ask whether the line can be WALKED rather than SEEN. buildNav reads the
WALL list, not the segment list, so the routing grid has always treated a window
as solid; a body denied the straight line gets the route it already had.

**MEASURED, the route out of every building with open ground outside it, both
maps at seed 4242, the dial off against on:** 1 of 13 on COLD STORAGE and 6 of
59 on THE COLD MILE were a straight line through a window and are a real route
now. Building 8: two points and a 6 unit corner before, six points and a 186 unit
corner after. Building 20 on the mile: a 2 unit corner before, 594 after, which
is a body that was walking into a window from six hundred units off its real
way out.

**AND IT DOES NOT, BY ITSELF, FREE A SINGLE MACHINE ON COLD STORAGE, which I am
saying plainly because my first check claimed it would.** Driven for seven
seconds and then for thirty, buildings 8, 9 and 10 still never reach the
player; they now walk a real route and end up further away instead of standing
at the glass. The reason is a SECOND defect: **the door of building 8 is plugged
by furniture.** Wall 245, a 36 by 26 piece, sits inside the 64 unit doorway at
x 2655 to 2719 and leaves 10.5 units one side of it and 17.5 the other, for a
body that needs 30. The route goes through the door; the body cannot. That is
the v10.40 "niches plugged by furniture" line, and it is not cosmetic, it seals
machines in. It is the next build. Four buildings reached the player before this
build and the same four reach it after; none was lost.

**MY MISTAKE, and it cost most of the tick:** my first sweep ran thirteen
buildings back to back on one deploy with the frame clock restarted for each,
so the game saw time run backwards and the crawler carried its wall-hug state
from one building into the next. It reported building 16 going from 183 units
to 34 and building 10 from 242 to 36. Neither is true; both read the same in
both arms when each trial gets its own deploy. Every number above is from a
fresh deploy per trial.

**NEW CHECK v11.12** is in three parts and none of them asks a crawler to do
something it cannot. Geometry: either side of a window, on at least three
windows with clear ground both sides, the game must report that you can see
across and cannot walk across. Route: from the middle of building 8 to the
player outside, the dial off must give two points and no corner, the dial on at
least three points and a corner over 60 units; and at least 1 route on COLD
STORAGE and at least 4 on THE COLD MILE must change shape. Guard: the crawler in
building 14, which reached the player at 34 units before this build, must still
reach him inside 60.

Three controls. An open line 120 units long must pass BOTH tests, or the walk
test is simply refusing everything. With winWalk 0 the walk test must agree with
the sight test on every window, or the dial does not turn the fix off. And
building 8 must still be the 2520,900,380,340 rectangle this was traced on, so
a moved map says so by name instead of quietly testing somewhere else.

Not verified: what this does to the extract rate. Every body on the map steers
through navSeek and navPath, so the bot and the pillagers route differently now
as well, and a paired A/B at the 320-seed standard is several hours in this
environment and was not run. The direction is not in doubt, a machine that used
to stand at a window now walks its real route, but the size of it is unmeasured,
and on COLD STORAGE at least it frees nobody until the furniture is moved.
winWalk 0 restores the old behaviour exactly if it turns out to matter.
## v11.11 - THE FRESH PROFILE HOUR, AND IT FOUND NOTHING

His notes are all shipped and the named audit backlog is empty, so this tick went
to the thing the alpha actually needs and nobody had done: **what a friend sees**.
A profile with no runs, no extracts, no stash, no contracts, no racks, one pistol
and 600 credits, and then every station on the Undercroft floor walked up to and
pressed.

**THE SWEEP FOUND NOTHING.** Nine stations. None threw, in the call or in a
handler afterwards. None opened a panel with nothing in it. None did nothing. The
stash reads correctly with nothing in it, saying "Nothing in the stash. Ascend,
pillage, extract.", and its tabs switch and filter.

**THREE TIMES MY OWN PROBE CRIED WOLF, and those are worth more than the clean
result**, because each was one sentence away from being reported to him as a bug:

  1. **"The stash station does nothing."** It opens a SCREEN and not a modal, and
     my sweep only looked for modals.
  2. **"The GUNS tab does not switch."** The tab elements are two levels down
     inside their container, so I had clicked the container.
  3. **"The GUNS tab counts one gun and shows an empty shelf."** An owned gun
     draws as an ICON with no text in it, and I was counting words. Counted in
     cells, the shelf has exactly the one gun on it.

**NEW CHECK v11.11** holds that sweep. It builds the fresh profile in memory,
walks every station, and requires no throw, a panel with real content or the hub
screen, and never a station that does nothing. Then it reads the stash in CELLS
rather than in words, requires the GUNS tab to switch and to draw his gun, and
requires SALVAGE to draw nothing at all on a profile that has never looted.

Two controls. SALVAGE drawing cells would mean the tabs are not filtering, and a
deliberate throw inside a click must be heard, because an error in a DOM handler
never reaches its caller and without that the clean result above proves nothing.

**There is no control that fails on the previous build, because there is no
defect.** This check passes on v11.10 and on v11.11 and exists to catch the day a
station starts throwing on a profile that has nothing.

Not verified: the first hour past the floor. This walks the Undercroft and its
panels; it does not go up, loot, die and come back, and the parts of the first
hour that need a raid behind them are still only covered by the checks that were
already there.

**AND IT BROKE TWO CHECKS THE FIRST TIME IT RAN IN THE CORPUS, WHICH IS MINE.**
v11.11 rewrote the profile to a fresh one, restored a LIST of twenty-four fields,
and then called saveProfile, writing whatever survived that list to disk. Two
checks downstream read fields the list had never heard of:

  - v11.09 reported a third typeface. Opening the Fashion station drew the
    clothing rack, and the 23 on a jersey swatch is set in Impact.
  - v10.99 reported that headgear, beards and tattoos had been taken off the
    operator, all three at zero pixels. Her hat had not gone anywhere: cosOwned
    derives what she owns from runs, extracts, level and warden kills, and the
    fresh profile had zeroed them, so cosWorn returned nothing to draw.

Three fixes, and the first is the rule: **a check may borrow the profile, it may
not persist what it borrowed, and it may not restore field by field, because the
next check depends on a field this one has never heard of.** v11.11 snapshots the
whole object and puts the whole thing back, and no longer saves. v10.99 unlocks
the rack for its own hero arm rather than trusting whatever progress happens to
be on the profile. And the jersey numeral is named as an exception by WHERE IT
LIVES, inside the Fashion figure and its swatches, because the span carries no
class to name it by; an Impact element planted anywhere else is still caught,
which is checked.
## v11.10 - THE v11.07 QUESTION ANSWERED: THE BOT CANNOT SEE THAT BUG AT ALL

At v11.07 I fixed the crawler that could not see a hidden man it was touching,
and said plainly that I had not measured what it does to the bot's extract rate.
This is that measurement, and the answer is about the instrument rather than the
game.

**THE PAIRED RUN IS NOT AFFORDABLE HERE.** One paired seed takes about thirty five
seconds in this environment, so the 320 pairs the standard asks for is several
hours, and a single pair outlives the window I can drive a call in. Seven pairs
completed before I stopped it: zero discordant, and neither arm extracted once,
which is a saturated result that says nothing. I am not going to spend more ticks
on a number I cannot finish.

**SO I MEASURED THE THING THAT DECIDES THE ANSWER.** The bug only fires when
concealment falls far enough that a crawler's sight, 100 units times concealment,
drops under its own 36 unit reach. That needs concealment below about **0.36**.

**MEASURED**, three seeded bot raids, 1,647 steps: crawlers were inside biting
distance of the bot for **693 frames**, and **zero** of those frames were in the
blind band. Over 300 frames the bot's own concealment ran **0.40 at its lowest**,
1.00 at its highest, **0.884 on average**, and it crouched in **not one frame**,
because the simCrouch dial is 0 and has been for its whole life.

**THE BOT NEVER GETS THERE.** It cannot exhibit the bug. That is why the seven
pairs showed no difference and why three hundred more would have shown none
either. The bug only ever reached a HUMAN who hides, which is exactly why he hit
it twice and why no number I have ever run showed it.

**NOTHING IN THE GAME CHANGED IN THIS BUILD.** What it adds is the limit, written
where it cannot be forgotten, because the mistake it prevents is one I was a
sentence away from making: quoting a sim number as though it covered how he
actually plays.

**NEW CHECK v11.10** is not shaped like the others and I am not going to pretend
it is. There is no defect here, so there is no control that fails on the previous
build: it passes on v11.09 and on v11.10 alike, and it is written to fail in the
FUTURE. It reads the crouch dial, which needs no raid at all, and fails if the
bot is ever allowed to crouch, because every extract rate in this file would then
describe a different player from the one that produced them. It steps one short
raid and fails if the bot's concealment ever reaches the band, because that would
mean the sim CAN see this class of bug and the reasoning above must be replaced
with a measurement. And where the bot simply meets no crawler, that is recorded
as a gap in the sample rather than counted as a fault in the game.

Not verified: the extract rate effect itself, which remains unmeasured and, on
the evidence above, unmeasurable by this bot. If he wants a real number it needs
either a bot that hides or a person, and the person is him.
## v11.09 - HIS NOTE 18, THE HALF I LEFT UNVERIFIED: THE MENUS

v10.95 put the canvas on one font and its own Not verified line said: "the DOM,
which this check does not trace, is set in the game font by the stylesheet but
was not measured word by word". His instruction was "use the entire font across
the entire game", and half of the game is menus.

**I ALMOST REPORTED IT CLEAN.** I grepped the file for a wrong font-family and
found none: every rule in the stylesheet names the game font, or inherits, and
the only exceptions are the wordmark and one dev editor. That was going to be the
finding.

**THEN THE CHECK READ WHAT THE BROWSER ACTUALLY COMPUTES, and found four.**

    pnamein    ARIAL       the box he types his pillager's NAME into
    delword    ARIAL       the box he types delete into to erase a save
    resword    ARIAL       the box he types restore into, mine, from v11.04
    verlabel   TITAN ONE   the version, inheriting the wordmark's face

**A GREP FINDS WHAT IS WRITTEN, NOT WHAT IS MISSING.** An input does not inherit
its font in any browser; it has to be told, and three of them never were. So the
very first thing a new player types into, the box that asks for his pillager's
name, has been in the browser's default face for the whole life of this game, and
searching for a wrong font could never have found it.

**THE FIX** is two rules: inputs, textareas and selects take the game font, and
the version readout beside the wordmark stops borrowing the display face, because
it is a readout and not the name. The name itself keeps it.

**NEW CHECK v11.09** walks every element in the document and reads the family the
browser resolves, rather than the family the stylesheet asks for, because a rule
can be overridden, a class can be absent and an inline style beats both. The two
deliberate exceptions are named rather than pattern matched: the game's own name,
and the dev text editor, which is monospace because it is a text editor.

Three controls. At least 120 elements must have been read, or the page did not
build and every clean line above is meaningless. At least 100 of them must be in
the game font, or the font failed to load and everything is falling back to the
same default. And an element in a foreign face is planted, caught and removed, so
a clean sweep is only trusted from a sweep that has just proved it can fail.

Fails on a v11.08 fixture with all four, named.

Not verified: the two hundred or so elements that exist only inside panels that
were not open when the sweep ran are covered, because getComputedStyle answers
for a hidden element too, but anything the game builds at runtime and had not
built yet was not read. The stash grid and the racks are built on open, and the
sweep runs on a fresh document.
## v11.08 - HIS NOTE 21: WHY A SHOT SOMETIMES MAKES A RED RING AND SOMETIMES NOT

"sometimes my shots make a red noise circle when they hit something, sometimes
they don't --whats up with that?", 2026-09-04.

**MEASURED.** One pistol round into one sentry at 160 units, thirty frames each,
with the target's own return fire held off so the only rings are the ones his
shot caused:

    idle machine that survives    one ring, and it is the machine MOVING
    awake machine that survives   one ring, and it is the machine MOVING
    machine killed outright       NO RING AT ALL

**SO THE RING IS NOT HIS HIT.** A landed round pings nothing at all. The ring that
follows is the thing he hit taking a STEP, drawn in the pale red of a machine
moving. Kill it outright and it never takes that step, so there is nothing. And
his own noises have drawn no ring since v5.31, on the grounds that he knows what
he just did. That is the whole rule, and it is a good rule: no ring after a hit
means the thing is dead.

**A PROBE THAT LIED, AND I CHECKED IT.** The first trial reported zero damage from
a shot that hit in the other two, which looked like a machine in patrol ignoring
a bullet. Re-run with the same setup a third time, an idle machine took the hit
at frame 5 like the others. It was the first shot after a deploy not landing in
my window, not a defect in the game. Reported here because it nearly became a
finding.

**AND THE ONE THING THAT IS SUPPOSED TO TEACH HIM THAT RULE WAS WRONG TWICE.** The
sound key beside the legend, whose entire job is the colour language, carried:

  - a cream swatch labelled "you", for a ring that CANNOT EXIST, because ping
    refuses to draw the player's own noises
  - #e65100 for pillager firing, an ORANGE, when the game has drawn that ring in
    #ff3b30 since v9.63, changed on his own one-word instruction: RED

So the legend taught him a colour that never appears and showed the wrong swatch
for one that does. A key that teaches the wrong colour is worse than no key.

**THE FIX:** the key is BUILT FROM the colour table rather than typed out beside
it, so a swatch can never drift from what is drawn again. The impossible row is
replaced by the rule that answers his question, "never your own", and the wording
moves from "robot" to "machine", which is the word the rest of the game uses.

**NEW CHECK v11.08** requires every swatch in the key to be a colour the game
really draws, cross-referenced against the colour table itself rather than a list
typed into the check; forbids a row telling him a ring can be him; and requires
the key to state that a ring is never his own noise. Three controls: the colour
table must have yielded at least four colours or the check is not looking at the
game; the key must still explain all four of the things that can hurt him,
accepting either the old or the new word so the control tests coverage and not my
choice of vocabulary; and the legend must still draw without throwing at 1920 by
1080 with the sound key at its new length.

Fails on a v11.07 fixture with all three findings.

Not verified: whether he wants the ring rule changed rather than merely stated. A
landed hit does play a sound and draws no ring, which is arguably a hole in a
visualiser that is documented as mirroring what you hear. I have not changed it,
because that would put a new ring on every landed shot in every firefight, and
that is his call rather than mine.
## v11.07 - HIS NOTE 22, ASKED TWICE: CRAWLERS ARE NOT ATTACKING PROPERLY

"Once again, crawlers aren't attacking properly?", 2026-09-04, and before that, on
2026-09-03: "i saw atleast one instance where i was standing still and crawler
didn't hurt me even though he was close".

**REPRODUCED, AND THE NUMBER IS SHARP.** One crawler stood 30 units from a still
player and facing him. Its bite reaches 36 (its own body is 15, the player's 11,
and the reach is 10 on top). Three seconds each time, varying only how well
hidden he was:

    concealment 1.00   65 damage
    concealment 0.80   65 damage
    concealment 0.60   65 damage
    concealment 0.45   65 damage
    concealment 0.35   65 damage
    concealment 0.25   ZERO, in patrol for the whole three seconds
    concealment 0.15   ZERO
    concealment 0.05   ZERO

**THE CAUSE: a crawler's eyes shrink with your concealment and its reach does
not.** Its sight is 100 units multiplied by concealment; its bite reaches 36. Below
about 0.3 there is a band where it is close enough to bite and cannot see, and the
bite lives inside the chase branch, so it never enters chase. It stands there
touching him and does nothing. That is exactly what he described, both times.

**WHY THE FIRST FIX DID NOT CATCH IT.** The 2026-09-03 report led to the two
if/else chains finding, where a non-raider fell into the idle wander branch mid
chase and wiped the attack cooldown every frame. That was a real bug and it was
fixed. It was also a different bug. Checking the same ground again: that wander
branch is inside the snitch block and ends in a continue, so a crawler cannot
reach it. The cooldown is not the problem now; being seen is.

**THE FIX: you cannot hide from something that is already touching you.** The
crawler's sight gets a floor equal to its own reach plus a small margin, applied
to the corner of the eye as well as to the cone, because you do not hide from
something you are touching by standing behind it. A wall still stops it: canSee
runs its own line of sight and the bite tests for one separately.

**THIS CHANGES WHAT CRAWLERS DO, and I am not pretending otherwise.** It sits on
a dial, touchSees, so the old behaviour stays measurable rather than deleted.

**NEW CHECK v11.07** puts a crawler at 85 percent of its own reach, taken from
the entity rather than typed in, in front of a still, hidden player, and requires
damage inside three seconds. Three controls, and they matter more than the
assertion: at 2.2 times the reach the same hidden man must still be safe, or
concealment has stopped meaning anything; a man in plain view must still be
bitten, or the check is measuring the wrong thing; and turning the dial off must
bring the silence back and turning it on must restore the bite, or the fix is not
what is being tested.

Fails on a v11.06 fixture with his own case in its own words: "a crawler 31 units
away, with a reach of 36, did nothing at all in three seconds while he stood
still and hidden".

Not verified: what this does to the bot's extract rate. Crawlers are the one
enemy the sim bot actually fights, so a crawler that notices it at touching range
may move that number, and I have not run the paired seeds to say by how much. The
alternative was to sit on a bug he has now reported twice, which is worse.
## v11.06 - HIS NOTE 20: THE BALLER'S JERSEY IS BEHIND A BLACK BLOCK

"micheal jordan character, can't see his jersey bc its blocked by a black block
(maybe supposed to be backpack straps?)", 2026-09-04.

**IT IS NOT THE BACKPACK.** The pack is drawn before the torso and the torso
covers it. Two other things are on that chest and I put both of them there.

**MEASURED**, one baller drawn alone at nine times raid size, every painted pixel
in a 125 by 130 box around the chest counted by colour:

    3,222  the red of the jersey
    2,384  the jersey's own black side panels
    1,602  the red in shadow
    1,582  the white of the 23
    1,506  the ink outline
      882  the chest rig band

The black side panels alone were 74 percent of the red. They were 2.4 wide each
on a chest 13 wide, so 4.8 of 13, **thirty-seven percent of the shirt in
near-black**. At sprite size two black bars down a chest read as straps, which is
exactly the word he used. And underneath them, the chest rig is a near-black band
the FULL width of the chest, drawn immediately after the jersey, straight across
the lower half of the numeral.

**THE FIX, both of them.** The side panels go from 2.4 to 1.4, which is trim
rather than a block. And the jersey is drawn AFTER the chest rig instead of
before it, so the 23 sits on top of the band. The rig still reads, between the
number and the panels.

**MEASURED AFTER:** the white of the 23 goes from 1,582 to **2,735**, a 73
percent gain, because nothing is painted across it any more. The red goes from
3,222 to 3,661. The black falls from 2,384 to 1,994 and its ratio to the red from
0.74 to 0.54. The black fell less than the panel width did because that exact
colour appears elsewhere on the figure, which is worth knowing before anybody
reads too much into that one number.

**NEW CHECK v11.06** finds the chest from the drawing rather than from
coordinates typed into it, using the jersey red as the marker, then requires at
least 2,000 pale pixels of numeral and a black-to-red ratio no worse than 0.62.
Two controls: a figure with no jersey must produce almost no jersey red and few
pale pixels, which proves the red is the shirt and the pale is the number rather
than the skin.

Fails on a v11.05 fixture with both findings and their numbers.

**AND THE v10.46 JERSEY CHECK HAD TO MOVE WITH IT.** It required at least 8 ink
pixels of side panel at raid scale, a floor calibrated on the very block he
complained about. Widening the art back until the old number returned would be
fitting the game to the test. Measured again at raid scale with the trim: red
+58, pale +24, ink +4. The floor is 2, half the live reading, which still catches
the panels being deleted and no longer demands a block.

Not verified: how it reads to him at play zoom and on the Fashion figure, which
is the judgement he will make; and whether the chest rig band should be there at
all on a jersey, which is a look decision rather than a defect.
## v11.05 - HIS QUESTION: IS A DAYTIME BLACKOUT ACTUALLY HARDER? NO, AND MY v11.00 PAID FOR IT ANYWAY

"is a daytime blsackout meaningfully harder than normal daytime play?",
2026-09-04.

**THE ANSWER IS NO, AND AT TWO TIMES OF DAY IT IS LITERALLY NOTHING.** Lamp
brightness in this game is

    wx().lights * (isDay() ? tod().lights : 1)

and the times of day carry lamp values of 0.7 at dawn, **ZERO at 8am**, **ZERO at
noon**, 0.25 at 6pm and 1 at dusk. Blackout multiplies by 0.18. At 8am and noon
that is zero times 0.18. The lamps a daytime blackout kills were already off.

**AND LAMP BRIGHTNESS FEEDS TWO THINGS IN THE WHOLE FILE:** the "lit" percentage
in the flight recorder, and the glow the lamps draw. Nothing in vision,
concealment or machine AI reads it. So a blackout is a change to what a HUMAN can
see, which is real difficulty for a person and none at all for the bot, and in
daylight it is not even that.

**WHAT THAT MAKES WRONG IS MINE, FROM FOUR BUILDS AGO.** v11.00 classed a weather
as hard if it cuts sight OR kills the lamps, and paid his 1.1x for it. In daylight
that paid a bonus for killing lamps that were already dark. His question found it.

**THE FIX.** Killing the lamps counts only when the lamps were on. The rule asks
how much light actually goes and wants a real amount of it, at least 0.15 of the
scale, so a blackout pays at night, at dusk and at dawn and pays nothing at 8am
and noon. Cutting SIGHT, which is rain, fog and storm, is untouched: that is the
weather itself and does not care what the hour is. The sector page stops
promising a bonus it may not deliver: pick a blackout in daylight and it says
"Only harder if the lamps were on, and in daylight that depends on the hour you
land at."

**THE CHECK IS THE v11.00 ONE, SPLIT BY WHAT THE WEATHER ACTUALLY DOES**, which
is what it should have been in the first place. Rain, fog and storm must be hard
whatever the hour. Blackout must be hard at night, hard at dusk, and NOT hard at
noon, which is his question stated as an assertion. Two controls, and they guard
the thing I got wrong: the build must have something that asks how much lamp
light there was before the weather, and the time-of-day table must actually carry
zero at noon and full at dusk, asked of the table rather than remembered, because
this whole rule rests on those two numbers.

Fails on a v11.04 fixture: "nothing asks how much lamp light there was before the
weather, so a blackout pays whatever the hour".

Not verified, and it is the honest limit of this: whether a blackout at night is
meaningfully harder for HIM. The bot cannot answer it, because nothing the bot
reads changes when the lamps go out; only a person playing in the dark can say.
And I have not touched what a blackout DOES, on his standing order that no dial

## v11.04 - HIS NOTE 14, SECOND HALF: PASTING THE CODE BACK IN

v11.03 put a RESTORE CODE at the end of every report and could read one back. A
code nobody can apply is a note in a bottle, so this is the other end of it: paste
it in Settings, in the recorder tab, directly under the report it came out of.

**IT IS DESTRUCTIVE AND IT SAYS SO.** Applying a code REPLACES the save being
played. So it is a three step door, the same shape as the save delete he already
has. **READ CODE** decodes it and says in plain words whose character it is and
what it is worth: "ZQXLOST, 77 raids, $771,122, 8,899 XP, 3 items in the stash".
Then a typed word. Then REPLACE. Nothing is written before the word is typed, and
what the code contains is on screen before he types it, so pasting the wrong one
is caught by reading rather than by losing a character to it. KEEP MINE backs out.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT DO.** It does not restore the run log. The log is history, it
is not in the code, and pretending to bring it back would be a lie in the one
place that has to be trustworthy. An item id that no longer exists in the game is
dropped rather than resurrected, because a stash key with no row in the item table
reads undefined in every panel that draws it.

**THE RELOAD IS ARMED, NOT FIRED, and that turned out to matter twice.** The page
reloads 400 milliseconds after the restore, because everything on the floor was
built from the profile that has just been replaced. The wait is for the profile
WRITE: storeSet can go through a promise on a host that provides storage, and a
page that reloads before the write lands loses the character it just restored,
which is the one failure this feature cannot have. But a timer is invisible to a
check, and an invisible timer is one that fires four hundred milliseconds later in
the middle of the next check and reloads the tab, taking the corpus with it. So
the arming is recorded where anything can read it and the handle is kept where a
check can cancel it, which the check now does.

**NEW CHECK v11.04** makes a character out of values the fallback could not
produce, takes its code, becomes somebody else entirely, and then drives the real
door. It requires that READING a code writes nothing; that REPLACE does nothing
with an empty box and nothing with the wrong word; that with the right word every
one of twenty-two fields comes back, including two of one item and one of another
in the stash, and that the old stash is gone; that a reload is armed; and that the
run log is untouched. Four controls: rubbish must not open the confirmation and
must be called rubbish on screen, the word alone with nothing pasted must do
nothing, and KEEP MINE must both close the door and disarm it.

Fails on a v11.03 fixture: a restore code cannot be applied at all.

Not verified: what happens when a code from a much older build is pasted into a
much newer one, since the code carries a version number and nothing yet reads it;
and whether he wants a restore to be allowed into an occupied save at all, rather
than only into an empty one.
## v11.03 - HIS NOTE 14, FIRST HALF: A CHARACTER YOU CAN GIVE BACK

"when friends give feedback the game should also log their character info -- that
way if they lose their character accidentally, we can give them a code to restore
it", 2026-09-04.

**REPRODUCED by reading what a report actually carries.** One summary line:
"Profile: 2 runs, 1 extracted, 0 died, best haul 2685c, credits 395700, XP 343,
racks 0, pack T1, notoriety 0, stash 4". That is a description of a character,
not a character. Nothing in it says what they were wearing, what is in the stash,
what they have unlocked, or where their contracts standing is, so nothing in a
report could rebuild anybody.

**WHY THE CODE IS SMALL, and this is the part worth knowing.** Cosmetics are not
stored as an owned list. cosOwned DERIVES what is unlocked from runs, extracts,
level, warden kills and the season board, so the code only has to carry those
numbers and the ids actually worn, plus anything bought outright. The stash goes
in as counts by key rather than a list of every copy. And the run log stays out
entirely: it is by far the biggest thing in a profile and it is history, not
identity.

**WHAT IT CARRIES:** name, credits, XP, level, runs, extracts, deaths, best haul,
notoriety, pack tier, racks, arrays, contracts standing, season tiers claimed,
kill tallies, cosmetics bought, junk tags, the chosen map, surface and weather,
every worn cosmetic, and the stash as counts. It is one line at the end of every
report, under a heading that says what it is.

**NEW CHECK v11.03** builds a character out of values the fallback could never
produce, a name of ZQXRESTORE, 918,273 credits, three of one thing and one of
another in the stash, then requires the code to appear in the real report, to
name itself so it can be told from any other pasted line, and to read back every
one of twenty-three fields exactly. Then four controls: an empty string, an
ordinary sentence and a corrupt code must all be refused rather than accepted as
a character; and the code must FOLLOW the profile, checked by changing the
credits and requiring the new number and not the old one, because a reader that
echoed a fixed object would pass every line above.

Fails on a v11.02 fixture: the report carries no restore code at all.

**APPLYING IT IS THE NEXT BUILD**, behind a typed confirmation, because an import
that overwrites a save without asking is a worse bug than the one it fixes.

Not verified: how long the code runs for a mature profile, since the check bounds
it at four thousand characters and the profile it measured is small; and whether
he wants the run log in it after all, which would make it a backup rather than a
restore and would be far too big to paste.
## v11.02 - HIS NOTE 8: WHY CHANGING SAVE LEAVES FULLSCREEN

"if i click fullscreen and then click to change the save, it kicks me out of
fullscreen --why??", 2026-09-04.

**THE ANSWER, AND IT IS NOT A BUG I CAN PATCH AWAY.** Clicking another save writes
the slot pointer and calls location.reload, because the profile key is read once
at file scope and the entire game is built from it. Every browser drops
fullscreen on a page load. It cannot be re-entered afterwards on its own, because
requestFullscreen requires a user gesture and a gesture does not survive a
navigation. So there are exactly two honest fixes: switch saves WITHOUT
reloading, which means re-reading the profile in place and re-initialising every
panel built from it, a deep change I am not making 55 hours from an alpha; or
stop it being a mystery and put the way back one click away. This is the second,
and I am saying plainly that it is the second.

**WHAT HE GETS.** A line under the saves, permanently: changing save reloads the
game, which is why it leaves fullscreen. And, if he WAS in fullscreen at the
moment he switched, the title screen tells him so on the way back in, with GO
FULLSCREEN sitting directly above it. The flag lives in its own storage key,
never the profile, because it is about the browser and the tab rather than about
a character, and it has to survive a switch between two saves without belonging
to either. It is read once and cleared once, so the line appears on the reload it
belongs to and never again.

**NEW CHECK v11.02** requires the saves panel to say both words, reload and
fullscreen, where the click is; requires switching while in fullscreen to be
remembered and switching while NOT in fullscreen to be remembered as nothing;
requires the line to appear once, to clear its own flag, and to be gone on the
next boot. One more control: it must not tell him he lost fullscreen while he is
in fullscreen, which is the one case where the line would be noise. Fullscreen
itself cannot be entered by a check, since a browser demands a gesture, so the
check makes the game believe it is in fullscreen and puts the real answer back
afterwards.

Fails on a v11.01 fixture on both halves: no explanation in the panel, and no
memory of having been in fullscreen.

**A CHECK BUG OF MINE, FIXED IN THE SAME BUILD.** The guard for the missing
memory used a return, which threw away the panel finding that had already been
recorded, so the old build reported half the defect. A guard that returns
discards what was already found; it pushes and returns the whole list now.

Not verified: whether he would rather have the deep fix, switching saves without
a reload, which would keep fullscreen and is the only thing that actually answers
his question with a no. That is a real piece of work and it is his call whether
it happens before or after the alpha.
## v11.01 - HIS NOTE: THE FEEDBACK BUTTONS AT THE END OF A RAID ARE OLD

"change the feedback buttons at the end of a raid to something more current",
2026-09-04.

**REPRODUCED BY READING THE LIST, and its own comment dates it.** Twenty-four
tags, with this written above them at v5.72: "the two music tags went where the
music went. These two are the live unknowns instead: the Listener teaching was
rewritten at v5.60 and nobody has tested it on a human, and the Choir has never
been fought at all."

Eight of the twenty-four were one-machine questions from that era: Listener
beatable, Listener unfair, Pillbox worth it, Pillbox a chore, Bulwark great,
Bulwark unfair, Howler great, Howler unfair. Every one of those machines still
exists, and he has logged dozens of runs against them since, so those questions
are answered by his own log rather than open. Meanwhile **nothing from the last
thirty builds had a tag at all**: not the grid backpack, not the hotbar, not
being downed and crawling, not the map screen, not the Undercroft, not the
weather he now chooses, and above all not "this crashed" or "this looked wrong",
which are the two things a friend cannot tell him any other way.

**WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS.** His friends are about to play. A tag
is the only feedback most people will ever give, and the run report is the only
channel back. A tag row full of questions about a machine somebody has not met
yet, with no way to say "it broke", wastes the alpha.

**THE NEW SET, thirty tags, every one judgeable in a single raid.** It opens with
the three he cannot get any other way, Something crashed, Something looked wrong,
Sound was off, then readability, which is where most of his own notes come from,
then feel, then what he carried and the room he keeps it in, then who was up
there, then the three newest systems, then the place and his oldest complaint,
then getting out. Old records keep their old strings, because a tag is just text
on a run row.

**NEW CHECK v11.01** requires a way to say it crashed, that something looked
wrong, that the sound was off and that text was hard to read; requires no more
than two of the eight v5.72 one-machine questions to survive; requires no
duplicates, nothing too long for the row, and a count between twelve and forty.
Then it drives the real thing: deploy, end the raid, press two buttons on the
real card, press a third twice, press the real way out, and require the two to
be on the logged run and the third, which was pressed twice, not to be. Controls:
the card must have drawn a button for every tag in the list, there must be a way
out of the card, and the run must have reached the log at all.

Fails on a v11.00 fixture with all five findings, including all eight stale
buttons named.

Not verified: whether he agrees with the eight I removed, which is a judgement
about what is still open and is his to overrule; and how thirty tags wrap on his
1440p and 4K screens, since the check counts them and does not measure the row.
## v11.00 - HIS NOTE 16: WEATHER IS A CHOICE, AND THE HARD ONES PAY MORE

"add weather conditions as a selection toggle in the 'Where are you going'
screen", and then, the same day: "choose more difficult weather shouild hive
small xp boost like 1.1x". 2026-09-04.

**REPRODUCED:** the sector page carries SURFACE with DAY and NIGHT, added at v9.97
on his note, and nothing at all for weather. The weather was one seeded roll at
the drop and he had never had a say in it.

**THE THING THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN INVISIBLE.** pickWeather draws from the SEEDED
stream. An implementation that skips the roll when a weather is pinned moves
every roll after it, so the map, the loot and the bodies all change and nothing
says so. The roll ALWAYS happens now; pinning replaces the answer, never the
draw. Measured across three pins on seed 4242, map 0: entities, containers and
walls identical every time.

**WHICH ONES PAY IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED.** A weather is hard if it cuts sight or
kills the lamps, which is view below 1 or lights below 1, asked of the weather
table rather than kept as a second list beside it. That is rain, fog, blackout
and storm today, and a state added later is priced by what it does rather than by
whether I remembered it. His 1.1x sits on a dial, wxXp, beside his nightXp 1.2,
and both apply, so a hard night pays 1.32x. The record carries wxHard the way it
already carried night, so the flight recorder knows what a run went up in.

**THE CONTROL** is a WEATHER row under his SURFACE row, in the same shape, with
the chosen one drawn amber like the chosen map: SURPRISE ME, CLEAR, RAIN, FOG,
BLACKOUT, STORM. SURPRISE ME is the default and is the old behaviour exactly.
Partly Cloudy is reachable only through it, on purpose, because it is the one
state that exists in order to TURN into another.

**NEW CHECK v11.00** presses the buttons rather than writing the profile, because
the button is the thing he presses, then requires the raid to come up in what he
asked for, and does that for every pinnable weather. It requires the map
fingerprint to be identical with a weather pinned and with the roll left alone,
which is the seeded-stream trap. It requires rain, fog, blackout and storm to
count as hard and clear and partly not to, or the bonus would mean nothing, and
it drives two identical runs through the real progress path, one hard and one
clear, and requires the XP ratio to be his number. Controls: there must be a way
to leave it to the roll, there must be something to pin, the clear run must have
paid something for the bonus to multiply, and the bonus must be above 1.

Fails on a v10.99 fixture: there is no weather control on the page at all.

Not verified: whether 1.1x feels worth a blackout to him, which is his judgement
and his dial; and whether the six buttons plus the surface row fit his 1440p and
4K layouts, since the check reads the DOM and the sector page is one column that
grows downward.
## v10.99 - NOTE 17: NO PILLAGER HAS EVER WORN A HAT, A BEARD OR A TATTOO

Found at v10.94 while proving the eye instrument, by asking each rack whether it
changes a NON-hero figure at all. The same rack, on the same call, at nine times
raid size:

    headgear   the operator 31,978 pixels changed, a pillager 0
    beard      the operator  5,221 pixels changed, a pillager 0
    tattoo     the operator    801 pixels changed, a pillager 0

**CAUSE.** The block that draws the operator's fringe also contains the tattoo,
the beard and the headgear, and the whole block sits behind a hero-only branch.
Hair colour and hair cut are outside it, which is why the crowd looks varied
enough that this went unnoticed for months.

**WHAT IT COST.** The Undercroft crowd rolls a hat, a beard and a tattoo for
every single member and none of them were drawn, and two lines of the new-in card
promise that the pillagers dress from the same racks he does. A shipped promise
that was not true.

**THE FIX.** The branch closes after the FRINGE, which is the one thing in there
that is genuinely hers, her own hair styling. The tattoo, the beard and the
headgear fall outside it and reach everybody. Every one of them already reads a
pillager's own look through st; that code was written for this and had never once
been reachable.

**MEASURED AFTER:** headgear 32,557 pixels on a pillager, the beard 3,233, the
tattoo 1,418, and the operator unchanged.

**NEW CHECK v10.99** requires each of the three racks to change a pillager by a
real amount, requires each to still change the operator, so this cannot be passed
by taking a rack off her, and requires the operator and a pillager wearing the
same things to still differ by thousands of pixels, which is her fringe and which
would collapse if I had ungated the whole branch. One more control: a full-body
suit must still overrule the headgear, which is the order v10.54 set and which
this change reaches straight through.

**AN INSTRUMENT NOTE I AM NOT GOING TO DRESS UP.** Run standalone, six
consecutive draws of the same pillager are byte identical. Run as a check inside
the corpus, the FIRST pair differs by 621 pixels and every pair after it is
exact. I did not find what settles on that first pair. Rather than assert on a
number I cannot explain, every measurement is now the SETTLED reading: the
smaller of two consecutive pairs, each pair drawn back to back. With that, the
noise floor reads 0 and the old build reports all three racks at exactly 0, which
is the defect stated precisely. Before that change the drift was larger than the
tattoo signal, and the tattoo would have passed on a build that draws no tattoo.

**AND A THING FOR HIM TO DECIDE, MEASURED WHILE TESTING.** The crowd's look
roller picks one item from every rack including the OUTFIT rack, which holds Own
Clothes plus seven full-body suits. So roughly seven of every eight people in the
Undercroft are wearing a Skeleton, a Machine, a Trooper, an Android, a Tomb
Explorer, a Baller or a Street Poet, and a suit overrules every other rack by
design. Measured: 3 of 16 crowd rolls show a visible hat. So this fix is real and
the raid will show it, but the Undercroft floor will still be mostly costumes
until he says otherwise. That is his call and it is logged as note 19.

Not verified: how the crowd reads to him on the floor now, and whether any hat
sits wrongly on a pillager's head at raid zoom, since the check measures that the
hat is drawn and not that it is drawn beautifully.
## v10.98 - HIS RUN REPORT: A CRASH ON THE CHARACTER SCREEN, AND IT WAS MINE

From his flight recorder of 2026-09-04, two real runs and a crash block:

    v10.96 error on hub x4: Uncaught ReferenceError: sub is not defined
      at psv.onclick (dark_raiders.html:32475)

**I DID THIS AT v10.96, AND HE HIT IT FOUR TIMES.** Renaming your pillager on the
character screen also updates the name line under the title, and it did that with
a third hand-written copy of that sentence, reading a variable named `sub` that
lived beside it. v10.96 wrapped that sentence in a function so the pause box
could reuse it when it puts the screen back up, which moved `sub` inside the
function, and left the rename button pointing at a name that no longer existed in
its scope. The name still saved, because saveProfile runs first, then the handler
threw and the line under the title never changed.

**THE FIX IS THE ONE v10.96 SHOULD HAVE MADE.** The rename button calls the same
function everything else calls, so there is one copy of that sentence rather than
three. A crash caused by having two copies is not fixed by restoring the second
one.

**NEW CHECK v10.98** puts the character screen up, types a name the fallback
could never produce, presses SAVE, and requires no throw, the profile to carry
the new name, and the line under the title to show it. Then it presses every
other button on that screen except the three that leave it, erase a save or need
a real user gesture, and requires none of them to throw either, because his crash
was one handler out of several and nothing was watching any of them.

Two controls, and the first is what makes the rest mean anything: **an error
inside a DOM handler does not propagate to the caller**, so a check that clicks
and carries on sees nothing at all. This one listens on the window, and then
proves the listener works by clicking a button that throws on purpose and
requiring that to be heard. The second is that at least one button was actually
pressed.

Run against a v10.97 fixture the check reports his exact words back:
"renaming your pillager threw: Uncaught ReferenceError: sub is not defined".

**HIS TWO RUNS, authenticated and consumed.** Run #1, COLD STORAGE in fog at
dawn, 59 seconds, EXTRACT with 2,685 credits from a single container, 18 shots at
67 percent, four crawlers down, one down of his own and revived twice by raiders,
two walls broken, one story read. Run #2, 13 seconds, ABANDON with 460 credits
carried and no shot fired, closest extract 96m. Both real: real durations, real
distance moved, a named weapon.

**AND THE CHECK I WROTE FOR IT DID SOMETHING WORSE, WHICH I OWN.** Pressing every
button on that screen includes NEW PILLAGER, which writes a new active slot to
storage and RELOADS THE TAB. It killed the corpus run mid-flight and left the
save pointer on slot 4. A check may press a button that ends a raid; it may not
press one that navigates, and it may not touch the slot pointer at all, because
that pointer decides which save boots and it is the one key in this game that has
never been allowed to move. It is skipped by name now, the pointer is read before
and put back in a finally whatever happens, and a control requires both dangerous
buttons to have actually been found under the names the skip list uses, so a
rename of either cannot quietly start pressing them again.

Not verified: whether the crash also broke anything else he did on that screen in
that session, since the recorder keeps the message and not what he pressed next;
and his run #2 abandoning at 13 seconds is unexplained, which is a question for
him rather than a defect I can measure.

## v10.97 - HIS NOTE 12: A CONTRACT TARGET IS NOT SALVAGE

"anything that can be used to craft or for a contract, etc. should not be
classified as salvage", his note of 2026-09-04.

**REPRODUCED BY ENUMERATION**, against the tables that do the wanting rather than
by reading the labels. Three items are wanted by something in this game and were
shelved as SALVAGE, described to him as "salvage, sell it", and cleared by SELL
JUNK AND LOOSE SALVAGE:

    Servo Actuator   the contract board asks for it by name
    Optics Lens      the contract board asks for it by name
    Data Core        the contract board asks for it by name, and the mainframe
                     burns one to send you up with intel

The classification was a hard-coded list of five ids. It is correct about recipes
and racks and knew nothing about the other things in the game that consume an
item, because the contract board's shopping list was a literal inside the
contract generator where nothing else could read it. So the obvious button could
sell the exact item a live contract was asking him to carry out, and the stash
told him to.

**MY ERROR, CAUGHT BEFORE IT SHIPPED, AND WORTH RECORDING.** My first pass said
the servo is a live repair part again, on the grounds that his answer makes kills
wear a gun and addWear runs on every shot. addWear does run, but WEARSTEPS
carries ONE band, so wearLive() is false and repairCost refuses every gun. The
repair economy is dormant exactly as v9.43 left it, and labelling a servo "for
gun repairs" would be the game promising a use it will not honour. The repair
answer is gated on the wear system actually being alive, which is the switch
v9.43 built for this: put a second band back in WEARSTEPS and the servo becomes a
repair part again on its own. The servo is kept today because the CONTRACT BOARD
wants it, which is true, and is his note.

**THE FIX IS THAT NOTHING KEEPS A LIST.** One function, itemWanted, answers what
wants an item and why, in words he can read, and it answers by asking the recipe
table, the rack costs, the repair parts, the mainframe and the contract board.
Where those were literals inside the code that used them they are named now, so
the next thing that wants an item cannot be added without this answer changing
with it. The stash's shelf rule, which lived inside its own renderer where
nothing could ask it, is one function at file scope. The sell button consults the
same answer, and a junk tag he sets himself still overrides all of it, so he is
never stuck holding a part he has decided to be rid of.

**MEASURED, before and after.** Before: servo, optic and core all sell. After:
all three are kept, shelved under PARTS, and the stash says what wants them. Ten
items are still loose salvage and still sell, the Titanium Cell, the Induction
Coil, the Bloom Sample, the Meridian Reactor Core and the Warden Core among
them, so this taught the sell button rather than switching it off.

**NEW CHECK v10.97** builds the wanted set from the tables themselves, then
requires that nothing in it is shelved as salvage and that nothing in it is
cleared by the sell button. Four controls: at least six items must have been
found to be wanted, or it is not enumerating the game; the contract list must be
readable at all, which on the old build it is not and which is the whole cause;
at least three items must remain loose salvage and sellable, or the fix is an off
switch rather than a rule; and a junk tag must still let him sell. It also
refuses to let the game claim a repair use while the wear system is switched off.

Fails on a v10.96 fixture: the shelf rule is unreachable, the contract list is
unreadable, and the Data Core is cleared by the sell button.


**AND TWO CHECKS DISAGREED ABOUT THE SERVO, WHICH THE CORPUS CAUGHT.** v9.43
